  • csrf=False without another authentication.
  • auth='public' with sudo() returning records.
  • sanitize=False on a user-editable Html field.
  • Comparing tokens with ==.
  • Using a record id or timestamp as an access token.
  • request.env[model] with a model name from parameters.
  • Open redirects through a redirect parameter.
  • Logging secrets.
  • Relying on hidden buttons and menus instead of server checks.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
16: the SQL class does not exist (absent from the 16.0 tools/sql.py); pass parameters to cr.execute. Use check_access_rights and check_access_rule. auth='bearer' is not available.

17: the SQL class exists in odoo/tools/sql.py (checked on the 17.0 branch). Check whether env.execute_query exists on your 17 build before using it, as it was only verified on 18.

18: everything above. check_access_rights is deprecated; check_access is the form to use.

20: @route(type='json') is a deprecated alias of type='jsonrpc' (since 19). The helpers named here (SQL, consteq, hmac) were checked in the 18 source; re-check them in 20 before relying on a signature.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
1. Write a controller method that searches library.book by a name parameter with the string-formatting form, then call it with x' OR '1'='1. Replace it with the parameterised form and repeat.
  2. Run the review checklist's first three greps on your own module and fix what they find.
  3. Add a webhook route that verifies an HMAC with tools.hmac and consteq, and test it with a wrong and a correct signature.
  4. Log in as a portal user and request /my/loans/<id> for someone else's loan.
Solution notes
  1. The formatted query returns every book because the injected quote closes the string and OR '1'='1' is always true; the parameterised version treats the whole text as one value and returns nothing.
  2. Typical finds are cr.execute(... % ...), sudo() inside search, and Markup(...) around request data.
  3. The route must return 403 for a wrong signature and process the body for a correct one; the scope string you pass to hmac must match on both sides.
  4. The route should redirect to /my or return 403; any data returned means the access check is missing.

docs.title: The security model
docs.text:
Odoo security is not one mechanism. It is five layers stacked on top of each other, each answering a different question, and almost every security bug in a custom module comes from a developer assuming one layer does the work of another. The following chapters go deep on each layer.

Checked against the Odoo 18 source (odoo/models.py, odoo/api.py, odoo/addons/base/models/ir_model.py, ir_rule.py, res_users.py).

docs.title: The five layers
docs.text:
Layer Question it answers Defined by Enforced by 1. Authentication Who is this? login, session cookie, API key odoo/http.py (auth= on routes) 2. Entry points Which menus, actions, buttons and views does this user see? groups on menus, actions, views, view nodes the web client and ir.ui.view processing 3. Model access (ACL) May this user read/write/create/delete records of this model at all? ir.model.access ir.model.access.check 4. Record rules On which rows of that model? ir.rule ir.rule._compute_domain 5. Field access Which columns? groups= on fields Field.is_accessible, check_field_access_rights

Layers 3 to 5 live in the ORM. They apply to every ORM call from every caller: a button, an RPC, a cron, a controller, an odoo shell session. They do not apply when the code runs in superuser mode.

Layers 1 and 2 are not security boundaries on their own. A hidden menu is not a locked door: the user can still call the underlying model over RPC. Only layers 3 to 5 protect data, and only code in your own methods protects anything beyond them.

docs.title: Layer 1: authentication
docs.text:
Every route declares how its caller is identified (@http.route(auth=...), documented in odoo/http.py):

auth Meaning 'user' a logged-in user is required; the request runs with that user's rights 'bearer' the Authorization: Bearer <api token> header identifies the user; without the header the request must belong to a session, as for user 'public' the user may be anonymous; if so the request runs as the shared public user 'none' active even without a database; no user available. For framework and login code

'bearer' appears in the 18 docstring; do not assume it exists on 16 or 17. For JSON-RPC and XML-RPC calls to the ORM from outside, authentication is by login plus password or API key, and the call then runs as that user with all of layers 3 to 5.

CSRF protection is also a property of the route, enabled by default for type='http' and disabled by default for JSON routes. The secure-coding chapter covers it.

docs.title: Layer 2: entry points
docs.text:
groups can be set on ir.ui.menu, ir.actions.act_window and the other action types, ir.ui.view records, and on individual nodes in view XML (<field groups="...">, <button groups="...">, <group groups="...">). The server strips nodes the user's groups do not allow before sending the view, and the client does not show menus the user cannot open.

This is a usability layer. The security statement you can make about it is weak: "a user without the group will not normally see this". Anything that must hold goes into layers 3 to 5.

docs.title: Layer 3: model access control lists
docs.text:
ir.model.access rows grant perm_read, perm_write, perm_create and perm_unlink on a model to a group. Rules about them:

  • Additive, never subtractive. A user gets the union of the rows of all their groups. There is no deny.
  • A model with no ACL rows at all is closed to everybody except the superuser: the check is "is this model in the set of models this user may access in this mode", computed from the rows of the user's groups (_get_allowed_models in ir_model.py).
  • A row with an empty group grants everyone. Odoo logs a warning when you create one: "Every access-granting rule should specify a group."
  • The result is cached in the registry and cleared when ACL rows change (call_cache_clearing_methods).

The check is ir.model.access.check(model, mode, raise_exception). In the ORM it is reached through check_access, has_access and the CRUD methods.

docs.title: Layer 4: record rules
docs.text:
ir.rule rows add a domain to a model for the operations they cover. The ORM computes, for the current user, model and operation, one final domain:

AND( global_rule_domains..., OR( domains of the group rules the user belongs to ) )

with two details that surprise people, both visible in _compute_domain of ir_rule.py:

  1. If the model has group rules but the user belongs to none of those groups, the OR part vanishes and only global rules remain. So a model with only group-scoped rules is unrestricted for users outside those groups, as long as their ACL lets them in. Restricting "everyone except managers" needs a global rule.
  2. For models using _inherits, the parents' rules are folded in as ('parent_field', 'any', parent_domain).

The record rules chapter is the detailed treatment.

docs.title: Layer 5: field access
docs.text: A field with groups="library.group_library_manager" is invisible and unwritable for users outside the group: Field.is_accessible(env) returns True when the field has no groups or the environment is superuser, False when groups == '.' (a special value meaning "always forbidden"), and otherwise whether env.user.has_groups(self.groups). Reading or writing such a field as a user without the group raises an AccessError that names the fields, and the field disappears from fields_get.

docs.title: The order in which the ORM applies them
docs.text:
For records.read(), search(), write(), unlink() and create() as a normal user the sequence is:

  1. ACL check for the operation on the model (ir.model.access.check). Failing here raises AccessError mentioning the groups that would grant access.
  2. For operations on existing records, the record rule domain for that operation. For search and read it is added to the SQL query, so unauthorised rows silently disappear. For write and unlink the records are checked and failing ones produce an AccessError that names the rule.
  3. Field-level check for the fields involved.

In Odoo 18 steps 1 and 2 are exposed together through three methods on recordsets:

records.check_access("write")          # raises AccessError if forbidden on the model or any record
records.has_access("write")            # same, returns a boolean
records._filtered_access("write")      # subset of records the user may write

Calling check_access on an empty recordset checks the model-level ACL only, which is the right way to ask "may this user write to this model at all?" before showing a button.

The older names check_access_rights, check_access_rule and _filter_access_rules still exist in 18 but are deprecated since 18.0 and emit a DeprecationWarning.

docs.title: The superuser and sudo()
docs.text:
Superuser mode (env.su is true) turns layers 3 to 5 off:

  • ir.model.access.check returns True immediately.
  • ir.rule._get_rules returns an empty set, so no rule applies.
  • Field.is_accessible returns True.
  • check_access does nothing.

Two ways to be in it:

  • records.sudo() keeps the current user (so env.user is unchanged, create_uid is still them) but switches the checks off. sudo(False) switches them back on.
  • User id 1, base.user_root ("OdooBot"), is always in superuser mode by convention. with_user(user) returns an environment with su=False unless the user is the superuser.

The administrator user (base.user_admin, id 2) is a normal user who belongs to many groups. It is not in superuser mode. Record rules apply to it, and a multi-company rule can hide records from the administrator.

The environment exposes env.is_superuser(), env.is_admin() (has the "Access Rights" group, or superuser) and env.is_system() (has the "Settings" group, or superuser).

The docstring of sudo in 18 warns in so many words that it "could cause data access to cross the boundaries of record rules, possibly mixing records that are meant to be isolated (e.g. records from different companies)", and that methods which select one record among many, such as getting the default company, can give unintuitive results. Treat every sudo() as a line in a security review.

# Wrong: returns data the caller cannot see, to the caller.
def action_show_all_loans(self):
    loans = self.env["library.loan"].sudo().search([])
    return {"domain": [("id", "in", loans.ids)], ...}

# Right: let the rules decide.
def action_show_loans(self):
    loans = self.env["library.loan"].search([])

When elevation is genuinely needed (a portal user triggers a job that must write to a model they cannot touch), do the check first as the user, then sudo only the narrow write:

def action_extend(self, days):
    self.ensure_one()
    self.check_access("write")                 # as the real user
    self.sudo().write({"due_date": self.due_date + timedelta(days=days)})

docs.title: Odoo 20: ACLs and rules become ir.access
docs.text:
The Odoo 20 source merges layers 3 and 4 into one model, ir.access (odoo/addons/base/models/ir_access.py). The ORM still exposes check_access, has_access and _filtered_access, but the data and the combining rule changed:

ir.access field Meaning model_id the model group_id a group makes the record a permission; no group makes it a restriction operation a subset of the letters crud (r, ru, cru, crud, ...) domain optional domain; an empty domain means all records active, name, note switch, label, free text

Model._access_domain(operation) builds the answer for the current user:

permissions = [domains of accesses with a group the user has]      # OR-ed
restrictions = [domains of accesses without a group]               # AND-ed
# parent models of _inherits are added as ('parent_field', 'any', parent_domain) restrictions
return Domain.OR(permissions) & Domain.AND(restrictions)

Consequences, all visible in that function and in _get_failed_accesses:

  • No applicable permission means no access at all. Domain.OR([]) is false, so the "model with only group rules is unrestricted for outsiders" trap of Odoo 18 does not exist. The failure is a model-level access error.
  • A permission with an empty domain gives access to every record, and it is OR-ed with the other permissions of the user. A user in group A (read everything) and group B (read own records) reads everything. In 18 the same pair was an ACL for A plus a group rule for B, and the rule narrowed the ACL. Converting by hand means giving each group's permission its own domain.
  • A restriction replaces the global rule. hr_employee_comp_rule in the 20 hr module is an ir.access row with an empty group and the domain [('company_id', 'in', company_ids + [False])].
  • The domain evaluation context is the same four names (user, time, company_ids, company_id).

Data files change too. The CSV is security/ir.access.csv with these columns, taken from the hr module:

id,name,model_id,group_id/id,operation,domain
access_hr_employee_user,hr.employee user,hr.employee,hr.group_hr_user,crud,
hr_employee_comp_rule,Employee multi company rule,hr.employee,,crud,"[('company_id', 'in', company_ids + [False])]"

Note model_id holds the model's technical name, not model_<name>, and operation replaces the four perm_* columns.

The Odoo 20 tree ships a conversion script, odoo/upgrade_code/19.4-00-ir-access.py, run with odoo-bin upgrade_code. It converts ir.model.access and ir.rule data to ir.access and logs a warning when an ACL that grants a whole model overlaps group rules that used to narrow it. Read those warnings; they point at exactly the reinterpretation described above. The migration chapter covers the command.

docs.title: Combining groups
docs.text: The ladder pattern keeps this manageable: an application defines groups where each higher group implies the lower (implied_ids), and each ACL line is granted to the lowest group that needs it. The groups chapter shows it in XML.

docs.title: Where the definitions live
docs.text:
Piece File in a module Loaded as Groups, categories security/library_security.xml data ACLs security/ir.model.access.csv data, after the model exists Record rules security/library_security.xml data Field groups Python, fields.X(groups="...") code Menu/action/view groups the groups attribute in XML data

The manifest data list order matters: the CSV references model_library_book, so models must be loaded before it, which they are (models load before data files), and group XML ids must exist before the CSV that names them, so list the groups file first.

docs.title: A decision procedure
docs.text:
When someone says "user X must not see Y", ask in this order:

  1. Is it the whole model? Add or remove ACL rows. Lowest group that needs it.
  2. Is it some rows? A record rule. Decide global or group-scoped using the AND/OR rule above.
  3. Is it one or two columns on rows the user may otherwise see? A field groups.
  4. Is it an action (a button) rather than data? Check in the method with check_access or user.has_group, and hide the button with groups as convenience.
  5. Is it something only some code paths may do? Put the check in that code, never only in the view.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
Hiding a menu or a button is not security. Any user with the right ACL can call the model over RPC regardless of what the web client shows.

  • A model with only group-scoped rules. Users outside those groups are not restricted. Add a global rule to restrict everybody.
  • sudo() on a search, then returning the records. The caller sees what the rules were meant to hide.
  • ACL rows with an empty group. They grant everyone, including portal and public users if the model is reachable.
  • Assuming the administrator bypasses rules. User 2 does not; only user 1 and sudo do.
  • Checking has_group in the view only. Re-check in the method that performs the action.
  • Using check_access_rights in new code on 18. It is deprecated since 18.0; use check_access or has_access.
  • Testing as admin. Admin passes most checks. Test with with_user of an ordinary user.
  • Forgetting that cron and server actions run as superuser or a configured user. They bypass or inherit rights differently from a button click.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
16 and 17: the deprecated method names (check_access_rights, check_access_rule) are the only ones. The auth='bearer' route option should not be assumed. Rule domains use user, time, company_ids, company_id.

18: check_access, has_access, _filtered_access. The deprecated names remain with warnings. auth='bearer' is documented in http.route.

20: groups are filed under privileges (privilege_id), members are user_ids, and the user's groups are group_ids/all_group_ids. ACLs and rules are one model, ir.access, with permissions OR-ed and restrictions AND-ed. Odoo 19 was not available to check. Do not copy 18 security data into 20.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
1. In an Odoo shell, as the administrator, run env["library.loan"].check_access("read") and then env["library.loan"].with_user(some_portal_user).check_access("read") and compare.
  2. Print the final domain a user gets for a model: env["ir.rule"].with_user(user)._compute_domain("library.loan", "read").
  3. Compare env["library.loan"].with_user(user).search_count([]) with .sudo().search_count([]).
Solution notes
  1. The administrator passes; a portal user raises AccessError unless an ACL row grants their group read.
  2. The result is a normalised domain list: global rule domains ANDed with the OR of the group rules that the user belongs to. Run it as different users to see the difference.
  3. The first count respects the rules; the second counts every row. A difference tells you the rules are doing something.

docs.title: Actions and menus
docs.text: An action tells the web client what to do when the user clicks something: open a list, run code, open a URL, show a client-side screen. A menu is only a pointer to an action. Understanding the action record gets you most of the way, because buttons, menu items and the "Action" dropdown all use the same machinery.

docs.title: Window actions
docs.text:
<record id="library_book_action" model="ir.actions.act_window">
  <field name="name">Books</field>
  <field name="res_model">library.book</field>
  <field name="view_mode">list,kanban,form</field>
  <field name="domain">[('active', '=', True)]</field>
  <field name="context">{'search_default_available': 1, 'default_state': 'draft'}</field>
  <field name="search_view_id" ref="library_book_search"/>
  <field name="help" type="html">
    <p class="o_view_nocontent_smiling_face">Create the first book</p>
  </field>
</record>

Key fields:

  • res_model: the model to display.
  • view_mode: comma-separated view types, in tab order. The first is the default. It is list, not tree, from Odoo 18 on.
  • view_id / view_ids: pin specific views. Without them, the highest-priority view of each type is used. view_ids (ir.actions.act_window.view) pins a view per mode and sets sequence.
  • domain: a permanent filter the user cannot remove. Use context plus a search default when the user should be able to clear it.
  • context: default_<field> pre-fills new records; search_default_<filter_name> turns on a filter from the search view; group_by sets default grouping.
  • target: current (default, replaces the view), new (dialog), fullscreen, main (replaces and clears breadcrumb).
  • limit: page size, default 80.
  • res_id: open one fixed record; combine with view_mode form.

docs.title: Opening an action from Python
docs.text:
def action_open_loans(self):
    self.ensure_one()
    return {
        "type": "ir.actions.act_window",
        "name": "Loans",
        "res_model": "library.loan",
        "view_mode": "list,form",
        "domain": [("book_id", "=", self.id)],
        "context": {"default_book_id": self.id},
    }

For a stable, overridable action prefer self.env["ir.actions.actions"]._for_xml_id("library.library_loan_action") and amend the returned dict. It reads the XML record, so customizations of the action apply.

docs.title: Other action types
docs.text:
• ir.actions.act_url: url and target (new, self, download). Use it for external links or controller downloads.
  • ir.actions.server: runs code or writes records; see the server actions chapter. When returned from a button, its result action is executed by the client.
  • ir.actions.client: opens a registered JavaScript action by tag; params pass through. The tag must exist in the actions registry of the web client.
  • ir.actions.report: prints a report; see the PDF reports chapter.

docs.title: Menus
docs.text:
<menuitem id="menu_library_root" name="Library" web_icon="library,static/description/icon.png"
          sequence="40"/>
<menuitem id="menu_library_books" name="Books" parent="menu_library_root"
          action="library_book_action" sequence="10"/>
<menuitem id="menu_library_config" name="Configuration" parent="menu_library_root"
          groups="library.group_manager" sequence="90"/>

A menu without a parent is an app tile. A menu without an action is a folder; it only shows if at least one child is visible to the user. groups restricts the menu, but it does not secure the model: users in other groups can still reach the data through URLs and RPC. Real protection is in access rights.

docs.title: Bindings: the Action and Print menus
docs.text:
Setting binding_model_id on an action adds it to the Action dropdown of that model's views. binding_type is action (the Action menu) or report (the Print menu), and binding_view_types limits it to list, form, or both.

<record id="library_book_archive_action" model="ir.actions.server">
  <field name="name">Archive selected</field>
  <field name="model_id" ref="model_library_book"/>
  <field name="binding_model_id" ref="model_library_book"/>
  <field name="binding_view_types">list</field>
  <field name="state">code</field>
  <field name="code">records.write({'active': False})</field>
</record>

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A user-visible domain on the action that conflicts with filters produces an empty list with no hint why. Keep domains narrow and document them.
  • context on the action is evaluated in the client, with uid, active_id, active_ids, context_today; it is not Python server-side.
  • Menus appear in order of sequence, ties broken by id; leaving all sequences at default produces install-order menus.
  • Deleting an action that a menu still references breaks the menu cache for everyone; remove the menu first, or declare both in one file.
  • Menu visibility is cached per user and group; after changing groups, update the module and reload.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: Odoo 16 uses tree in view_mode; 17 and 18 use list. ir.actions.server gained the webhook state in 18. The old ir.actions.act_window view_type field is gone.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Find every action bound to your model and where its menus point:

select a.id, a.name->>'en_US', a.res_model, a.view_mode from ir_act_window a where a.res_model = 'library.book';

docs.title: Data files
docs.text: Data files are how a module ships records: views, menus, security rules, demo content, configuration. They are declared in the manifest, loaded in order at install and update, and tracked through ir.model.data so a second load updates instead of duplicating. Most upgrade bugs trace back to misunderstanding this loop.

docs.title: Manifest keys
docs.text:
{
    "name": "Library",
    "version": "18.0.1.0.0",
    "depends": ["base", "mail"],
    "data": [
        "security/library_security.xml",
        "security/ir.model.access.csv",
        "views/library_book_views.xml",
        "views/library_menus.xml",
        "data/library_sequence.xml",
    ],
    "demo": ["demo/library_demo.xml"],
}

Files in data load on install and on every update. Files in demo load only when the database was created with demo data. Order inside the list is the load order: a file may only reference XML IDs defined earlier (or in a dependency). Security groups go first, because access rules and views reference them; menus go after the actions they point to.

docs.title: XML records
docs.text:
<odoo>
  <record id="book_dune" model="library.book">
    <field name="name">Dune</field>
    <field name="author_id" ref="author_herbert"/>
    <field name="pages" eval="412"/>
    <field name="tag_ids" eval="[(6, 0, [ref('tag_scifi')])]"/>
  </record>
</odoo>
  • ref="module.xmlid" resolves a many2one; the module prefix is optional inside the same module.
  • eval runs a Python expression with ref(), time, datetime, timedelta and a few helpers in scope. Use it for numbers, booleans, and x2many commands.
  • type="xml" or type="html" on a field stores a literal markup fragment, used for QWeb arch and HTML fields.
  • Shortcuts exist: <menuitem>, <template>, <report>-style elements are sugar that generate ir.ui.menu, ir.ui.view, and (in older versions) report actions. They are covered in their own chapters.

docs.title: How the XML ID works
docs.text: Every <record id="x"> creates an ir.model.data row (module, name, model, res_id). On the next load the loader looks that row up: found means write to the existing record, missing means create. Renaming an id therefore creates a second record and orphans the old one; the old row is cleaned up only if the loader sees it is no longer declared (and it is not under noupdate).

docs.title: noupdate
docs.text:
<odoo noupdate="1">
  <record id="seq_loan" model="ir.sequence">
    <field name="name">Loan</field>
    <field name="code">library.loan</field>
    <field name="prefix">LN/</field>
  </record>
</odoo>

With noupdate="1", the record is created on install and never touched again by module updates. Use it for data the customer is expected to edit: sequences, mail templates they customize, default configuration. Do not use it for views or security rules you expect to change; an edited XML would silently not apply.

A single record can opt in with <record noupdate="1"> inside a normal <odoo> block. The flag lives on the ir.model.data row (noupdate column), which means it is set when the record is first created. Changing the attribute in XML later does not change existing rows in a stable way; if you need to force a reload of a noupdate record, write the record from a migration script or set the ir.model.data.noupdate flag to false first.

A common production surprise: you fix a mail template or a record rule in XML, deploy, update the module, and nothing changes. The record is noupdate. Check with select module, name, noupdate from ir_model_data where name = 'your_xmlid';.

docs.title: Updating and deleting from data files
docs.text:
<!-- change one field on a record owned by another module -->
<record id="base.main_company" model="res.company" forcecreate="0">
  <field name="street">Example Street 1</field>
</record>

<!-- remove a record -->
<delete model="ir.ui.view" search="[('name', '=', 'library.book.legacy')]"/>
<delete model="library.tag" id="tag_obsolete"/>

Writing onto another module's XML ID works, but if that record is noupdate the write is skipped on updates. forcecreate="0" tells the loader not to recreate the record if it was deleted by the user.

docs.title: CSV files
docs.text:
The file name is the model name; the first row is the header.

id,name,code
tag_scifi,Science fiction,SF
tag_history,History,HI
  • Many2one columns use field_id for the XML ID or field_id:id; to match by name use field_id/name... but prefer XML IDs, names are not unique.
  • The special file ir.model.access.csv uses columns id,name,model_id:id,group_id:id,perm_read,perm_write,perm_create,perm_unlink. model_id:id is model_library_book, the XML ID Odoo generates for each model (model_ plus the dotted name with underscores).
  • CSV records are updated by XML ID too. There is no noupdate attribute in CSV; the loader treats those rows as normal updatable data, except ir.model.access.csv entries, which are updated on every upgrade.

docs.title: Load order and dependencies
docs.text:
1. Modules load in dependency order, then alphabetically.
  2. Within a module: data files in manifest order, then demo.
  3. After all files, the module's post_init_hook runs on install only.

If file B needs a record from file A, put A first. If two modules each need the other's data, the design is wrong; move the shared piece into a base module.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Referencing an XML ID from a module not in depends works on your machine, because that module happens to be installed, and fails on a clean database.
  • Forgetting a new file in the manifest: the file is simply not loaded, with no warning.
  • Putting demo records in data: they ship to production.
  • Using noupdate on ir.ui.view and then wondering why a fix does not apply.
  • Copying a record with its XML ID from a dump: two records cannot share one ID, the loader reports a duplicate key on ir_model_data.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: The <report> shortcut tag was removed years ago; define ir.actions.report records instead (see the PDF reports chapter). Since 17 the loader also validates view architecture earlier, so a bad view in a data file fails at update time rather than at first open.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Run the update and read what the loader did:

odoo-bin -d dev_db -u library --stop-after-init --log-level=info 2>&1 | grep -i "library"

Then list what you own and which of it is frozen:

select name, model, noupdate from ir_model_data where module = 'library' order by model;

docs.title: Email templates
docs.text: A mail.template stores a subject, body, recipients and attachments for one model, with placeholders filled in per record at send time. Use it when the text should be editable by an administrator without touching code.

docs.title: A template record
docs.text:
<odoo noupdate="1">
  <record id="mail_template_loan_due" model="mail.template">
    <field name="name">Library: loan due</field>
    <field name="model_id" ref="model_library_loan"/>
    <field name="subject">Loan {{ object.name }} is due on {{ object.due_date }}</field>
    <field name="email_from">{{ (object.company_id.email_formatted or user.email_formatted) }}</field>
    <field name="partner_to">{{ object.borrower_id.id }}</field>
    <field name="report_template_ids" eval="[(4, ref('library.action_report_loan'))]"/>
    <field name="body_html" type="html">
      <div>
        <p>Hello <t t-out="object.borrower_id.name or ''"/>,</p>
        <p>Your loan <strong t-out="object.name"/> is due on
           <t t-out="format_date(object.due_date)"/>.</p>
      </div>
    </field>
  </record>
</odoo>

Two syntaxes live side by side:

  • Fields like subject, email_from, partner_to, email_to, email_cc, reply_to, lang use inline expressions: {{ expression }}, Python evaluated by the inline renderer.
  • body_html uses QWeb: t-out, t-if, t-foreach. The context has object, user, ctx, and helpers such as format_date, format_datetime, format_amount.

noupdate="1" is the norm: administrators edit these through the UI, and an update must not overwrite their wording. See the data files chapter.

partner_to takes ids as a comma-separated string, evaluated per record. email_to is for raw addresses. Prefer partners: they carry the language, the bounce history, and the opt-out flags.

docs.title: Sending from code
docs.text:
template = self.env.ref("library.mail_template_loan_due")
template.send_mail(loan.id, force_send=False, email_values={"email_cc": "desk@example.com"})
  • force_send=False queues the mail.mail for the mail cron instead of sending inside the transaction. This is what you want in loops, and if the SMTP server is down your transaction still commits.
  • email_values overrides template fields for this send only.
  • send_mail creates a mail.mail and, with mail.compose.message semantics, logs the message on the record's chatter unless you pass email_layout_xmlid or use message_post_with_source.

For chatter-integrated sending prefer:

loan.message_post_with_source(
    "library.mail_template_loan_due",
    subtype_xmlid="mail.mt_comment",
)

This renders the template, posts it in the chatter and emails followers. Use email_layout_xmlid="mail.mail_notification_light" to wrap the body in the notification layout.

docs.title: Previewing and testing
docs.text: template.generate_email(res_ids, ["subject", "body_html", "email_to"]) returns the rendered values as a dict without sending. The template form has a "Preview" button in developer mode that does the same for a chosen record.

docs.title: Languages
docs.text: Set the lang field to an inline expression like {{ object.borrower_id.lang }}. Translations of the template are stored per field, so translate through the UI or .po files; the template is rendered in that language when lang resolves.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Mixing syntaxes: {{ }} in body_html does not work as in subject; QWeb is used there. And t-out in subject is meaningless.
  • object.name or '' guards against False printing as nothing odd in some contexts; with t-out False renders empty anyway, but inside {{ }} concatenation it can raise.
  • Outgoing mail server not configured on a staging copy: use mail neutralization so staging does not send real mail. Never test against real addresses.
  • Missing recipients: mail.mail created, state "Outgoing", no error. Check the mail.mail list and the log.
  • Editing the template in the UI and then updating the module: the noupdate flag protects the edits; a missing flag overwrites them.
  • Sandbox: users without the technical group cannot edit dynamic placeholders; only designated groups can write expressions.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: Inline placeholders {{ }} replaced the old ${} Mako syntax in 15, so 16 and later are on the new form. In 17, templates gained report_template_ids (many2many) in place of the single report_template; in 18 the field is the many2many form.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Preview a rendered template without sending anything, in a development shell:

env.ref("library.mail_template_loan_due").generate_email([1], ["subject", "body_html"])

docs.title: Form views
docs.text: A form view is the single-record editor. Most of the work in a module's UI goes here: laying out fields, exposing workflow buttons, and showing related records. The structure is fixed by convention, and following it gets you responsive behaviour, chatter placement, and readonly handling for free.

docs.title: Skeleton
docs.text:
<record id="library_book_view_form" model="ir.ui.view">
    <field name="name">library.book.form</field>
    <field name="model">library.book</field>
    <field name="arch" type="xml">
        <form string="Book">
            <header>
                <button name="action_borrow" string="Borrow" type="object"
                        class="btn-primary" invisible="state != 'available'"/>
                <button name="action_return" string="Return" type="object"
                        invisible="state != 'borrowed'"/>
                <field name="state" widget="statusbar"
                       statusbar_visible="available,borrowed"/>
            </header>
            <sheet>
                <div class="oe_button_box" name="button_box">
                    <button name="action_view_loans" type="object"
                            class="oe_stat_button" icon="fa-book">
                        <field name="loan_count" widget="statinfo" string="Loans"/>
                    </button>
                </div>
                <widget name="web_ribbon" title="Archived" bg_color="text-bg-danger"
                        invisible="active"/>
                <field name="image_1920" widget="image" class="oe_avatar"/>
                <div class="oe_title">
                    <label for="name"/>
                    <h1><field name="name" placeholder="Title"/></h1>
                </div>
                <group>
                    <group name="main">
                        <field name="author_id"/>
                        <field name="isbn"/>
                    </group>
                    <group name="dates">
                        <field name="published_on"/>
                        <field name="company_id" groups="base.group_multi_company"/>
                    </group>
                </group>
                <notebook>
                    <page string="Loans" name="loans">
                        <field name="loan_ids">
                            <list>
                                <field name="partner_id"/>
                                <field name="date_out"/>
                                <field name="date_due"/>
                            </list>
                        </field>
                    </page>
                    <page string="Notes" name="notes">
                        <field name="note"/>
                    </page>
                </notebook>
            </sheet>
            <chatter/>
        </form>
    </field>
</record>

<chatter/> is the Odoo 18 shorthand for the followers/messages/activities block. It requires the model to inherit mail.thread (and mail.activity.mixin for activities).

Versions. Before 17 the chatter was written as <div class="oe_chatter"> with three <field name="message_follower_ids"/>, <field name="activity_ids"/>, <field name="message_ids"/> children. The old markup still renders in 17 and 18 core views that have not been converted, but new code should use <chatter/>. Verify on your target version before publishing a module for 16.

docs.title: Layout primitives
docs.text:
• <sheet> gives the centred white paper look. Without it, the form uses the full width and has no padding; use that for wizards and dialog forms.
  • <group> lays out label/field pairs. Two sibling groups inside a parent group render as two columns. col="4" on a group sets the number of columns; colspan on a child spans them.
  • <separator string="..."/> is a labelled rule between blocks inside a group.
  • <notebook> / <page> are tabs. Always set name on pages: it is the stable anchor other modules use in xpath.
  • <div class="oe_title"> with <h1> is the large title area under the button box.
  • <field ... nolabel="1"/> hides the label; to supply your own, use <label for="field"/>.

docs.title: Buttons
docs.text:
<button name="action_borrow" string="Borrow" type="object"/>
<button name="%(library.action_loan_wizard)d" string="Loan..." type="action"/>
  • type="object" calls a method on the model with self set to the current record. The method must be public (no leading underscore) because it is callable from the client.
  • type="action" runs an action by ID. %(module.xml_id)d resolves to the numeric ID at load time.
  • class="btn-primary" marks the main action of a given state; keep one primary per state.
  • confirm="Return this book?" adds a confirmation dialog.
  • data-hotkey="q" binds a keyboard shortcut.

docs.title: Visibility expressions
docs.text:
In Odoo 17 and 18 the attributes invisible, readonly, required (and column_invisible in lists) take a Python-like expression evaluated against the record's field values:

<field name="isbn" readonly="state != 'draft'" required="kind == 'book'"/>
<field name="date_due" invisible="not date_out"/>

Supported: field names, comparison and boolean operators, literals, context.get(...), parent.field inside x2many sub-views, id, uid is not available. All fields used in an expression must be present in the view, otherwise the client does not know their value; add them as <field name="x" invisible="1"/> when you only need them for logic.

Versions. attrs and states were removed. In Odoo 16 you wrote attrs="{'invisible': [('state', '!=', 'available')]}" and states="draft,sent" on buttons; both are invalid in 17 and 18 and fail with an arch validation error at load. Convert: states="draft,sent" becomes invisible="state not in ('draft', 'sent')". I checked the Odoo 18 sale order form and it uses direct expressions only.

docs.title: Statusbar
docs.text: widget="statusbar" on a Selection or Many2one shows the pipeline. statusbar_visible lists the states shown when the record is not in them; the current state is always shown. For a Many2one stage, add options="{'clickable': '1'}" to allow clicking to change stage, and options="{'fold_field': 'fold'}" to collapse folded stages.

docs.title: Smart buttons
docs.text:
A smart button is a oe_stat_button in a oe_button_box at the top of the sheet. Pattern: a computed count field on the model, a button calling a method that returns a window action filtered on the record.

loan_count = fields.Integer(compute='_compute_loan_count')

def _compute_loan_count(self):
    data = self.env['library.loan']._read_group(
        [('book_id', 'in', self.ids)], ['book_id'], ['__count'])
    counts = {book.id: count for book, count in data}
    for book in self:
        book.loan_count = counts.get(book.id, 0)

def action_view_loans(self):
    self.ensure_one()
    action = self.env['ir.actions.act_window']._for_xml_id('library.action_loan')
    action['domain'] = [('book_id', '=', self.id)]
    action['context'] = {'default_book_id': self.id}
    return action

Use _read_group with __count once per recordset, not a search_count per record; the latter issues one query per row when the button appears in a list or kanban.

For a boolean toggle (active, published) use widget="boolean_button" with options="{'terminology': 'archive'}".

docs.title: Fields worth knowing
docs.text: widget use many2one_avatar_user user with avatar many2many_tags tags, with options="{'color_field': 'color'}" monetary requires a currency_field on the model or options="{'currency_field': 'currency_id'}" html rich text; options="{'collaborative': true}" for live editing priority star rating from a Selection handle drag handle in an x2many list

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Field used in an expression but missing from the view. The expression silently evaluates with the value undefined. Always include logic-only fields as invisible.
  • Putting groups on a field that other expressions depend on. For users without the group the field is removed from the arch, and the expression that reads it fails. Guard the expression too, or move it into a group-restricted container.
  • Calling a private method from a button. Odoo rejects type="object" buttons that start with an underscore.
  • Missing ensure_one() in button methods that assume one record. Multi-selection actions call the method with several records.
  • Heavy computed fields in the form. A non-stored compute with a search-per-record loops once per displayed record in x2many lists. Batch it with _read_group.
  • Page without name. The next module that wants to add a sibling tab has to anchor on position.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Load a form as the client would, read-only, to see what survives inheritance and group pruning:

arch = env['library.book'].get_view(view_type='form')['arch']
print(arch)

Search it for the field names your expressions use; any missing one is the bug.

docs.title: Kanban views
docs.text: A kanban view renders one card per record, optionally in columns by a group-by field. The card is a QWeb template run in the browser, not on the server, so the data it can use is only what the view declared as <field> and what the web client adds.

docs.title: Minimal view
docs.text:
<record id="library_book_kanban" model="ir.ui.view">
  <field name="name">library.book.kanban</field>
  <field name="model">library.book</field>
  <field name="arch" type="xml">
    <kanban default_group_by="state" class="o_kanban_small_column" quick_create="false"
            records_draggable="1" group_create="false">
      <field name="name"/>
      <field name="state"/>
      <field name="color"/>
      <field name="author_id"/>
      <progressbar field="state" colors='{"available": "success", "lent": "warning", "lost": "danger"}'/>
      <templates>
        <t t-name="card">
          <field name="name" class="fw-bold fs-5"/>
          <div class="text-muted">
            <field name="author_id"/>
          </div>
          <footer>
            <field name="tag_ids" widget="many2many_tags" options="{'color_field': 'color'}"/>
            <field name="user_id" widget="many2one_avatar_user" class="ms-auto"/>
          </footer>
        </t>
      </templates>
    </kanban>
  </field>
</record>

docs.title: Template mechanics
docs.text:
• The card template is named card in 18 (a <t t-name="card"> directly under <templates>). In 16 and 17 it is kanban-box, and menus use kanban-menu.
  • <field name="x"/> outputs the field with its widget. record.x.value gives the raw value and record.x.raw_value the unformatted one, available in t-esc expressions. Every field you read must be declared in the view, or it is not loaded.
  • Standard layout classes: Bootstrap 5 utilities (d-flex, fw-bold, ms-auto) and Odoo's o_kanban_* helpers.
  • t-if, t-foreach, t-att-class, t-attf-class work as in server QWeb, but the expression language is JavaScript, not Python.
<div t-attf-class="oe_kanban_color_#{record.color.raw_value} oe_kanban_global_click">

oe_kanban_global_click makes the whole card open the record; without it only the fields with links react.

docs.title: Columns, quick create, drag and drop
docs.text:
• default_group_by: the field to group columns by. Many2one, selection, and date fields work. Dragging between columns writes the field, so it must be writable and not computed.
  • Empty stages: for a many2one the empty groups are shown when the comodel defines _group_expand or group_expand on the field; otherwise only groups with records appear.
  • quick_create: the small "add" row. on_create="module.quick_create_view" points to a minimal form view used in a dialog.
  • records_draggable, groups_draggable, group_create, group_edit, group_delete toggle the controls.
  • sample="1" shows fake cards when the model is empty, which helps first-run screens.

docs.title: Progress bar
docs.text: <progressbar field="state" colors="{...}"/> draws a bar at the top of each column, counting records by the value of field. An optional sum_field sums a numeric field instead of counting. Clicking a segment filters the column. Value keys in colors must match the selection keys, not the labels.

docs.title: Dropdown menu and actions
docs.text:
Buttons inside cards use type="object", type="action", or type="open", type="edit", type="delete":

<button name="action_mark_lent" type="object" class="btn btn-sm btn-primary">Lend</button>

In 18, a dropdown menu is declared with a separate <t t-name="menu"> template; in 16/17 it is kanban-menu. Items there are links with type="..." and the same classes.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Using a field in the template without declaring it: it renders empty, with no error in production.
  • Python expressions in the template: they are JS. record.name.value is fine; len(...) is not.
  • Expensive related fields on a card multiply by the page size (default 40 per column, 80 in ungrouped). Store what you display.
  • Grouping on a non-stored computed field fails; the group needs a database column.
  • Images: use <field name="image_128" widget="image"/> and a small size field; never image_1920 in a card.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: The kanban template syntax changed in 18. <t t-name="kanban-box"> with oe_kanban_* markup is the 16/17 form; 18 replaces it with t-name="card" and a simpler structure. The legacy kanban-box still renders in 18 but logs a deprecation warning in the console (verified in the 18 arch parser); convert views when you touch them.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text: Add default_group_by="state" to the view and drag a card between columns. Check the write in the server log, and then try the same with a computed state to see the failure.

docs.title: List views
docs.text:
The list view shows many records as rows. It is the default entry point to most menus, so its columns decide what users see first and how much the server reads per page. Odoo 18 names the root element <list>.

Versions. Up to Odoo 17 the root element was <tree> and the view type was tree. In Odoo 18 core views, including sale.sale_order_tree (checked in the source), use <list>. The view type string in actions is list as well: view_mode="list,form". Existing <tree> arch in custom modules is still accepted on 18 for compatibility, but write <list> in anything new and //list in new xpaths. Odoo 16 only knows <tree>.

docs.title: Basic list
docs.text:
<record id="library_book_view_list" model="ir.ui.view">
    <field name="name">library.book.list</field>
    <field name="model">library.book</field>
    <field name="arch" type="xml">
        <list string="Books" default_order="name">
            <field name="name"/>
            <field name="author_id"/>
            <field name="published_on" optional="hide"/>
            <field name="state" widget="badge"
                   decoration-success="state == 'available'"
                   decoration-warning="state == 'borrowed'"/>
            <field name="company_id" groups="base.group_multi_company" optional="show"/>
        </list>
    </field>
</record>

docs.title: Row decorations
docs.text:
On the <list> element, decoration-* attributes style whole rows from an expression over the row's fields:

<list decoration-danger="date_due and date_due < current_date"
      decoration-muted="state == 'returned'"
      decoration-bf="state == 'overdue'">

Available suffixes: bf, it, danger, info, muted, primary, success, warning. The same attributes work on a single <field> to colour one cell. current_date is available in these expressions. All fields in the expression must appear in the list, as invisible columns if needed: <field name="date_due" column_invisible="1"/>.

In 17 and 18 the expressions are Python-like (state == 'x'). Older versions used the same decoration syntax, but invisible on columns used attrs; see the form chapter for the replacement.

docs.title: Optional columns
docs.text: optional="show" or optional="hide" puts the column in the toggle dropdown at the right of the header, with the stated default. The user's choice is stored in the browser, per list view and user. Use it for everything beyond the three or four columns that identify the record.

docs.title: Hiding a column by condition
docs.text:
<field name="price" column_invisible="parent.kind == 'service'"/>

column_invisible hides the whole column and is evaluated once for the list (against the parent record when the list is inside an x2many). invisible on a field in a list hides the cell per row. The two are different; using invisible and expecting the header to disappear is a frequent surprise.

docs.title: Editable lists
docs.text:
<list editable="bottom">

editable="top" or "bottom" makes rows editable inline, with new rows added at that end. Without it, clicking a row opens the form. Related attributes:

  • create="0", edit="0", delete="0" disable the corresponding action.
  • import="0" hides the import button.
  • multi_edit="1" allows editing a field across all selected rows.
  • open_form_view="1" adds an arrow to open the full form from an editable x2many.
  • on_create="module.action_xml_id" replaces the quick-add row with an action (typically a wizard).

Inside an editable list, required and readonly accept expressions over the row:

<field name="date_due" readonly="state == 'returned'" required="state == 'borrowed'"/>

docs.title: Widgets worth knowing
docs.text: widget use handle drag handle, requires an integer sequence field and default_order="sequence" badge coloured pill for Selection/Many2one many2many_tags tags, short and wrapped boolean_toggle inline switch progressbar percentage with options="{'current_value': 'x', 'max_value': 'y'}" monetary respects the row's currency

docs.title: Totals and grouping
docs.text:
<field name="amount" sum="Total"/>
<field name="qty" avg="Average"/>

sum, avg, min, max on a field display a footer value for the loaded page. For exact totals over the whole result, rely on group headers: a grouped list shows the aggregate of each group computed in the database by read_group. Aggregation needs the field to be stored; a non-stored computed field shows no aggregate.

Group by a field from the search view or by default through the action context: {'search_default_group_by_author': 1} with a matching filter in the search view, or {'group_by': ['author_id']} for a direct default.

groups_limit, limit on the list, and default_group_by are available on the root element: <list default_group_by="state" limit="40">.

docs.title: x2many lists inside a form
docs.text:
The <list> inside a <field name="loan_ids"> is an inline view used only there. It can differ from the model's standalone list:

<field name="loan_ids">
    <list editable="bottom">
        <field name="partner_id"/>
        <field name="date_out"/>
    </list>
</field>

If you omit the inline <list>, Odoo uses the model's default list view, which may have many columns. Define the inline view when the sub-table must be compact.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Columns that compute per row. A non-stored compute or a related field across several relations is evaluated for every row on the page. 80 rows with a compute that runs a search inside is 80 queries. Store it or batch the computation.
  • optional columns still load. The server reads the fields whether or not the user displays the column. Hiding a costly column does not make the list faster.
  • Decoration fields not in the view. The decoration silently never fires. Add the field as column_invisible="1".
  • Using sum on the page as a global total. It sums only the loaded records (up to limit). Mislabelled totals cause real accounting confusion; label the footer or use a pivot/report for exact figures.
  • Editable list with required fields on a hidden column. The user cannot save a row because a field they cannot see is empty. Give it a default or make it visible.
  • Changing the standard list through xpath on tree. On Odoo 18 core views the element is list; an xpath on //tree does not match and the module update fails.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Check which fields and decorations the client receives, read-only:

arch = env['library.book'].get_view(view_type='list')['arch']
print(arch)

Compare with the model's _fields to see which columns are stored and therefore sortable and aggregatable:

print({n: f.store for n, f in env['library.book']._fields.items()})

docs.title: Other views
docs.text:
Besides list, form and kanban, Odoo ships analytical and scheduling views. All are declared as ir.ui.view records of the matching type and enabled by adding the type to the action's view_mode. Several of them depend on the Enterprise edition; check before promising them to a Community project.

View Edition Purpose pivot Community Cross-tab of measures by row and column groups graph Community Bar, line, pie charts from the same grouping engine calendar Community Records as events on a date grid activity Community (needs mail) Matrix of records by scheduled activity type cohort, gantt, map, grid Enterprise Retention, timeline planning, geographic, timesheet entry

docs.title: Pivot
docs.text:
<pivot string="Loans" sample="1">
  <field name="book_id" type="row"/>
  <field name="loan_date" interval="month" type="col"/>
  <field name="fee" type="measure"/>
</pivot>

type is row, col, or measure. Date fields take interval (day, week, month, quarter, year). A measure must be a stored numeric field with an aggregator; aggregator="sum" (the default) can be changed to avg, min, max, count_distinct on the field definition in Python. Odoo 16 spelled this group_operator; 17 and later use aggregator.

docs.title: Graph
docs.text:
<graph type="bar" stacked="True">
  <field name="loan_date" interval="month"/>
  <field name="book_id"/>
  <field name="fee" type="measure"/>
</graph>

The first dimension field is the x axis; the second splits into series. type is bar, line, or pie. Graph and pivot read through formatted_read_group style grouping, so everything shown must be stored.

docs.title: Calendar
docs.text:
<calendar string="Loans" date_start="loan_date" date_stop="due_date" color="book_id" mode="month" quick_create="0">
  <field name="book_id"/>
  <field name="borrower_id" avatar_field="avatar_128"/>
</calendar>

date_start is required; date_stop or date_delay (hours) set the length; all_day names a boolean field. color accepts a many2one or selection field and picks a color per value. mode is day, week, month, or year. Filters in the right panel come from <field ... filters="1"/>.

docs.title: Activity
docs.text:
<activity string="Books">
  <templates>
    <t t-name="activity-box">
      <field name="name"/>
    </t>
  </templates>
</activity>

Requires mail.activity.mixin on the model. The card template is activity-box. The view shows one row per record and one column per activity type.

docs.title: Gantt, map, cohort (Enterprise)
docs.text: These live in web_gantt, web_map, web_cohort. Gantt needs date_start and date_stop plus default_scale; map needs a res_partner many2one (res_partner) with coordinates; cohort needs date_start, date_stop, measure, interval. Because they are Enterprise code, test your module on both editions and keep the view in a separate file loaded only when the dependency is present.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A view type missing from view_mode: the switch button never appears and nothing logs an error.
  • Pivot on a non-stored measure: the field list is empty or the measure raises on load.
  • Putting thousands of rows into a calendar month: every record is fetched for the visible range; add a domain via action context.
  • Many2one color field in calendar must be stored; computed values flicker.
  • Dates in the calendar are converted to the user's timezone, but date fields have none; use datetime for events.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: 16 uses <tree>-style naming elsewhere but these views are unchanged by name. In 17 group_operator became aggregator on fields; 18 keeps aggregator. The 18 pivot and graph use the new formatted_read_group on the server when available.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text: Add pivot,graph to the loans action's view_mode, upgrade the module, and open the Pivot. Drag "Book" from row to column and watch the grouping change the RPC call in the network tab.

docs.title: PDF reports
docs.text: A PDF report is a QWeb template rendered to HTML on the server, then converted to PDF by wkhtmltopdf. A report action (ir.actions.report) links the template to a model and puts a button in the Print menu.

docs.title: Report action and template
docs.text:
<record id="action_report_loan" model="ir.actions.report">
  <field name="name">Loan slip</field>
  <field name="model">library.loan</field>
  <field name="report_type">qweb-pdf</field>
  <field name="report_name">library.report_loan_document</field>
  <field name="report_file">library.report_loan_document</field>
  <field name="print_report_name">'Loan - %s' % (object.name or 'draft')</field>
  <field name="binding_model_id" ref="model_library_loan"/>
  <field name="binding_type">report</field>
  <field name="paperformat_id" ref="library.paperformat_a5"/>
</record>

<template id="report_loan_document">
  <t t-call="web.html_container">
    <t t-foreach="docs" t-as="doc">
      <t t-call="web.external_layout">
        <div class="page">
          <h2>Loan <span t-field="doc.name"/></h2>
          <p>Borrower: <span t-field="doc.borrower_id"/></p>
          <table class="table table-sm">
            <tr t-foreach="doc.line_ids" t-as="line">
              <td t-out="line.book_id.name"/>
              <td class="text-end" t-field="line.fee"/>
            </tr>
          </table>
        </div>
      </t>
    </t>
  </t>
</template>

Essentials:

  • report_name is the XML ID of the template; docs is the recordset being printed, doc_ids and doc_model are also passed.
  • web.html_container provides the HTML shell; web.external_layout adds the company header and footer; web.internal_layout is the plain variant. Content goes in <div class="page">.
  • print_report_name is a Python expression with object; it sets the download filename.
  • binding_type of report shows the action in the Print dropdown. attachment and attachment_use store the generated PDF on the record and reuse it, which freezes the output; set them only for legal documents.

docs.title: Custom data: report models
docs.text:
When the template needs computed data, define an abstract model named report.<report_name>:

class ReportLoan(models.AbstractModel):
    _name = "report.library.report_loan_document"
    _description = "Loan slip report"

    @api.model
    def _get_report_values(self, docids, data=None):
        docs = self.env["library.loan"].browse(docids)
        return {"doc_ids": docids, "doc_model": "library.loan", "docs": docs,
                "total_fee": sum(docs.mapped("fee"))}

The returned dict becomes the template context.

docs.title: Paper format
docs.text:
<record id="paperformat_a5" model="report.paperformat">
  <field name="name">A5 library</field>
  <field name="format">A5</field>
  <field name="orientation">Portrait</field>
  <field name="margin_top">30</field>
  <field name="margin_bottom">20</field>
  <field name="header_spacing">25</field>
  <field name="dpi">90</field>
</record>

header_spacing is the gap between the header and content; if the header overlaps the body, raise it and margin_top together. Use dpi 90 to match what wkhtmltopdf renders consistently.

docs.title: Rendering from code
docs.text:
pdf, _fmt = self.env["ir.actions.report"]._render_qweb_pdf("library.action_report_loan", res_ids=loan.ids)

The first argument is the report reference (XML ID or report_name). Attach it to a mail with ir.attachment and attachment_ids.

docs.title: wkhtmltopdf
docs.text:
wkhtmltopdf with patched Qt is required; the unpatched distro build ignores header and footer templates and spacing. Odoo checks the binary and logs a warning on start if it is missing or unpatched. It renders an old WebKit: no CSS grid, limited flexbox. Use tables and Bootstrap's grid (row/col-* work, but print with col-6 rather than responsive classes).

For local debugging, add ?debug=1 to the report URL /report/html/<report_name>/<id> to see the HTML before conversion.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Header and footer are rendered in separate processes; assets (fonts, images) must be reachable at the base URL (web.base.url) from the server itself. A wrong web.base.url gives blank logos.
  • t-field with widget: "image" on large images produces large PDFs; use the sized variants.
  • Report changes not showing: a stored attachment is reused. Delete the attachment or clear attachment on the action.
  • Fonts: wkhtmltopdf uses system fonts; if a glyph is missing, install the font on the server, not in CSS.
  • Multi-record prints loop docs; page breaks need style="page-break-after: always;" on each doc.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: From 17 to 18 the layouts are web.external_layout with company-selectable styles; report_type, report_name, and _render_qweb_pdf keep the same shape. In 16, _render_qweb_pdf took res_ids as the first argument after a report reference, in 17+ the report is resolved through the action record; check your call site when porting.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text: Open /report/html/library.report_loan_document/1 in a browser (developer mode) to iterate on the layout without PDF conversion, then print the same report from the UI to compare.

docs.title: QWeb templates
docs.text: QWeb is Odoo's XML template engine. The same directive language renders website pages, PDF reports, emails (in part), and, with a JavaScript implementation, the OWL components of the web client. This chapter is about the server side, where templates are ir.ui.view records of type qweb evaluated by Python.

docs.title: Defining a template
docs.text:
<template id="book_card" name="Book card">
  <div class="card">
    <h3 t-out="book.name"/>
    <p t-if="book.author_id">By <span t-field="book.author_id"/></p>
    <p t-else="">Anonymous</p>
    <ul>
      <li t-foreach="book.loan_ids" t-as="loan">
        <t t-out="loan_index + 1"/>. <t t-out="loan.borrower_id.name"/>
        <t t-if="loan_last"> (latest)</t>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</template>

<template> is shorthand for an ir.ui.view with type="qweb"; id becomes the XML ID.

docs.title: Directives you use daily
docs.text:
• t-out="expr": output an escaped value (the successor of t-esc/t-raw). False and None render as empty. Markup objects are not escaped again.
  • t-field="record.field": render a field using its formatting (dates, monetary values, many2one names). Accepts t-options='{"widget": "monetary"}'. Only works on records, not plain values.
  • t-if, t-elif, t-else: conditions. Python expressions.
  • t-foreach / t-as: loops. Helpers x_index, x_first, x_last, x_size, x_even, x_odd are available per alias.
  • t-set / t-value: assign a variable; t-set with a body captures markup. Variables are scoped to the enclosing element.
  • t-att-name="expr", t-attf-name="text #{expr}", t-att="dict": dynamic attributes.
  • t-call="module.template": include another template; the body of t-call becomes 0 (the "slot"), output with <t t-out="0"/>.
  • t-set-slot, t-slot and t-inherit: used for newer slot mechanisms and inheritance; stick to t-call plus t-out="0" unless you know why.
<template id="layout_box">
  <div class="box"><t t-out="0"/></div>
</template>
<template id="book_page">
  <t t-call="library.layout_box">
    <t t-set="title">Books</t>
    <p t-out="title"/>
  </t>
</template>

docs.title: Evaluation context
docs.text:
In website and report templates the context includes request, user_id, res_company, website, json, time, datetime, len, abs, min, max, and the values passed by the caller. Rendering from Python:

html = self.env["ir.qweb"]._render("library.book_card", {"book": book})

This returns Markup. Pass only trusted values in as markup; everything else is escaped.

docs.title: Escaping and safety
docs.text:
QWeb escapes on output by default, so t-out of user text is safe in HTML. The unsafe cases are building markup yourself in Python and passing it as a plain string (it will be escaped and look broken) or wrapping untrusted text in Markup() (it will be injected). Use Markup.format() or markupsafe.escape when composing.

Templates run in a restricted evaluator: no imports, no __ attribute access, no arbitrary builtins. Computation belongs in the model; the template displays.

docs.title: Inheritance
docs.text:
QWeb views inherit like other views, with xpath, covered in the next chapter on view inheritance:

<template id="book_card_extra" inherit_id="library.book_card">
  <xpath expr="//h3" position="after"><small t-out="book.isbn"/></xpath>
</template>

For website pages, customize_show="True" and active="False" make optional templates togglable from the editor.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• t-esc and t-raw are deprecated in favour of t-out (the Odoo 18 ir_qweb.py documents both as "Deprecated, please use t-out" and still compiles them). t-raw in particular was an XSS source; replace it.
  • A t-foreach over a recordset inside another over the same alias: inner variables shadow the outer.
  • t-field on a related path that is empty returns blank; on a False boolean it prints nothing useful. Use t-out with your own text.
  • Queries inside templates: each loan.borrower_id.name can hit the database. Prefetch in the model, pass a prepared structure.
  • Forgetting that t-set inside a loop does not leak outside; use an accumulator on the model side.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: t-raw and t-esc are deprecated in favour of t-out; Odoo 18 still accepts both (verified in ir_qweb.py), so old templates keep rendering, but write new ones with t-out. Report templates since 17 render through ir.qweb with web.external_layout, and 18 relies on the OWL-compatible attribute handling for t-att.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Render a template from the shell of a development database:

print(env["ir.qweb"]._render("library.book_card", {"book": env["library.book"].search([], limit=1)}))

docs.title: Scheduled actions
docs.text: ir.cron records run a server action at an interval. They are the standard way to do periodic work: nightly cleanups, sync jobs, reminders. The scheduler picks due jobs, locks each one, runs it as a given user, and moves nextcall forward.

docs.title: Defining one
docs.text:
<odoo noupdate="1">
  <record id="cron_library_overdue" model="ir.cron">
    <field name="name">Library: remind overdue loans</field>
    <field name="model_id" ref="model_library_loan"/>
    <field name="state">code</field>
    <field name="code">model._cron_remind_overdue()</field>
    <field name="user_id" ref="base.user_root"/>
    <field name="interval_number">1</field>
    <field name="interval_type">days</field>
    <field name="nextcall" eval="(datetime.now() + timedelta(days=1)).replace(hour=3, minute=0, second=0)"/>
    <field name="priority">5</field>
    <field name="active" eval="True"/>
  </record>
</odoo>

ir.cron inherits from ir.actions.server, so it has state, code, model_id. Fields verified in the 18 source: interval_number, interval_type (minutes, hours, days, weeks, months), nextcall, priority (0 is highest, default 5), active, user_id.

The code calls a model method; keep the method in the model:

@api.model
def _cron_remind_overdue(self):
    loans = self.search([("state", "=", "out"), ("due_date", "<", fields.Date.today())])
    template = self.env.ref("library.mail_template_loan_due")
    for loan in loans:
        template.send_mail(loan.id, force_send=False)

Name the method with a leading underscore so it is not callable over RPC by users.

docs.title: How the scheduler runs
docs.text:
A cron worker (or the main process with threads in dev) queries jobs where active and nextcall <= now(), ordered by failure count then priority. Each job is locked with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so two workers never run the same job. After the run, nextcall advances by the interval, repeated until it lies in the future: a job that was down for a week does not run seven times, it runs once (missed runs are skipped).

The job runs under user_id, with that user's access rights and company. base.user_root (OdooBot) bypasses access rules; a normal user does not. Choose deliberately. Multi-company: the cron sees the user's allowed companies only.

docs.title: Long jobs: batch and commit
docs.text:
A cron runs in one transaction by default, with a time limit set by limit_time_real_cron (falls back to limit_time_real). Processing a million rows in one go risks a timeout and a total rollback. Process in batches and let the framework help:

@api.model
def _cron_sync(self, batch=200):
    todo = self.search([("synced", "=", False)], limit=batch)
    for rec in todo:
        rec._sync_one()
    if len(todo) == batch:
        self.env.ref("library.cron_library_sync")._trigger()

_trigger() schedules an extra run soon, which is how you continue a batch without waiting a full interval. Odoo 18 also provides self.env["ir.cron"]._notify_progress(done=..., remaining=...), which reports how much of the job is done and how much is left (verified in ir_cron.py); there is no _commit_progress helper in 18.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• noupdate omitted: every module update resets nextcall or overwrites the interval an admin tuned.
  • nextcall default evaluated at install time: all your crons fire together at the same minute. Stagger them.
  • Cron on a copy of production: a restored database sends real mail and calls real APIs. Odoo's neutralization script disables crons and outgoing mail; run it on every non-production copy.
  • Doing work in the method that depends on request, the web session or the current user's company: none exists.
  • Swallowing exceptions: a failing cron that logs nothing is invisible. Let it raise; failures are counted and, after repeated failures, Odoo deactivates the job and notifies.
  • Running slow jobs at the same time as backups or peak hours.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: Up to 17 an ir.cron had numbercall (-1 for unlimited) and doall (catch up missed runs). Both are gone in 18; a data file that still sets them fails on load because the fields no longer exist. A one-shot job is now created and deactivated by the code, or triggered with _trigger(). Verified: numbercall does not appear in the 18 ir_cron.py.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
See what is scheduled and when, read-only:

select cron_name, nextcall, interval_number, interval_type, active, priority from ir_cron order by nextcall;

Run one job by hand from the UI: Settings, Technical, Scheduled Actions, open the record and press "Run Manually" (developer mode).

docs.title: Search views
docs.text: The search view defines what the user can type into the search box, which filters appear in the dropdown, and how records can be grouped. It is a separate view record of type search, attached to an action through search_view_id or picked by priority.

docs.title: Anatomy
docs.text:
<record id="library_book_search" model="ir.ui.view">
  <field name="name">library.book.search</field>
  <field name="model">library.book</field>
  <field name="arch" type="xml">
    <search string="Books">
      <field name="name" string="Title" filter_domain="['|', ('name', 'ilike', self), ('isbn', '=', self)]"/>
      <field name="author_id"/>
      <field name="tag_ids"/>
      <separator/>
      <filter name="available" string="Available" domain="[('state', '=', 'available')]"/>
      <filter name="late" string="Overdue" domain="[('due_date', '<', context_today().strftime('%Y-%m-%d'))]"/>
      <separator/>
      <filter name="archived" string="Archived" domain="[('active', '=', False)]"/>
      <group expand="0" string="Group By">
        <filter name="group_author" string="Author" context="{'group_by': 'author_id'}"/>
        <filter name="group_year" string="Published" context="{'group_by': 'published_date:year'}"/>
      </group>
      <searchpanel>
        <field name="category_id" icon="fa-folder" enable_counters="1"/>
      </searchpanel>
    </search>
  </field>
</record>

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: A <field> makes the search box offer "Search Title for: ...". The operator defaults to ilike for text and = for numbers and relations. filter_domain overrides it; self stands for the typed value. List several fields and the user chooses; fields marked operator or with filter_domain search that way. string renames the entry.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
• domain: applied when toggled. Filters in the same block (no <separator/> between) are ORed; separated blocks are ANDed. This is the single most misunderstood rule; test it with two filters toggled.
  • name is needed if you want search_default_<name> in an action context, and for inheriting.
  • date attribute: <filter name="d" date="create_date" string="Created"/> renders the period picker (month/quarter/year) in the dropdown.
  • Domains can use context_today(), relativedelta, datetime, time, and uid. Escape < as < in XML.

docs.title: Group by
docs.text: A group_by context on a filter. Date fields accept a granularity suffix: :day, :week, :month, :quarter, :year. Grouping by a related field works if it is stored.

docs.title: Search panel
docs.text: <searchpanel> adds a side tree for a many2one or selection field. Use select="multi" for checkboxes with a groupby for hierarchies. It issues extra read_group calls, so avoid it on huge models without a good index.

docs.title: Search defaults
docs.text:
On the action, context:

{'search_default_available': 1, 'search_default_author_id': 3}

The first toggles the filter named available; the second pre-fills the author_id field with a value. search_default_* keys are read by the view, not by the server, so they have no effect in a plain search() call.

docs.title: Custom saved filters
docs.text: Users create their own through "Save current search"; these are ir.filters records. If you want to ship one, create an ir.filters record with model_id, domain, context, and user_id empty for a shared filter.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Searching on a non-stored computed field fails unless you give it a search method.
  • filter_domain using self in a field of many2one is evaluated against the typed text; use name_search semantics deliberately, not the id.
  • Using attrs or states in a search view is meaningless; they are for form fields. See Versions.
  • A filter without a name cannot be targeted by search_default_* or by an xpath in an inherited view.
  • Default filters hide data: a user who sees "no records" because search_default_available hides most of them files a bug. Show the active filter in a help text.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: In 16 the search view takes the same elements as in 17 and 18. What changed is around it: attrs and states were dropped on form elements in 17 (use invisible, readonly and required with Python-like expressions), and in 18 tree became list in actions. Search views themselves were stable across these versions.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text: Open the Books list, toggle "Available" and "Overdue" together, then add "Archived" after the separator. Watch the domain with developer mode's "Edit Domain" or the network panel to see how OR and AND combine.

docs.title: Server actions and automation
docs.text: A server action is a stored operation on a model: write fields, create a record, run Python, call a webhook, or chain other actions. An automation rule (base.automation) attaches server actions to events such as record creation, a field change, or a time condition. Together they are the low-code layer; knowing their limits tells you when to write a module instead.

docs.title: Server action types (Odoo 18)
docs.text:
Verified in the 18 source, state offers: object_write (Update Record), object_create (Create Record), code (Execute Code), webhook (Send Webhook Notification), multi (Execute Existing Actions).

<record id="action_loan_mark_late" model="ir.actions.server">
  <field name="name">Mark overdue loans</field>
  <field name="model_id" ref="model_library_loan"/>
  <field name="binding_model_id" ref="model_library_loan"/>
  <field name="state">code</field>
  <field name="code">
for loan in records.filtered(lambda l: l.due_date and l.due_date < datetime.date.today()):
    loan.write({'state': 'late'})
  </field>
</record>

docs.title: Code context
docs.text:
Python in a server action runs in a restricted evaluator with: env, model, record (single, when called on one), records (the selection), uid, user, time, datetime, dateutil, timezone, float_compare, log(message, level), UserError, Warning, and _logger style helpers. To return a next step, assign an action variable:

action = {"type": "ir.actions.act_window", "res_model": "library.loan", "view_mode": "list"}

No imports and no attribute names starting with underscore. Anything non-trivial belongs in a model method that the action calls: records.action_mark_late(). Method code is versioned, testable, and reviewable; the code field is data in a database.

docs.title: Triggers for automation
docs.text:
base.automation (module base_automation) fields:

  • model_id, trigger: on_create, on_write, on_create_or_write, on_unlink, on_change, on_time, on_time_created, on_time_updated, on_state_set, on_user_set, on_tag_set, on_priority_set, on_archive, on_unarchive, on_message_received, on_message_sent, on_webhook, on_stage_set depending on the fields the model has.
