  • trigger_field_ids: for write triggers, fire only if one of these fields changed.
  • filter_pre_domain (Before Update Domain) and filter_domain (Apply on): the record must match the first before the change and the second after. Together they detect transitions.
  • action_server_ids: the server actions to run, in order.
  • on_time triggers use trg_date_id (a date field), trg_date_range and trg_date_range_type, run by a cron.
<record id="automation_late_loan" model="base.automation">
  <field name="name">Library: flag late loans</field>
  <field name="model_id" ref="model_library_loan"/>
  <field name="trigger">on_time</field>
  <field name="trg_date_id" ref="field_library_loan__due_date"/>
  <field name="trg_date_range">1</field>
  <field name="trg_date_range_type">day</field>
  <field name="filter_domain">[('state', '=', 'out')]</field>
  <field name="action_server_ids" eval="[(4, ref('action_loan_mark_late'))]"/>
</record>

docs.title: Execution behaviour
docs.text:
Write and create automations run synchronously inside the transaction of the triggering call, after the ORM operation. An exception in the action rolls back the user's save. Time-based rules run from a cron every few minutes and only evaluate records created or updated after the last run window, so adding one later does not back-fill history.

Automations triggered by their own writes can loop; the engine guards against direct recursion for the same rule, not through a chain of different rules.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Heavy code in an on_write automation on a hot model: every save pays for it, including imports and RPC.
  • Data in the database not in the repo: an automation created through the UI vanishes on a database rebuild and escapes code review. Ship the ones you depend on as XML.
  • Server action code indentation: a leading newline is fine, inconsistent indentation is not; use spaces.
  • Using record when the action is run on a list selection: it is empty; use records.
  • Testing on staging with real outgoing webhooks or mail: neutralize first.
  • binding_model_id makes the action visible to every user with access to the model unless you add groups_id.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: webhook as a server action type is new in 17/18 (the 18 source has it; check your version's selection). The automation trigger list was extended in 17 and 18 (tags, priorities, message events, on_webhook). In 16 trigger names are fewer and filter_pre_domain works the same way.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Read what is already defined on your model before adding anything:

select id, name->>'en_US', state from ir_act_server where model_id = (select id from ir_model where model = 'library.loan');

docs.title: View inheritance and XPath
docs.text: Every customisation of a standard screen is a view that inherits another view. Odoo never edits the parent record: at render time it takes the parent arch, applies each child's patch in order, and returns the merged result. Done well, your module survives upgrades of the module you extend. Done badly, it breaks on the first minor release that moves a <group>.

docs.title: The minimal inheritance record
docs.text:
<record id="view_partner_form_library" model="ir.ui.view">
    <field name="name">res.partner.form.library</field>
    <field name="model">res.partner</field>
    <field name="inherit_id" ref="base.view_partner_form"/>
    <field name="arch" type="xml">
        <xpath expr="//field[@name='vat']" position="after">
            <field name="library_card_number"/>
        </xpath>
    </field>
</record>

inherit_id takes an external ID, with the module prefix when it is not your own. The parent must be loaded before the child, so the module that owns it has to be in depends. The name field is only a label; make it unique and descriptive because it is what you will search for in Settings > Technical > Views.

docs.title: The shorthand form
docs.text:
When the target is a single element you can skip xpath and write the element itself. Odoo builds the expression from the tag and its attributes:

<field name="vat" position="after">
    <field name="library_card_number"/>
</field>

This is equivalent to //field[@name='vat']. It only works with a unique match on name; anything more specific needs an explicit xpath.

docs.title: Positions
docs.text: position effect after insert the content as next sibling before insert the content as previous sibling inside append to the end of the matched element (default) replace replace the matched element; with an empty body, delete it attributes change attributes of the matched element, content is <attribute name="..."> move inside an xpath child, relocate a matched node (see below)

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
<xpath expr="//field[@name='vat']" position="attributes">
    <attribute name="invisible">not is_company</attribute>
    <attribute name="string">Registration number</attribute>
</xpath>

Setting an attribute overwrites the parent's value. To append to an existing expression, use add and separator:

<attribute name="class" add="text-muted" separator=" "/>
<attribute name="invisible" add="state == 'cancel'" separator=" or "/>

remove does the opposite for token lists such as class.

docs.title: Moving nodes
docs.text:
<xpath expr="//field[@name='ref']" position="after">
    <xpath expr="//field[@name='vat']" position="move"/>
</xpath>

The inner xpath with position="move" takes the node out of its old place and puts it where the outer one points. Use it instead of deleting and re-declaring a field, because it keeps the field's own attributes and children.

docs.title: Replace with $0
docs.text:
In replace, the string $0 inside the new content stands for the original node. It lets you wrap an element without copying it:

<xpath expr="//field[@name='vat']" position="replace">
    <div class="o_row">$0</div>
</xpath>

docs.title: Writing selectors that survive
docs.text:
Selectors are XPath 1.0 over the parent arch. In order of robustness:

  1. //field[@name='x']: a field name is part of the model contract.
  2. //group[@name='sale_info'] or //page[@name='...']: named containers. Odoo core sets name on most structural nodes on purpose.
  3. //button[@name='action_confirm']: button method names.
  4. Position-based: //group[2], //sheet/div[1]. Avoid. They break when someone inserts an element above.

Anchor on the element nearest to where you want the change, not on the form root. //field[@name='partner_id']/.. is a legitimate way to reach the enclosing group.

docs.title: Duplicate fields
docs.text: A form may show the same field twice (once visible, once invisible="1" for computing a domain). //field[@name='partner_id'] then matches the first in document order. If that is the wrong one, qualify it: //group[@name='main']//field[@name='partner_id'], or use [@invisible] / [not(@invisible)].

docs.title: Mode: extension versus primary
docs.text:
<field name="mode">primary</field>

The default mode is extension: your patch is applied on top of the parent every time the parent is rendered. With primary, the child is an independent view that starts from a copy of the parent. Choose primary when an action needs its own form variant without touching the original, for example a read-only variant for a portal-like menu. Reference it with view_id on the action, or through ir.actions.act_window.view.

docs.title: Priorities and ordering
docs.text:
Children of one parent apply in ascending priority, then ascending id. The default is 16.

<field name="priority" eval="20"/>

Raise the priority when your patch depends on elements added by another child. A child that targets a node created by a sibling with a lower priority works; the reverse fails with a missing-node error at install. If two unrelated modules patch the same node, the later one wins, so a module that must always win declares a high priority rather than relying on install order.

docs.title: Inheriting views of other view types
docs.text:
The same mechanism works for list, kanban, search, calendar and QWeb views. For list views, use <list> as the parent element in new code:

<record id="view_partner_list_library" model="ir.ui.view">
    <field name="name">res.partner.list.library</field>
    <field name="model">res.partner</field>
    <field name="inherit_id" ref="base.view_partner_tree"/>
    <field name="arch" type="xml">
        <field name="email" position="after">
            <field name="library_card_number" optional="show"/>
        </field>
    </field>
</record>

The ID of the standard partner list is base.view_partner_tree even though the element inside is now <list>; Odoo did not rename external IDs. See the view ID catalogue.

docs.title: Groups on inherited elements
docs.text:
Restrict a patch to users of a group with the groups attribute on the inserted element, not on xpath:

<field name="library_card_number" position="after" groups="library.group_librarian">

An element with unmet groups is dropped from the arch server-side, so users never receive it. Keep this in mind for the next point.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
A parent that loses its anchor. If a later upgrade removes //field[@name='vat'], your view fails to load and the whole module update aborts with Element '<field name="vat">' cannot be located in parent view. Prefer anchors that core is unlikely to drop, and test module updates against the next minor release.

  • Group-restricted anchors. If the parent element you target has groups="..." and the user lacks the group, the element is already gone when your patch applies for them. Odoo applies patches on the unrestricted arch and then prunes, so this works in a normal run. It fails in custom contexts that pre-prune; keep anchors on ungrouped nodes where you can.
  • Copy-paste of the full arch. Replacing the whole <sheet> with your own copy freezes the form in the version you copied. Every upgrade then needs a manual merge.
  • position="replace" on a container with children others patch. Another module's child that targeted a node inside the replaced element now has no target. Prefer attributes or move.
  • Editing a view in the UI on production. It creates a ir.ui.view record with noupdate behaviour disconnected from the module source; the next module update will overwrite or fight it. Make the change in code.
  • Name collisions in XML IDs. Your child's ID must be unique in your module. Reusing view_partner_form inside a module that already defines one overwrites its own record, not the parent.

Versions. In Odoo 16 and earlier, hiding was done with attrs="{'invisible': [('state', '=', 'draft')]}" and states="draft". Odoo 17 replaced both with direct Python-style expressions: invisible="state == 'draft'". In Odoo 18 the old syntax is gone; a view using attrs fails validation. If you patch the attribute from an old module, rewrite the expression, you cannot add to a domain list.

Versions. Odoo 18 list views use <list>. The legacy <tree> tag was accepted as an alias for the list view type and is still read for compatibility, but new views should write <list>, and an xpath that targets //tree on a core 18 view will not match.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Inspect the merged result of a view and the chain of children, read-only, from odoo shell:

view = env.ref('base.view_partner_form')
print(len(view.inherit_children_ids), [c.name for c in view.inherit_children_ids])
merged = env['res.partner'].get_view(view.id, 'form')
print(merged['arch'][:2000])

get_view returns the arch after all inheritance and group pruning for the current user, which is what the web client actually receives.

docs.title: Wizards
docs.text: A wizard is a dialog that collects input and then does something to other records. Technically it is a TransientModel: a normal model whose rows are temporary and cleaned by a vacuum job. It gives you a real form, validation, and onchange without a permanent table of junk.

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
from odoo import api, fields, models
from odoo.exceptions import UserError


class LibraryLoanWizard(models.TransientModel):
    _name = "library.loan.wizard"
    _description = "Lend books"

    borrower_id = fields.Many2one("res.partner", required=True)
    book_ids = fields.Many2many("library.book", string="Books")
    due_date = fields.Date(default=lambda self: fields.Date.add(fields.Date.today(), days=14))

    @api.model
    def default_get(self, fields_list):
        res = super().default_get(fields_list)
        if self.env.context.get("active_model") == "library.book":
            res["book_ids"] = [(6, 0, self.env.context.get("active_ids", []))]
        return res

    def action_confirm(self):
        self.ensure_one()
        if not self.book_ids:
            raise UserError("Select at least one book.")
        loans = self.env["library.loan"].create([
            {"book_id": b.id, "borrower_id": self.borrower_id.id, "due_date": self.due_date}
            for b in self.book_ids
        ])
        return {
            "type": "ir.actions.act_window",
            "res_model": "library.loan",
            "view_mode": "list,form",
            "domain": [("id", "in", loans.ids)],
        }

<record id="library_loan_wizard_form" model="ir.ui.view">
  <field name="name">library.loan.wizard.form</field>
  <field name="model">library.loan.wizard</field>
  <field name="arch" type="xml">
    <form>
      <group>
        <field name="borrower_id"/>
        <field name="due_date"/>
        <field name="book_ids" widget="many2many_tags"/>
      </group>
      <footer>
        <button name="action_confirm" type="object" string="Confirm" class="btn-primary" data-hotkey="q"/>
        <button string="Cancel" special="cancel" data-hotkey="x"/>
      </footer>
    </form>
  </field>
</record>

<record id="library_loan_wizard_action" model="ir.actions.act_window">
  <field name="name">Lend books</field>
  <field name="res_model">library.loan.wizard</field>
  <field name="view_mode">form</field>
  <field name="target">new</field>
  <field name="binding_model_id" ref="model_library_book"/>
  <field name="binding_view_types">list,form</field>
</record>

docs.title: Moving parts
docs.text:
• target="new" opens the form in a dialog. The <footer> holds the buttons; buttons outside it render inside the form body.
  • binding_model_id puts the wizard in the Action menu of the books list and form. The selected records arrive as active_ids and active_model in the context.
  • default_get seeds fields from the context. Alternatively pass default_<field> keys in the action context.
  • Buttons call methods on the wizard record. self is the wizard; the target records are in self.book_ids or self.env[...].browse(self.env.context["active_ids"]).
  • A method can return an action dict to navigate, or {"type": "ir.actions.act_window_close"} to close the dialog, or a notification:
return {"type": "ir.actions.client", "tag": "display_notification",
        "params": {"title": "Done", "message": "3 loans created", "type": "success", "next": {"type": "ir.actions.act_window_close"}}}

docs.title: Opening a wizard from a button
docs.text:
def action_lend(self):
    return {
        "type": "ir.actions.act_window",
        "res_model": "library.loan.wizard",
        "view_mode": "form",
        "target": "new",
        "context": {"default_book_ids": self.ids},
    }

docs.title: Access and cleanup
docs.text: Transient models need no ir.model.access.csv entries since 14; any user can create and access their own wizard records, with a record rule that limits them to the creator. Rows are removed by an autovacuum (ir.autovacuum calls _transient_vacuum), by default after a few hours or when the number of rows exceeds a limit, so never store anything you need to keep.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Using self.env.context["active_ids"] after the wizard has already moved on: the context is lost once you return another action; pass ids explicitly.
  • Many2one fields pointing to a transient model from a persistent model: records disappear and leave a broken reference (the database refuses it by a constraint, or it errors on vacuum).
  • Long processing inside the button: the dialog freezes and the request may time out. Queue the work in a cron or a job and tell the user.
  • Forgetting ensure_one() when the button was triggered on several wizard records.
  • Returning nothing from a button leaves the dialog open on some versions; return the close action explicitly.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: The ir.actions.act_window dialog and footer mechanics are the same in 16, 17 and 18. The visible difference is in view XML: attrs and states on wizard fields and buttons were removed in 17; write invisible="not book_ids" instead of attrs="{'invisible': [...]}".

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Select two books in the list, open Action, and run "Lend books". Check the created loans, then look at the leftovers:

select id, create_date from library_loan_wizard order by id desc limit 5;

docs.title: Assets and bundles
docs.text:
Front-end files are not loaded because they exist. They are loaded because a manifest assets key (or an ir.asset record) lists them in a bundle. Forget this and your code is silently absent: no error, no warning, just nothing happening.

Checked against the Odoo 18 source (odoo/addons/base/models/ir_asset.py, assetsbundle.py, addons/web/__manifest__.py) and the Odoo 20 tree. Differences are in the Versions section.

docs.title: Declaring assets
docs.text:
# library/__manifest__.py
{
    "name": "Library",
    "version": "18.0.1.0.0",
    "depends": ["web"],
    "assets": {
        "web.assets_backend": [
            "library/static/src/**/*",
            ("remove", "library/static/src/**/*.test.js"),
        ],
        "web.assets_frontend": [
            "library/static/src/website/**/*",
        ],
        "web.assets_tests": [
            "library/static/tests/tours/**/*",
        ],
    },
}

An entry is either a string (a path or glob, appended to the bundle) or a tuple (directive, ...). A path starts with the addon name, not with a slash: library/static/src/js/foo.js. The path must point inside the static folder of an installed addon, which is why a typo gives no error beyond a log warning.

File types the bundler accepts: js, css, scss, sass, less and xml (templates). Anything else matching a glob is skipped. This is why static/src/img/*.png never needs listing: images are served directly by URL and are not part of a bundle.

docs.title: What a bundle is made of
docs.text:
A bundle is a list of files assembled in a fixed order, then compiled into one .js and one .css file stored as attachments. The assembly order, from IrAsset._fill_asset_paths:

  1. ir.asset database records for the bundle whose sequence is below 16, in sequence order.
  2. The assets entries of every installed addon's manifest, addon by addon in dependency order (topologically sorted), and entry by entry inside each manifest.
  3. The remaining ir.asset records (sequence 16 and above).

So a module you write after web always sees the bundle as web left it, and can insert before, after, replace or remove a file of web. An addon that does not depend (directly or indirectly) on the one it patches may be processed before it, and its before/after/replace finds nothing.

('include', 'other.bundle') splices the whole other bundle at that point, and circular includes raise "Circular assets bundle declaration".

Globs expand alphabetically inside one entry. ** is recursive. Order inside a glob matters only for SCSS (variables, mixins) and for non-module scripts; ES modules are ordered by their imports, not by file position.

docs.title: Directives
docs.text:
"web.assets_backend": [
    "library/static/src/js/new_file.js",                                    # append (default)
    ("prepend", "library/static/src/scss/early.scss"),                      # start of this bundle
    ("before", "web/static/src/core/foo.js", "library/static/src/js/a.js"), # before the target
    ("after",  "web/static/src/core/foo.js", "library/static/src/js/b.js"), # after the target
    ("replace","web/static/src/core/foo.js", "library/static/src/js/foo.js"),
    ("remove", "web/static/src/core/foo.js"),
    ("include", "web._assets_helpers"),
]

Note the argument order of before, after and replace: target first, new file second. The ir.asset model uses the same logic with separate target and path fields.

Semantics worth knowing:

  • prepend inserts at the beginning of the current bundle as the bundle is being assembled, not at the very top of the final list. If another addon later prepends, its file ends up in front of yours.
  • before/after/replace/remove accept globs as the new path, and remove accepts a glob as its path. The target of before/after/replace must resolve to one existing file in the bundle at that moment; otherwise assembly raises ValueError: File(s) <path> not found in bundle <bundle>.
  • If the target's extension is not an asset extension, the directive is silently ignored.
  • replace and remove break when the target is renamed in a later version. For JavaScript, prefer a registry entry or patch(); for templates, t-inherit.
  • remove applies to files already in the bundle. Removing something a later addon adds does nothing.

docs.title: External files
docs.text:
A path with a scheme or a host is passed through untouched, not aggregated into the bundle:

"web.assets_frontend": [
    "https://cdn.example.com/lib/chart.min.js",
],

External assets add a render-blocking request and a runtime dependency on a third party. For anything that must keep working offline (the reason this book exists) vendor the file under static/lib/ and list it as a normal path.

docs.title: Bundles that matter
docs.text:
From addons/web/__manifest__.py (18):

Bundle Purpose web.assets_backend the internal web client: core, views, fields, services of every installed app web.assets_backend_lazy graph and pivot views and other heavy parts, loaded on demand web.assets_web entry bundle of the backend: includes web.assets_backend, then main.js and start.js web.assets_frontend website, portal, e-commerce, public pages web.assets_frontend_lazy lazily loaded public code web.report_assets_common, web.report_assets_pdf what wkhtmltopdf loads when rendering reports web.assets_tests tours; loaded only when tests are enabled web.assets_unit_tests, web.assets_unit_tests_setup hoot unit tests and their runner web.assets_web_dark, web.assets_backend_lazy_dark dark mode variants of the above web._assets_primary_variables, web._assets_secondary_variables SCSS variable layers, see below web._assets_helpers, web._assets_backend_helpers, web._assets_frontend_helpers mixins and functions shared by SCSS files web._assets_core module loader, OWL, luxon and everything under core/

Where a file goes decides who sees it. Code for logged-in staff goes into web.assets_backend. Code for the public website goes into web.assets_frontend. A report stylesheet goes into web.report_assets_common. Putting a backend file in the frontend bundle fails with missing dependencies: @web/views/... does not exist there.

docs.title: SCSS, variables and themes
docs.text:
Stylesheets in a bundle are compiled to one CSS file with the SCSS compiler. Two bundles are included first in every compilation: the helpers (functions and mixins, web._assets_helpers) and the variables, so your file can use Bootstrap variables and the Odoo palette without importing them.

To change a variable you do not write a new rule. You add a file to the variables bundle, which is processed before everything else:

"web._assets_primary_variables": [
    "library/static/src/scss/primary_variables.scss",
],

// library/static/src/scss/primary_variables.scss
$o-library-accent: #5b7fa6 !default;

mail and portal do exactly this (mail/static/src/**/primary_variables.scss, portal/static/src/scss/primary_variables.scss). The core bundle also picks up any file named *.variables.scss under web/static/src. Use !default so another module can still override your value.

Variants by file suffix:

  • Files ending in .dark.scss are excluded from the normal backend bundle (('remove', 'web/static/src/**/*.dark.scss')) and included in the dark bundles. Put dark mode overrides there.
  • RTL stylesheets are generated automatically by flipping the compiled CSS. You do not write them. Use logical properties (margin-inline-start) and avoid hand-rolled direction hacks.

In templates and JavaScript, use Bootstrap utility classes instead of new CSS wherever you can. Every selector you add is a global selector. Prefix your own: .o_library_book_list.

docs.title: Loading code on demand
docs.text:
Some code is only needed on one screen. Put it in a separate bundle and load it when needed. The web client offers helpers in @web/core/assets:

import { loadBundle, loadJS, loadCSS } from "@web/core/assets";

await loadBundle("library.assets_chart");              // js and css of a bundle
await loadJS("/library/static/lib/chart/chart.min.js"); // one script
await loadCSS("/library/static/src/scss/print.css");    // one stylesheet

loadBundle calls /web/bundle/<name> to get the list of files and loads them. Results are cached: a second call returns the same promise. A failed load is retried, with a delay.

Define the bundle in the manifest under your own name. Keep it to two dot-separated parts, addon.name, like every core bundle:

"assets": {
    "library.assets_chart": [
        "library/static/lib/chart/chart.min.js",
        "library/static/src/chart/**/*",
    ],
},

For a whole component, LazyComponent loads a bundle and then looks the class up in the lazy_components registry:

<LazyComponent bundle="'library.assets_chart'" Component="'library.Chart'" props="chartProps"/>

registry.category("lazy_components").add("library.Chart", Chart);

The core uses the same pattern for heavy things: the graph and pivot views sit in web.assets_backend_lazy.

A library that is not an ES module (a UMD build such as chart.js) attaches itself to window. Load it with loadJS before use and read it from window, for example window.Chart. Do not list it in web.assets_backend: it loads on every page for every user.

docs.title: Data-driven assets: ir.asset
docs.text:
The same directives exist as database records, which is useful for hotfixes on a database you cannot redeploy, for per-website assets, and for toggling a file on and off without changing code. The model ir.asset has the fields name, bundle, directive, path, target, active and sequence (default 16).

<record id="library_hide_old_banner" model="ir.asset">
    <field name="name">Remove old banner script</field>
    <field name="bundle">web.assets_frontend</field>
    <field name="directive">remove</field>
    <field name="path">library/static/src/website/old_banner.js</field>
</record>

Creating or writing an ir.asset clears the assets cache. Records with a sequence below 16 are applied before manifests, the rest after. Prefer the manifest for anything that ships with your module; ir.asset is for runtime control.

docs.title: Caching, regeneration and debugging
docs.text:
Compilation is expensive, so the result is stored as attachments with the version hash in the URL (/web/assets/<hash>/web.assets_web.min.js). In normal mode:

  • The bundle is generated once per cache key (bundle plus parameters such as website) and then reused until the cache is cleared or the hash changes.
  • Changing a source file does not change the bundle. You are still running the old compiled copy.
  • Installing or updating a module, or the "Regenerate Assets Bundles" entry of the debug menu, rebuilds it.

With ?debug=assets in the URL, Odoo serves files unminified and, when a source file changes, regenerates the bundle. The server-side comment in ir_qweb.py says it plainly: with debug=assets the assets are regenerated when a composing file has been modified, otherwise they are generated once and cached.

Server flags matter too:

# 18: dev features are all, reload, qweb, xml (there is no "assets" feature)
./odoo-bin -d dev --dev=reload,qweb,xml
  • xml stops the assets path list from being cached, so edits to the assets key and new files are picked up without a restart for the asset lookup. (It also reads views from source files instead of the database.)
  • reload restarts the server when Python files change.
  • qweb logs the compiled XML when a QWeb error occurs.

A common mistake is writing --dev=assets. That is not a server option in 18 or 20. The browser's ?debug=assets is what unminifies and regenerates bundles.

docs.title: Where bundles live
docs.text:
Compiled bundles are rows in ir_attachment whose URL starts with /web/assets/ (the URL format is /web/assets/<unique>/<filename>). When a bundle seems stale in a way ?debug=assets does not fix, look:

-- read-only
SELECT id, name, url, write_date
FROM ir_attachment
WHERE url LIKE '/web/assets/%'
ORDER BY write_date DESC
LIMIT 20;

To force a rebuild you can delete those rows. This is safe: they are regenerated on the next request. It is a data change on the database, so run the SELECT first, take a backup on production, and expect the next page load to be slow while bundles rebuild:

DELETE FROM ir_attachment WHERE url LIKE '/web/assets/%';

From an Odoo shell, delete the attachments and clear the assets cache with env.registry.clear_cache("assets"), or simply click "Regenerate Assets Bundles" in the debug menu. (ir.asset.create and write call clear_cache("assets") themselves.)

docs.title: The "my file is not loaded" procedure
docs.text:
Work through these in order. Each step cuts the problem in half.

  1. Is the module installed and updated? Manifests are read at registry load. Edit __manifest__.py, restart (or use --dev=reload), then -u library.
  2. Is the path valid? The path starts with the addon name. In the Odoo log look for IrAsset: the path "..." did not resolve to anything. A wrong glob logs exactly that line.
  3. Is it in the right bundle? Backend code in web.assets_backend, public code in web.assets_frontend.
  4. Is the extension supported? Only js, css, scss, sass, less, xml.
  5. Is the browser really loading the new bundle? Load the page with ?debug=assets, open the Sources tab and find library/static/src/.... If it is there, the problem is in your code, not in the bundle.
  6. Did the module throw while loading? Open the console. Look for "The following modules failed to load because of an error" and inspect odoo.loader.failed and odoo.loader.jobs. A missing dependency puts a module in jobs forever.
  7. Is the template in the bundle? A component whose XML was never listed fails at mount with a missing template error, not at load time.
  8. Was another addon's remove or replace applied after yours? Print what the server resolved:
# Odoo shell
paths = env["ir.asset"]._get_asset_paths("web.assets_backend", {})
for path, addon, bundle in paths:
    if addon == "library":
        print(path)

_get_asset_paths(bundle, assets_params) returns tuples of (path, addon, bundle). The signature is the one in 18; assets_params is {} unless a module such as website overrides _get_asset_params.

docs.title: A realistic manifest
docs.text:
A module with a backend UI, a public page, a lazily loaded chart library, tour tests, unit tests and a report stylesheet:

"assets": {
    "web._assets_primary_variables": [
        "library/static/src/scss/primary_variables.scss",
    ],
    "web.assets_backend": [
        "library/static/src/backend/**/*",
        ("remove", "library/static/src/backend/**/*.test.js"),
    ],
    "web.assets_frontend": [
        "library/static/src/public/**/*",
    ],
    "library.assets_chart": [
        "library/static/lib/chart/chart.min.js",
        "library/static/src/chart/**/*",
    ],
    "web.report_assets_common": [
        "library/static/src/report/report.scss",
    ],
    "web.assets_tests": [
        "library/static/tests/tours/**/*",
    ],
    "web.assets_unit_tests": [
        "library/static/src/**/*.test.js",
    ],
},

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A file under static/src that matches no glob is never served, and nothing reports it. Search the Sources tab, not the file system.
  • A backend file in web.assets_frontend fails with missing dependencies. A frontend file in the backend runs on every page for every employee.
  • ("before", new, target) with the arguments swapped. The target is the second element.
  • A target that is not in the bundle yet. Your addon is processed before the addon that adds the target, usually a missing depends.
  • Importing a module from a bundle not loaded on that page fails at load time and lists your module in odoo.loader.jobs.
  • Changing the manifest without restarting the server. The assets key is read when the registry loads.
  • Vendoring a library into web.assets_backend and shipping megabytes to every user. Make it a lazy bundle.
  • SCSS that relies on file order. Put variables in the variable bundle, mixins in helpers, and rules in the normal bundle.
  • --dev=assets. It does nothing. Use ?debug=assets in the browser.
  • A bundle name with three parts (library.assets.chart). The compiled-bundle URL parser (_parse_bundle_name) requires exactly two dot-separated parts, so keep your own bundle names to addon.name.
  • Deleting attachments to fix a bundle and forgetting the cache. After a database edit, restart or clear the registry caches too.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
16: no web.assets_web bundle; the client loads web.assets_backend directly. Templates are listed in the same assets key as JavaScript (there is no separate qweb key). The @odoo-module header is required.

17: web.assets_web exists and includes web.assets_backend.

18: the lazy bundles and dark variants shown above exist. The server accepts --dev=all,reload,qweb,xml (all stands for reload,qweb,xml).

20: --dev accepts access, qweb, reload, replica and xml, and all expands to access,qweb,reload,xml. The bundle list adds icon font bundles (web.material_symbols_*, web.odoo_ui_icons, web.icons_fonts) and drops the jQuery helper bundle web._assets_jquery that 18 has. The directives and the assembly order are the same as in 18.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
1. Create a file library/static/src/hello.js that logs a line, list it in web.assets_backend, update the module, and find it in the Sources tab with ?debug=assets.
  2. Mistype the path on purpose and find the warning in the server log.
  3. Add ("before", "web/static/src/main.js", "library/static/src/early.js") and check, with the Odoo shell snippet above, where your file landed.
  4. Run the read-only SQL on ir_attachment and note how many compiled bundles exist.
Solution notes
  1. The path in the Sources tab is library/static/src/hello.js. In a normal (non-debug) page you would see only the minified bundle.
  2. The log line is IrAsset: the path "library/static/src/helo.js" did not resolve to anything., at WARNING level.
  3. Printing _get_asset_paths("web.assets_web", {}) shows your file immediately before web/static/src/main.js. Use web.assets_web, since main.js belongs to that bundle and not to web.assets_backend.
  4. One .js and one .css per bundle and per language direction, plus lazy and report bundles.

docs.title: Custom field widgets
docs.text:
A field widget is an OWL component that displays and edits one field of a record, registered in the fields registry and selected from a view with widget="name". A view widget is the same idea without a field behind it, registered in view_widgets and placed with <widget name="..."/>.

All behaviour was read from the Odoo 18 source (addons/web/static/src/views/fields, views/widgets, model/relational_model).

docs.title: How a widget is found
docs.text:
When a form, list or kanban arch is parsed, each <field> node goes through Field.parseFieldNode. The resolution of the widget class is getFieldFromRegistry(fieldType, widget, viewType, jsClass):

  1. If the node has widget="foo", look for foo in the fields registry, trying these keys in order: <jsClass>.foo (only if the view has a js_class), <viewType>.foo (for example list.foo, form.foo, kanban.foo), then plain foo. The first that exists wins. If none exists you get a console warning Missing widget: foo for field of type char and a fallback.
  2. Otherwise look up the field's type the same way (char, many2one, ...), falling back to a generic DefaultField.

This lookup order is the reason the core registers many2one and list.many2one separately, and it gives you a clean way to ship one widget with a different implementation for lists: register library_isbn and list.library_isbn.

The parser also collects, per field node: options (the dictionary from the options="{...}" attribute, evaluated), attrs (every other non-dynamic attribute such as placeholder, password), context, domain, string, help, decoration-*, and the invisible, readonly, required, column_invisible expressions. Your widget never parses arch. It receives these through extractProps.

docs.title: The anatomy of a widget
docs.text:
Two objects: the component and the definition.

import { registry } from "@web/core/registry";
import { standardFieldProps } from "@web/views/fields/standard_field_props";

export class MyField extends Component {
    static template = "library.MyField";
    static props = {
        ...standardFieldProps,       // id, name, readonly, record
        strict: { type: Boolean, optional: true },
    };
}

export const myField = {
    component: MyField,
    displayName: "My field",                  // label in the Studio-like editors
    supportedTypes: ["char"],                 // field types it can be used on
    supportedOptions: [ ... ],                // documented options (optional)
    extractProps(fieldInfo, dynamicInfo) {    // arch -> component props
        return { strict: Boolean(fieldInfo.options.strict) };
    },
};

registry.category("fields").add("my_field", myField);

The keys of the definition, from the registry validation schema in field.js:

Key Purpose component the OWL component class (mandatory) displayName human-readable name supportedTypes field types the widget works on supportedOptions, supportedAttributes descriptions of options/attributes, used by editors; each is { label, name, type, default?, help?, choices? } extractProps(fieldInfo, dynamicInfo) turns arch information into extra props isEmpty(record, fieldName) custom emptiness for the "empty field" styling isValid(record, fieldName, fieldInfo) replaces the validity test used for the red outline (visual only, does not block saving) fieldDependencies extra fields the widget needs loaded (array, or function of the field node) relatedFields, useSubView for x2many-like widgets that need subview fields additionalClasses CSS classes added to the field wrapper listViewWidth default column width in lists (number, [min, max], or function) label set false to suppress the label

fieldInfo is the parsed node: { name, type, widget, options, attrs, string, context, decorations, ... }. dynamicInfo holds what depends on the current record: readonly, required, context, and a domain() function. Always take readonly from dynamicInfo when you need it in props: the final readonly state of the widget is readonly || !record.isInEdition, which Field computes for you.

docs.title: What your component receives
docs.text:
In props:

  • record: the record datapoint.
  • name: the field name. Never hard-code it; the same widget serves many fields.
  • readonly: true when the widget must not edit. It already accounts for view readonly attributes and for the record not being in edition.
  • id: the DOM id to put on your input so the label focuses it.
  • plus whatever extractProps returned.

On record you will use:

Member Meaning record.data[name] the current value (formats below) record.fields[name] field metadata from the server: type, string, size, trim, translate, required, selection, relation, ... record.update(changes, { save }) change one or more fields; save: true writes to the database immediately record.isInEdition whether the record is editable right now record.isNew, record.resId, record.resModel identity record.setInvalidField(name) mark the field invalid (red) record.isFieldInvalid(name) read it back record.model.bus event bus of the model

Value formats in record.data:

Field type JavaScript value char, text, html string (false when empty for some types, normalise with || "") integer, float, monetary number boolean boolean date, datetime luxon.DateTime, or false when empty selection the key string, or false many2one [id, display_name] pair, or false one2many, many2many a static list object (not an array of ids)

Write with the same shapes. To set a many2one pass [id, display_name] or false; incomplete pairs are completed from the server. Never mutate record.data directly: record.update runs onchange, dirty tracking and validation.

docs.title: Reading luxon dates
docs.text:
luxon is a global in the web client:

const { DateTime } = luxon;
const due = this.props.record.data.due_date;      // DateTime or false
const days = due ? Math.floor(DateTime.now().startOf("day").diff(due.startOf("day"), "days").days) : 0;

docs.title: Example 1: an editable ISBN field
docs.text:
Requirement: a char field that accepts ISBN-10 or ISBN-13 with or without hyphens, rejects invalid check digits (red outline, record cannot be saved), and stores the digits only.

The validation logic is a plain module, so it can be tested alone. library/static/src/fields/isbn.js:

/** @odoo-module **/

export function normalizeIsbn(raw) {
    return (raw || "").replace(/[\s-]/g, "").toUpperCase();
}

export function isValidIsbn(raw) {
    const s = normalizeIsbn(raw);
    if (/^\d{9}[\dX]$/.test(s)) {
        let sum = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
            sum += (s[i] === "X" ? 10 : Number(s[i])) * (10 - i);
        }
        return sum % 11 === 0;
    }
    if (/^\d{13}$/.test(s)) {
        let sum = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 13; i++) {
            sum += Number(s[i]) * (i % 2 ? 3 : 1);
        }
        return sum % 10 === 0;
    }
    return false;
}

export function formatIsbn(raw) {
    const s = normalizeIsbn(raw);
    if (s.length === 13) {
        return `${s.slice(0, 3)}-${s.slice(3, 4)}-${s.slice(4, 9)}-${s.slice(9, 12)}-${s.slice(12)}`;
    }
    return s;
}

The three functions were run against known values: 9780306406157, 0-306-40615-2 and 080442957X are valid; the same numbers with a changed last digit, abc and the empty string are not; formatIsbn("9780306406157") returns 978-0-30640-615-7.

The component, library/static/src/fields/isbn_field.js:

/** @odoo-module **/
import { Component } from "@odoo/owl";
import { registry } from "@web/core/registry";
import { _t } from "@web/core/l10n/translation";
import { standardFieldProps } from "@web/views/fields/standard_field_props";
import { useInputField } from "@web/views/fields/input_field_hook";
import { formatIsbn, isValidIsbn, normalizeIsbn } from "./isbn";

export class IsbnField extends Component {
    static template = "library.IsbnField";
    static props = {
        ...standardFieldProps,
        placeholder: { type: String, optional: true },
    };

    setup() {
        useInputField({
            getValue: () => formatIsbn(this.props.record.data[this.props.name]),
            parse: (value) => this.parse(value),
        });
    }

    get formattedValue() {
        return formatIsbn(this.props.record.data[this.props.name]);
    }

    parse(value) {
        if (!value.trim()) {
            return false;
        }
        if (!isValidIsbn(value)) {
            throw new Error("Invalid ISBN");   // marks the field invalid
        }
        return normalizeIsbn(value);
    }
}

export const isbnField = {
    component: IsbnField,
    displayName: _t("ISBN"),
    supportedTypes: ["char"],
    extractProps: ({ attrs }) => ({
        placeholder: attrs.placeholder,
    }),
    isEmpty: (record, fieldName) => !record.data[fieldName],
};

registry.category("fields").add("library_isbn", isbnField);

library/static/src/fields/isbn_field.xml:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<templates xml:space="preserve">
    <t t-name="library.IsbnField">
        <t t-if="props.readonly">
            <span class="o_library_isbn font-monospace" t-out="formattedValue"/>
        </t>
        <t t-else="">
            <input class="o_input font-monospace" type="text"
                   t-att-id="props.id"
                   t-att-placeholder="props.placeholder"
                   t-ref="input"/>
        </t>
    </t>
</templates>

Use it in a view:

<field name="isbn" widget="library_isbn" placeholder="978-0-..."/>

What each piece does:

  • useInputField is the hook the core uses for text inputs. It looks for a t-ref="input" element, writes getValue() into it unless the user is typing or the field is invalid, listens to input, change and keydown, and on commit calls parse and then record.update. It also protects what the user is typing from being overwritten by an onchange that arrives meanwhile. That is why you do not write your own t-on-change.
  • parse throws to say "this text is invalid". The hook catches it and calls record.setInvalidField(name), which gives the red outline and blocks saving with the usual "Invalid fields" message. Return the value to store otherwise. Returning false empties a char field.
  • getValue formats for display; the stored value is the normalised digits. The same value goes through formatIsbn in readonly mode, which is the only place where display and storage differ.
  • isEmpty makes an empty field show the usual "empty" styling in readonly forms.

On the server, enforce the same rule, because the widget is not security. A Python constraint using the same check digit rules belongs on library.book (@api.constrains("isbn")), see the constraints chapter.

docs.title: Example 2: a read-only "days overdue" widget using an extra field
docs.text:
A widget on the state field of library.loan that shows a badge and, for open loans, how many days past due_date they are. It needs due_date, a field that may not be in the view, so it declares it as a dependency.

/** @odoo-module **/
import { Component } from "@odoo/owl";
import { registry } from "@web/core/registry";
import { _t } from "@web/core/l10n/translation";
import { standardFieldProps } from "@web/views/fields/standard_field_props";

const { DateTime } = luxon;

export class LoanStateField extends Component {
    static template = "library.LoanStateField";
    static props = { ...standardFieldProps };

    get state() {
        return this.props.record.data[this.props.name];
    }

    get daysOverdue() {
        const due = this.props.record.data.due_date;
        if (this.state !== "open" || !due) {
            return 0;
        }
        const days = DateTime.now().startOf("day").diff(due.startOf("day"), "days").days;
        return Math.max(0, Math.floor(days));
    }

    get badgeClass() {
        if (this.daysOverdue > 0) {
            return "text-bg-danger";
        }
        return { open: "text-bg-info", returned: "text-bg-success" }[this.state] || "text-bg-secondary";
    }

    get label() {
        const selection = this.props.record.fields[this.props.name].selection || [];
        const found = selection.find(([key]) => key === this.state);
        return found ? found[1] : "";
    }
}

export const loanStateField = {
    component: LoanStateField,
    displayName: _t("Loan state"),
    supportedTypes: ["selection"],
    fieldDependencies: [{ name: "due_date", type: "date" }],
};

registry.category("fields").add("library_loan_state", loanStateField);
// same widget in lists
registry.category("fields").add("list.library_loan_state", loanStateField);

<t t-name="library.LoanStateField">
    <span class="badge rounded-pill" t-att-class="badgeClass">
        <t t-out="label"/>
        <t t-if="daysOverdue" t-out="' (' + daysOverdue + ' d late)'"/>
    </span>
</t>

<field name="state" widget="library_loan_state"/>

fieldDependencies makes the model request due_date along with the fields of the view, even if the view does not show it. Without it record.data.due_date is undefined when the arch lacks the field. For the dependency to be useful the field must exist on the model; if it does not, loading the view fails with an unknown field error that names it.

Since the widget has no input, it works unchanged in readonly and edit mode. Add readonly handling only if you add editing.

docs.title: Example 3: a view widget
docs.text:
A view widget is not tied to a field. It is useful for banners, buttons and ribbons placed in a form. It gets record and readonly (standardWidgetProps) and extractProps receives the node's attributes.

/** @odoo-module **/
import { Component } from "@odoo/owl";
import { registry } from "@web/core/registry";
import { standardWidgetProps } from "@web/views/widgets/standard_widget_props";

export class OverdueBanner extends Component {
    static template = "library.OverdueBanner";
    static props = { ...standardWidgetProps, text: { type: String, optional: true } };

    get overdue() {
        const { state, due_date } = this.props.record.data;
        return state === "open" && due_date && due_date < luxon.DateTime.now();
    }
}

export const overdueBanner = {
    component: OverdueBanner,
    fieldDependencies: [
        { name: "state", type: "selection" },
        { name: "due_date", type: "date" },
    ],
    extractProps: ({ attrs }) => ({ text: attrs.text }),
};

registry.category("view_widgets").add("library_overdue_banner", overdueBanner);

<t t-name="library.OverdueBanner">
    <div t-if="overdue" class="alert alert-danger mb-0" role="alert">
        <t t-out="props.text or 'This loan is overdue.'"/>
    </div>
</t>

<widget name="library_overdue_banner" text="Return reminder sent after 14 days"/>

The core ribbon (web_ribbon) is the model to read: its extractProps maps the title, bg_color and tooltip attributes onto props, and it lists them in supportedAttributes.

docs.title: Extending an existing widget
docs.text:
If you want most of the behaviour of a core widget, subclass the component and spread the definition:

import { CharField, charField } from "@web/views/fields/char/char_field";

class UpperCharField extends CharField {
    parse(value) {
        return super.parse(value).toUpperCase();
    }
}

registry.category("fields").add("library_upper_char", {
    ...charField,
    component: UpperCharField,
    displayName: "Uppercase text",
});

The definition object is plain data, so spreading it carries over supportedTypes, extractProps and the rest. The template is inherited with the class: UpperCharField still uses web.CharField. Give it your own template (static template = "library.UpperCharField", with t-inherit="web.CharField" t-inherit-mode="primary") only if markup must change.

docs.title: Reacting to other fields
docs.text:
A widget can read any field that is loaded in the view or in fieldDependencies. It re-renders when record.data changes, including after an onchange. To change another field in response to an edit, call record.update with several keys at once:

await this.props.record.update({
    [this.props.name]: value,
    title_hint: computeHint(value),
});

One call produces one onchange round trip, whereas two calls produce two.

For autosaving widgets (toggles, ratings), pass { save: true }. The core toggle does it by default and exposes an autosave option:

await this.props.record.update({ [this.props.name]: newValue }, { save: this.props.autosave });

Autosave on a new, invalid or dirty record can surprise the user with a half-saved form, so make it optional as the core does.

docs.title: Formatting and parsing outside widgets
docs.text: Read-only display of values in lists, kanban and other places uses two registries, formatters and parsers, keyed by field type, plus helpers in @web/views/fields/formatters such as formatChar, formatInteger. You rarely need to touch them. When you need the same formatting in a widget and elsewhere, factor it into a plain function as the ISBN example does, then call it from both.

docs.title: Supported options and Studio
docs.text:
supportedOptions and supportedAttributes do not change runtime behaviour. They document what the widget accepts and let the view editors present controls. Provide them for widgets you hand to others:

supportedOptions: [
    {
        label: _t("Strict check digit"),
        name: "strict",
        type: "boolean",
        default: true,
        help: _t("Reject numbers whose check digit is wrong."),
    },
],

docs.title: Debugging a widget
docs.text:
• ?debug=1, hover a field label: the tooltip lists the widget (and its displayName) when the node has a widget attribute. If the entry is missing or shows the default, your key did not match.
  • Console warning Missing widget: library_isbn for field of type char: the registry key does not exist. Either the module with the registration is not in the bundle (see the assets chapter) or the key is misspelled.
  • Registry validation errors in debug mode (component, supportedTypes, extractProps types) appear when the module loads, with the key name.
  • Check what the widget receives: add console.log(this.props) in setup. extractProps is the place for missing props.
  • If the value does not update after typing, you probably wrote your own change handling instead of using useInputField, or you mutated record.data directly.

docs.title: Odoo 20 form of the same widget
docs.text:
OWL 3 changes how props and refs are declared (see the OWL 3 chapter). The field definition object, the registry, extractProps, fieldDependencies and useInputField stay. In the Odoo 20 source:

  • standardFieldProps is an object of OWL 3 types: { id: t.string().optional(), name: t.string(), readonly: t.boolean().optional(), record: t.object() }.
  • Components declare props = useProps({ ...standardFieldProps, placeholder: t.string().optional() }).
  • The input ref is input = signal.ref(), templates use t-ref="this.input", and the hook is called as useInputField({ ref: this.input, getValue, parse }).
  • Templates address members as this.props.readonly, this.formattedValue.
  • charField.supportedTypes is ["char", "text"] there.

A port of IsbnField therefore changes the props declaration, the ref, the template prefixes, and nothing in isbn.js or in the definition object.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
Widgets run in lists, forms, kanban and dialogs, with and without edit mode. Test each context you register for. A widget that assumes record.isInEdition crashes in a list cell.

  • Hard-coding the field name. Use this.props.name.
  • Mutating record.data. Use record.update, or onchange, dirty state and saving break.
  • Writing a many2one as a number. Use [id, display_name] or false.
  • Treating dates as strings. They are luxon DateTimes; compare with <, diff, toISODate().
  • Forgetting fieldDependencies. The extra field is undefined when the arch does not contain it.
  • Not throwing in parse for invalid input. Returning something odd stores it; throwing marks the field invalid.
  • Returning a value without trimming or normalising and then comparing in constraints. Normalise once, in parse.
  • Own change handlers instead of useInputField. An onchange response can overwrite what the user is typing.
  • Registering only fields and forgetting list rendering. If the list needs a different look, add list.<name>.
  • Keys without a prefix. isbn could clash with another module; use library_isbn.
  • Skipping the server check. A widget is a convenience, never validation.
  • Missing template in the bundle. The widget fails at mount; the template is a separate file in the same bundle.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
16: widgets are legacy classes (AbstractField subclasses registered in field_registry) or OWL components registered in the OWL field registry, depending on the field. The definition objects above are the 17+ model.

17 and 18: the OWL field registry model described here, with static props and useState.

20: same registry and definition keys, with OWL 3 props, refs and template prefixes.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
1. Add the ISBN field to library.book's form with widget="library_isbn". Type 9780306406158 and tab out. Then type 978-0-306-40615-7.
  2. Add isValid to the definition so a value that is non-empty but not a valid ISBN is outlined red, and check whether it also blocks saving.
  3. Register the same definition under list.library_isbn with a different component that renders only the formatted text.
  4. Build the loan state widget, then change due_date in the form and watch the badge update.
Solution notes
  1. The first value is rejected: the field turns red and saving shows the invalid fields message. The second is stored as 9780306406157 and displayed as 978-0-30640-615-7.
  2. isValid: (record, name) => !record.data[name] || isValidIsbn(record.data[name]) changes only the red outline: fieldVisualFeedback uses it instead of record.isFieldInvalid. It does not block saving, which is why the real check stays in parse (invalid field) and in the Python constraint.
  3. The lookup for a list cell tries list.library_isbn before library_isbn, so the list uses the second component and the form the first, with no change to the arch.
  4. daysOverdue is a getter reading record.data, so it recomputes after the onchange or edit that changes due_date.

docs.title: Customising views
docs.text:
Every list, form and kanban screen is assembled from a small set of replaceable parts: a controller, a renderer, a model, an arch parser, and a button template. They are bundled into a view definition stored in the views registry, and an individual view picks its definition with the js_class attribute. That is the supported way to change one screen without touching any other, and this chapter shows how it works and walks through four recipes: a list with an extra control panel button, a list that colours rows by a business rule, a form that confirms before a button runs, and a kanban card with extra classes.

Everything was read from the Odoo 18 source (addons/web/static/src/views).

docs.title: The view stack
docs.text:
When an action opens a view, the View component (views/view.js) does the following:

  1. Loads the arch and field metadata from the server.
  2. Reads the js_class attribute of the arch root, or falls back to the view type (list, form, kanban, ...). That string is the key looked up in the views registry.
  3. If the key is not in the registry it first loads the lazy bundle web.assets_backend_lazy (this is how the graph and pivot views load on demand) and then looks again.
  4. Calls the definition's props(genericProps, view) function to build the props for the controller. It parses the arch with ArchParser, and passes Model, Renderer, buttonTemplate and archInfo along.
  5. Renders Controller, which renders Renderer inside a Layout with the control panel.

So a definition is a plain object:

export const listView = {
    type: "list",
    Controller: ListController,
    Renderer: ListRenderer,
    ArchParser: ListArchParser,
    Model: RelationalModel,
    buttonTemplate: "web.ListView.Buttons",
    canOrderByCount: true,
    props: (genericProps, view) => { /* returns the controller props */ },
};
registry.category("views").add("list", listView);

Your override is the same object with some keys replaced:

registry.category("views").add("library_loan_list", {
    ...listView,
    Controller: LoanListController,
});

The spread copies props, which reads Renderer, Model and buttonTemplate from the view argument (the definition object itself), so replacing a key on your copy is enough: the standard props function passes it on. For the kanban view the core comments that it does not pass Compiler automatically "in stable, for backward compat"; if you replace Compiler on a kanban definition, read kanban_view.js and pass it yourself in a custom props.

Select the definition per view, on the root tag:

<record id="view_loan_list" model="ir.ui.view">
    <field name="name">library.loan.list</field>
    <field name="model">library.loan</field>
    <field name="arch" type="xml">
        <list js_class="library_loan_list">
            <field name="book_id"/>
            <field name="member_id"/>
            <field name="due_date"/>
            <field name="state"/>
        </list>
    </field>
</record>

Two points:

  • In Odoo 18 the list arch root tag is <list> and the view type is list. Earlier versions call it <tree>. A 17 arch must say <tree js_class="...">.
  • js_class is the registry key and has nothing to do with a file name. If the key is not registered, the view falls back to loading the lazy bundle and then raises "Cannot find key" in the views registry. Check the console.

Only views that carry the attribute change. Everything else keeps using the stock definition, which is the point.

docs.title: What each part does
docs.text:
Part Class (list) Customise it to Controller ListController add buttons and actions, hook into save, delete, open record, react to selection Renderer ListRenderer change how rows and cells look: classes, cell content, column headers Model RelationalModel change how data loads and saves (advanced) ArchParser ListArchParser read extra arch attributes into archInfo buttonTemplate web.ListView.Buttons change the buttons in the control panel Compiler (form, kanban) FormCompiler, KanbanCompiler change how arch XML becomes a template

The controller owns actions and the model; the renderer owns presentation. Put logic in the controller and keep the renderer to appearance.

docs.title: Recipe 1: an extra button in the list control panel
docs.text:
Goal: a "Overdue report" button next to the standard buttons of library.loan lists. Clicking it opens the loans list filtered to open, past-due loans.

Controller, library/static/src/loan_list/loan_list_controller.js:

/** @odoo-module **/
import { registry } from "@web/core/registry";
import { listView } from "@web/views/list/list_view";
import { ListController } from "@web/views/list/list_controller";
import { useService } from "@web/core/utils/hooks";

export class LoanListController extends ListController {
    setup() {
        super.setup(...arguments);
        this.libraryAction = useService("action");
    }

    onClickOverdue() {
        this.libraryAction.doAction({
            type: "ir.actions.act_window",
            name: "Overdue loans",
            res_model: "library.loan",
            views: [[false, "list"], [false, "form"]],
            domain: [["state", "=", "open"], ["due_date", "<", new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)]],
        });
    }
}

registry.category("views").add("library_loan_list", {
    ...listView,
    Controller: LoanListController,
    buttonTemplate: "library.LoanListView.Buttons",
});

Button template, library/static/src/loan_list/loan_list.xml. It extends the standard buttons template as a new, separate template:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<templates xml:space="preserve">
    <t t-name="library.LoanListView.Buttons" t-inherit="web.ListView.Buttons" t-inherit-mode="primary">
        <xpath expr="//div[hasclass('o_list_buttons')]" position="inside">
            <button t-if="!editedRecord" type="button" class="btn btn-secondary"
                    t-on-click="onClickOverdue">
                Overdue report
            </button>
        </xpath>
    </t>
</templates>

Why it is built this way:

  • t-inherit-mode="primary" creates the new template library.LoanListView.Buttons, leaving web.ListView.Buttons alone. Other lists keep the standard buttons. With extension you would modify the standard template for every list.
  • The buttons template is rendered with the controller as its context (t-call="{{ props.buttonTemplate }}" inside web.ListView), which is why editedRecord and onClickOverdue are visible by name.
  • The standard buttons template holds the Save and Discard buttons for inline editing, wrapped in a div with class o_list_buttons. Adding inside that div keeps your button in the same toolbar.
  • The date comparison uses toISOString().slice(0, 10), which is UTC. For a domain on a date field that is fine for a report, but in a timezone far from UTC close to midnight it can be a day off. For exact "today", compute it server-side with a filter in the search view (<filter name="overdue" domain="[('due_date', '<', context_today().strftime('%Y-%m-%d'))]"/>).

If the button should act on selected rows, read them from the model: this.model.root.selection is the list of selected records in 18 (the core builds its active ids from it with this.model.root.selection.map((r) => r.resId)).

docs.title: Recipe 2: colouring rows by a business rule
docs.text:
Decorations in the arch are the first tool and need no JavaScript:

<list decoration-danger="state == 'open' and overdue" decoration-muted="state == 'returned'">

decoration-* attributes take a Python-like expression over the fields in the view. Use them whenever the rule is a condition on fields already in the list (overdue could be a stored or computed boolean field).

When the rule needs computation that a decoration expression cannot express (dates compared to now, several records), override getRowClass in a renderer. The base method collects decoration classes and adds selection classes, so call it first:

/** @odoo-module **/
import { registry } from "@web/core/registry";
import { listView } from "@web/views/list/list_view";
import { ListRenderer } from "@web/views/list/list_renderer";

const { DateTime } = luxon;

export class LoanListRenderer extends ListRenderer {
    getRowClass(record) {
        let classes = super.getRowClass(record);
        const due = record.data.due_date;
        if (record.data.state === "open" && due && due < DateTime.now().startOf("day")) {
            classes += " o_library_overdue";
        }
        return classes;
    }
}

registry.category("views").add("library_loan_list", {
    ...listView,
    Renderer: LoanListRenderer,
});

// library/static/src/loan_list/loan_list.scss
.o_list_renderer .o_data_row.o_library_overdue {
    --table-bg: var(--bs-danger-bg-subtle);
}

To combine recipes 1 and 2 in one view definition, put both keys in a single registration, since two registrations of library_loan_list would collide:

registry.category("views").add("library_loan_list", {
    ...listView,
    Controller: LoanListController,
    Renderer: LoanListRenderer,
    buttonTemplate: "library.LoanListView.Buttons",
});

record.data.due_date is available only when due_date is in the list. If you do not want the column visible, add it with column_invisible="1":

<field name="due_date" column_invisible="1"/>

Other renderer methods worth knowing in 18: getCellClass(column, record), getCellTitle(column, record), getColumnClass(column), isSortable(column), canUseFormatter(column, record). Prefer overriding one of these small methods rather than copying a large template.

docs.title: Recipe 3: a form that confirms a button
docs.text:
Form buttons of type="object" or type="action" go through beforeExecuteActionButton(clickParams) in the controller. It saves the record first by default and returns whether it succeeded; returning false cancels the click. Wrap it to ask first:

/** @odoo-module **/
import { registry } from "@web/core/registry";
import { formView } from "@web/views/form/form_view";
import { FormController } from "@web/views/form/form_controller";
import { ConfirmationDialog } from "@web/core/confirmation_dialog/confirmation_dialog";
import { useService } from "@web/core/utils/hooks";

export class LoanFormController extends FormController {
    setup() {
        super.setup(...arguments);
        this.libraryNotification = useService("notification");
    }

    async beforeExecuteActionButton(clickParams) {
        if (clickParams.name === "action_return") {
            const confirmed = await new Promise((resolve) => {
                this.dialogService.add(ConfirmationDialog, {
                    title: "Return this loan?",
                    body: "The book will be marked as available.",
                    confirm: () => resolve(true),
                    cancel: () => resolve(false),
                    dismiss: () => resolve(false),
                });
            });
            if (!confirmed) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return super.beforeExecuteActionButton(...arguments);
    }

    async onWillSaveRecord(record) {
        if (!record.data.book_id) {
            this.libraryNotification.add("Pick a book before saving.", { type: "danger" });
            return false;   // cancels the save
        }
    }
}

registry.category("views").add("library_loan_form", {
    ...formView,
    Controller: LoanFormController,
});

<form js_class="library_loan_form">
    <header>
        <button name="action_return" type="object" string="Return" class="btn-primary"/>
    </header>
    ...
</form>

Notes:

  • this.dialogService exists on the form controller in 18 (the core uses it for the archive and delete confirmations). The controller has no notification property, so the example gets its own with useService("notification") in setup.
  • clickParams.name is the name attribute of the button, so one controller can treat several buttons differently.
  • The hook onWillSaveRecord is documented in the source: it runs "before the record save if the record is valid" and returning false prevents the save.
  • Remember that confirmation in JavaScript protects users, not data. If a rule must hold, enforce it with a constraint or a state check in the Python method.

docs.title: Recipe 4: a kanban card with extra classes
docs.text:
The kanban card is the KanbanRecord component. The renderer lists it in static components, so you replace it by overriding that list on a renderer subclass, and then register the renderer:

/** @odoo-module **/
import { registry } from "@web/core/registry";
import { kanbanView } from "@web/views/kanban/kanban_view";
import { KanbanRenderer } from "@web/views/kanban/kanban_renderer";
import { KanbanRecord } from "@web/views/kanban/kanban_record";

class LoanKanbanRecord extends KanbanRecord {
    getRecordClasses() {
        let classes = super.getRecordClasses();
        if (this.props.record.data.state === "open") {
            classes += " o_library_open_loan";
        }
        return classes;
    }
}

class LoanKanbanRenderer extends KanbanRenderer {
    static components = { ...KanbanRenderer.components, KanbanRecord: LoanKanbanRecord };
}

registry.category("views").add("library_loan_kanban", {
    ...kanbanView,
    Renderer: LoanKanbanRenderer,
});

getRecordClasses() returns a string of classes in 18 (classes.push(...) then joined). Always call super and append to the string. The card template itself comes from the arch (<templates><t t-name="card">) and is compiled by the kanban compiler, so markup changes belong in the arch of the view.

docs.title: The arch parser: reading new attributes
docs.text:
To give your view its own arch attributes, parse them into archInfo:

import { ListArchParser } from "@web/views/list/list_arch_parser";

class LoanListArchParser extends ListArchParser {
    parse(xmlDoc, models, modelName) {
        const archInfo = super.parse(...arguments);
        archInfo.libraryWarnDays = parseInt(xmlDoc.getAttribute("library_warn_days") || "0", 10);
        return archInfo;
    }
}

registry.category("views").add("library_loan_list", {
    ...listView,
    ArchParser: LoanListArchParser,
});

<list js_class="library_loan_list" library_warn_days="3">

The renderer and controller receive archInfo as a prop, so this.props.archInfo.libraryWarnDays is available. Server-side arch validation in Odoo 18 checks known attributes of known tags against RNG schemas; an unknown attribute on a standard tag may be rejected when the view is saved. If it is, put the setting in options or in the context of the action instead.

docs.title: Layout slots and where markup goes
docs.text: The list view template web.ListView fills slots of the Layout component: control-panel-create-button, layout-buttons, control-panel-always-buttons, layout-actions, control-panel-navigation-additional, among others. The buttons template you replaced above is what the layout-buttons slot calls. For changes that fit a slot, the button template is the smaller intervention. For deeper structural changes, extend the template with t-inherit (see the patching chapter) rather than copy it.

docs.title: Sharing code across views
docs.text: A recurring need is "all list views of module X should behave like this". Do not patch ListController for it. Define the definition once and select it explicitly with js_class on each arch that wants it. Where many views need the same behaviour, make the shared part a mixin-style base class and give each view its own small subclass registered under its own key.

docs.title: Odoo 20 notes
docs.text:
In the Odoo 20 source the view definition objects keep their shape (type, Controller, Renderer, ArchParser, Model, buttonTemplate, props). What changes is the component code underneath:

  • Controllers declare props = useProps({...}) with OWL 3 types instead of static props.
  • Templates address members with this..
  • Some method signatures changed. Examples from the two trees: ListController.openRecord(record, force) becomes openRecord(record, { force, newWindow }), and FormController.beforeLeave() becomes beforeLeave({ forceLeave }). Re-read each method you override.
  • The 20 list view definition does not carry the limit: 80 key that 18 has.

The registry key, the js_class attribute and the subclass-and-spread technique carry over. Treat each override as something to re-verify after a major upgrade.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Registering the same key twice. The second add throws on load. Build one definition per js_class and put all keys in it.
  • js_class typo. The view loads the lazy bundle, then fails looking the key up.
  • Using <tree> in 18. The arch root is <list> in 18.
  • Overriding a method and not calling super. You lose selection classes, decorations or saving behaviour of the base.
  • Using extension instead of primary for a buttons template. The standard list buttons change for every list in the database.
  • Reading a field that is not in the arch. record.data.due_date is undefined unless the field is in the view; add it with column_invisible="1".
  • Relying on private members (_something) of controllers or models. Prefer documented hook methods (onWillSaveRecord, beforeExecuteActionButton, afterExecuteActionButton, getRowClass).
  • Logic in the renderer. Actions belong to the controller; the renderer re-renders often and should stay pure.
  • Client-side checks as business rules. The server must enforce them.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
16: views are mixed legacy and OWL. The OWL view stack exists for list, form, kanban and others, but legacy views still appear. Arch root is <tree>.

17: the OWL view stack is the only one. Arch root is <tree>.

18: arch root is <list>; the registry shapes above apply.

20: same registry model, OWL 3 component code.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
1. Implement recipe 1. Open library.loan through an action. Check the button appears on lists using js_class and not on others.
  2. Add recipe 2's renderer to the same definition. Create a loan with a past due date and confirm the row class.
  3. Replace t-inherit-mode="primary" with extension in the buttons template, restart, and look at a different model's list. Revert it.
  4. Misspell js_class in the arch and read the console.
Solution notes
  1. The button only exists where the arch has js_class="library_loan_list", because only that definition points at the new button template.
  2. The row gets the class from getRowClass; with ?debug=1 you can inspect the tr and find o_library_overdue.
  3. With extension, the standard template web.ListView.Buttons is modified, so every list view in the database shows the button (and onClickOverdue does not exist on other controllers, so the click throws).
  4. The views registry reports that the key cannot be found, after the lazy bundle has been requested.

docs.title: Frontend overview
docs.text:
Odoo ships three different JavaScript worlds, and most confusion comes from mixing them. A snippet that works in the backend does nothing on a public page, and a tutorial for one version can crash another.

Everything below was checked against the Odoo 18 source and, where noted, against Odoo 20. Version differences are called out in the Versions section at the end.

docs.title: The three worlds
docs.text:
World Where it runs Stack Entry bundle Backend web client /odoo (18, 20) or /web (16, 17) after login OWL, ES modules, registries, services web.assets_web (includes web.assets_backend) Website and portal public pages, /my, e-commerce publicWidget (jQuery era), OWL for newer parts, public_components web.assets_frontend Tours and tests any of the above web_tour, hoot unit tests (QUnit in older code) web.assets_tests, web.assets_unit_tests

Two more bundles you will meet: web.report_assets_common (what PDF reports load, see the reports chapter in part 08) and web.assets_backend_lazy (graph and pivot views, loaded on demand).

List the bundles of the version you run instead of trusting a table:

grep -nE "^\s+'web\.[a-z_]+': \[" addons/web/__manifest__.py

In 18 this prints web.assets_backend, web.assets_backend_lazy, web.assets_web, web.assets_frontend, web.assets_frontend_lazy, web.report_assets_common, web.assets_tests, web.assets_unit_tests, the private web._assets_* helper bundles, and a few more.

The rule of thumb: ask where the code will execute. If a logged-in employee sees it, it is the backend client. If an anonymous visitor or a portal user sees it on a QWeb page, it is the website world. If the code only exists to drive a browser through a scenario, it is a tour.

docs.title: How the backend client starts
docs.text:
Understanding the boot sequence explains most "my code is not running" problems.

  1. The browser requests /odoo (18) or /web (16, 17). The controller in addons/web/controllers/home.py renders the web.webclient_bootstrap QWeb template. That template emits the <script> and <link> tags for the web.assets_web bundle and a small inline odoo global with the session info.
  2. The bundle loads. Each .js file is a module registered with a tiny loader (addons/web/static/src/module_loader.js). The loader keeps odoo.loader.modules (a Map of started modules), odoo.loader.factories (modules defined but not yet started) and odoo.loader.failed. A module starts once all its dependencies have started.
  3. main.js calls startWebClient(WebClient), which waits for the DOM and calls mountComponent. That builds the env, starts every service in the services registry in dependency order, loads templates, and mounts the WebClient OWL component on document.body.
  4. The web client loads the menus (/web/webclient/load_menus/<hash>), reads the URL, and asks the action service to open the matching action. The action's type and view_type select entries from the actions and views registries.

Two consequences:

  • Registries are filled at module load time, step 2, before services start in step 3. That is why every registry.category(...).add(...) sits at the top level of a file and not inside a function.
