      end-cleanup.py
    18.0.1.2.0/
      post-recompute-fees.py
    0.0.0/
      end-invariants.py

Rules from MigrationManager:

  • Scripts are looked up in <module>/migrations/<version>/ and <module>/upgrades/<version>/, and in the odoo.upgrade package paths under a folder named after the module.
  • The folder name must match the version pattern, otherwise Odoo logs Invalid version for upgrade script and ignores it. A folder named tests is skipped.
  • A file's stage is its prefix: pre- runs before the module's data files are loaded, post- after them, end- after all modules have been updated. Files in one stage run in file-name order.
  • Files without these prefixes, and anything not ending in .py, are ignored.

docs.title: Which versions trigger a script
docs.text:
For a module being updated, a folder V runs when the installed version is lower than V and V is lower than or equal to the new manifest version:

installed < V <= current
  • A folder with two or three parts such as 1.1 is a "majorless" version: Odoo prepends the server series (18.0.1.1) for ordering but compares only the module part, so a 1.1 script does not run again when you move the same module from series 17 to series 18.
  • A folder with the full server version (18.0.1.2.0) is processed only by that server series.
  • 0.0.0 runs on any version change. In the pre stage its scripts run first; in post and end they run last.

Scripts run only for modules that are being updated. A fresh install runs none of them, so initial data belongs in the module's normal data files.

docs.title: The function
docs.text:
# library/migrations/1.1/pre-rename-isbn.py
def migrate(cr, version):
    # `version` is the installed version before the update, or '' if unknown.
    cr.execute("SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns "
               "WHERE table_name = 'library_book' AND column_name = 'isbn_code'")
    if cr.fetchone():
        cr.execute("ALTER TABLE library_book RENAME COLUMN isbn_code TO isbn")

The loader checks the signature: the parameters must be exactly (cr, version), or the underscore variants (_cr, _version), positional. Anything else raises TypeError, and a file without migrate raises AttributeError naming the file. Each file is imported as odoo.upgrade.<module>.<version>.<name> and logged as Running upgrade [>1.1] pre-rename-isbn (pre), [1.1>] (post) or [$1.1] (end).

docs.title: Which stage for which job
docs.text: Job Stage Why Rename a column or table the new model expects under a new name pre the ORM creates missing columns during the update and would make an empty duplicate Drop a constraint or index that blocks the new schema pre the new definition cannot load while the old one stands Backfill a new stored field from old data post the column exists only after the module loaded Fix data using new ORM methods post models and fields are available Cleanup that depends on other modules being updated end all modules have finished An invariant to re-check on every upgrade 0.0.0/end-... runs last, on any change

docs.title: Writing scripts that can run twice
docs.text:
An upgrade is rehearsed several times, and a failed run is retried. Write every script so a second run changes nothing:

def migrate(cr, version):
    cr.execute("""
        UPDATE library_loan
           SET state = 'returned'
         WHERE state = 'closed'
    """)

UPDATE ... WHERE state = 'closed' is safe to repeat. ALTER TABLE ... RENAME is not, which is why the example above checks information_schema first. Read-only counterpart first:

SELECT state, count(*) FROM library_loan GROUP BY state ORDER BY 2 DESC;

Rules:

  1. SQL for volume, the ORM for logic. A table of a million rows is UPDATE in pre, not a loop in post. When you need ORM behaviour, build the environment: env = api.Environment(cr, SUPERUSER_ID, {}).
  2. Never commit. The loader owns the transaction. A script that calls cr.commit() breaks rollback of a failed upgrade.
  3. Be explicit about data you cannot convert. Log it (_logger.warning) or raise, rather than skipping rows silently.
  4. Do not import models in pre. The registry for the new code is not built yet.
  5. Keep scripts small and named after the job: pre-rename-isbn.py, not pre-fixes.py.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Restore a copy of production, install the old version of your module, bump the manifest version, run the update with the script and compare:

odoo-bin -d upgrade_test -u library --stop-after-init --log-level=info

Then run the same command again. The second run must log the scripts and change nothing. Check the log for Running upgrade lines to confirm which scripts fired. If a script did not run, compare the installed version (SELECT latest_version FROM ir_module_module WHERE name = 'library') with the folder name and the manifest version using the installed < V <= current rule.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A folder named 1.1.0 when the manifest says 18.0.1.2.0: it is lower than the installed version on later runs and never fires.
  • Forgetting to bump the manifest version. Without a higher version the module updates but no script folder qualifies.
  • Putting initial data in a script. Fresh installs skip scripts.
  • Renaming a model or a field without a pre script, which leaves the old column and the data in it behind.
  • Importing the module's own models in pre.
  • Calling cr.commit().

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
1. Create migrations/1.1/pre-rename-isbn.py as above and bump the version.
  2. Run the update twice and compare the logs.
  3. Add migrations/0.0.0/end-log.py that logs one line, and see when it fires.
Solution notes
  1. The first run logs Running upgrade [>1.1] pre-rename-isbn and renames the column; the second sees no isbn_code and does nothing.
  2. The second run does not log the 1.1 script at all if the installed version is already at or above it.
  3. The 0.0.0 script fires on every version change, last in the end stage.

docs.title: Upgrading a database
docs.text: A database upgrade is a data project, not a deployment. The goal is to prove on a copy that the upgraded database behaves, and only then repeat on production in a maintenance window.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text:
1. Inventory: which modules are installed, which are custom, which are community.
  2. Port every custom module to the target version (see Upgrading a module).
  3. Restore a copy of production on a test server.
  4. Run the upgrade on the copy; fix; restore the copy again; repeat until a clean run needs no manual steps.
  5. Have business users test their flows on the final copy.
  6. Freeze production, take a backup, run the same scripted steps, validate.

Repeating from a fresh restore each time is the point: a run that needs a manual fix in the middle is not yet reproducible.

docs.title: Read-only inventory
docs.text:
SELECT name, state, latest_version FROM ir_module_module
WHERE state = 'installed' ORDER BY name;

SELECT relname, n_live_tup FROM pg_stat_user_tables
ORDER BY n_live_tup DESC LIMIT 20;

The second query finds the tables where a recompute or a loop script will take hours.

docs.title: Run the upgrade
docs.text:
Odoo's own modules are migrated by Odoo's upgrade service or by the community OpenUpgrade project, depending on your edition and version path (neither is part of the source checked for this book); custom modules by your scripts. Whichever tool moves the standard schema, finish with your modules. odoo-bin db helps with the copies: dump writes a dump with the filestore, load restores one (--neutralize neutralises it afterwards), duplicate copies a database with its filestore (also --neutralize), and odoo-bin neutralize -d <db> --stdout prints the neutralisation SQL instead of applying it.

pg_restore -d lib_test backup.dump
odoo-bin -d lib_test -u all --stop-after-init --log-level=info 2>&1 | tee upgrade.log

Jumping several series is done step by step (16 to 17 to 18), not in one run, because each series' migration assumes the previous one's schema.

docs.title: After the run
docs.text:
grep -cE "ERROR|CRITICAL" upgrade.log

Then check data, not just logs:

SELECT count(*) FROM library_book WHERE isbn13 IS NULL;
SELECT model, count(*) FROM ir_model_data WHERE module = 'library' GROUP BY model;

Open the main menus as a normal user, not as admin: access rules and record rules are where an upgrade quietly hides records.

docs.title: Things that break only on real data
docs.text:
• Views stored in the database (customised from the UI) that point at removed fields. List them: SELECT id, name FROM ir_ui_view WHERE arch_updated.
  • Server actions and automations containing Python or domains in the old syntax.
  • Mail templates using removed fields in QWeb.
  • Reports with custom paper formats.
  • Attachments: confirm the filestore is copied with the database dump, or every file is gone.

Never run -u all on production for the first time. Always restore a copy, and never point a copy at the production outgoing mail server or crons; neutralise them first (odoo-bin db load --neutralize or odoo-bin neutralize).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Testing with a small anonymised database that lacks the data shapes that break (null parents, archived records, multi-company).
  • A copy that still sends email or calls external APIs through live cron jobs.
  • Forgetting that dumps do not include the filestore.
  • No rollback plan. The rollback is the backup plus the old server, so keep both until sign-off.

docs.title: Upgrading a module
docs.text: You have a custom module that works on one version and must load on the next. This page is the order of work that avoids rediscovering errors one at a time. The reference for what changed is Version differences.

docs.title: Work on a branch per version
docs.text: Create a branch named after the target (18.0), not a long-lived feature branch. Bump the manifest version to 18.0.1.0.0. The first two segments are the Odoo series. The migration loader compares the module version with the installed one to decide which migrations/ folders run, so a higher version is what triggers your scripts.

docs.title: The sequence
docs.text:
1. Run the rewrite scripts on a clean branch first: odoo-bin upgrade_code --addons-path=./my_addons --from <your current series> --dry-run, then without --dry-run, and commit the result on its own (see Deprecations). Available from 18.0.
  2. Start a throw-away database with only your module's dependencies, then install your module with -i library --stop-after-init. Read the first traceback; fix; repeat. Do not fix everything by grepping first, the real loader order shows what matters.
  3. Fix XML first. View validation fails before Python is imported for most issues. Convert attrs/states to expressions (no script does it), tree to list (script tree-to-list), replace removed XML ids.
  4. Fix Python: removed or renamed methods (name_get is gone in 18, _name_search became _search_display_name), changed signatures, check_access_rights (deprecated in 18, gone in 20), _sql_constraints, type='json' routes, _cr/_uid/_context. The version table in Version differences lists each with its release.
  5. Fix data files: noupdate records that reference renamed ids, removed groups, changed selection keys.
  6. Rewrite JavaScript. Legacy widgets are not portable; treat each as a new OWL component.
  7. Run the tests: -u library --test-tags /library --stop-after-init.
  8. Only then write migration scripts for existing databases (see Migration scripts).
odoo-bin -d lib_18 -i library --stop-after-init --log-level=warn 2>&1 | tee install.log
grep -nE "WARNING|ERROR|Deprecat" install.log

docs.title: Find removed standard ids
docs.text:
The most common XML failure is a reference to a standard view or group that was renamed. Check the target source read-only:

grep -rn 'id="view_partner_form"' odoo/addons/base/views/ addons/*/views/

If an inherit_id target moved, the traceback names the ref that failed. Replace it with the new xml id, and if the anchor element (//field[@name='x']) disappeared, re-anchor on a stable sibling.

docs.title: Keep one codebase when you must
docs.text:
If you maintain two series, do not sprinkle if version in Python. Keep one branch per series and cherry-pick fixes. The XML syntax differences make a shared branch unreadable.

A module that installs cleanly on an empty database can still fail on upgrade of a real one: new required fields without defaults, changed constraints, and renamed selection keys only show on existing rows.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Forgetting to bump the manifest version: no migrations/ folder qualifies and none of your scripts run.
  • Leaving external_dependencies unchanged when the target needs a newer Python library.
  • Adding a stored computed field on a large table without checking recompute time; it recomputes on update.
  • Overriding create with the old single-vals signature and breaking batch creation.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text: Run your test suite once with the old branch on the old version, record the pass count, then compare after the port. A lower count is a regression, not a "removed test".

docs.title: Version differences, 16 to 20
docs.text: This page lists changes that break custom module code, grouped by the release that introduced them. Each item was checked in the source of at least one release: the 16.0 and 17.0 branches, the 18.0 source, and the Odoo 20 tree. Odoo 19 was not available as a full checkout. Items for 19 come from the deprecation markers and the upgrade_code scripts shipped in the 20 tree, and are labelled that way.

docs.title: Reading the upgrade_code version numbers
docs.text: Odoo ships rewrite scripts in odoo/upgrade_code/, named <version>-<name>.py. The prefix is the master development version in which the change landed, not a release number. The branch listings show the mapping: the 18.0 branch contains only 17.5-* scripts, the 19.0 branch contains 17.5 to 18.5, and the 20 tree adds 19.1 to 20.0. So 17.5 means "in Odoo 18", 18.x means "in Odoo 19", 19.x and 20.0 mean "in Odoo 20". The upgrade-a-module chapter shows how to run them.

docs.title: 16.0 to 17.0
docs.text:
Views: attrs and states are removed. The 17.0 view validation raises Since 17.0, the "attrs" and "states" attributes are no longer used. (ir_ui_view.py). invisible, readonly, required and column_invisible take expressions:

<!-- 16.0 -->
<field name="note" attrs="{'invisible': [('state', '=', 'done')], 'required': [('kind', '=', 'x')]}"/>
<button name="action_close" states="open,late"/>

<!-- 17.0 and later -->
<field name="note" invisible="state == 'done'" required="kind == 'x'"/>
<button name="action_close" invisible="state not in ('open', 'late')"/>

Conversion: ('a', '=', False) becomes not a, ('a', 'in', [1, 2]) becomes a in (1, 2), domain operators | and & become or and and. A field referenced in an expression must be present in the view; add it with invisible="1" if needed.

_read_group gets its aggregate-based signature. 16.0 has _read_group(domain, fields, groupby, offset, limit, orderby, lazy). From 17.0 it is _read_group(domain, groupby=(), aggregates=(), having=(), offset=0, limit=None, order=None), returning tuples (group values first, then aggregates such as '__count' or 'amount:sum'). Many2one group keys are records. read_group remains for the web client.

name_get is deprecated. The 17.0 name_get emits Since 17.0, deprecated method, read display_name instead. _compute_display_name already exists in 16.0. _name_search changes signature in 17.0 (name, domain, operator, limit, order instead of name, args, operator, limit, name_get_uid).

JavaScript. The legacy widget layer leaves the backend client; custom JavaScript from 16 is a rewrite. See the frontend part.

docs.title: 17.0 to 18.0
docs.text:
<tree> becomes <list>. In 18.0 ir.ui.view.type has list and no tree (17.0 has tree), and the 18.0 branch ships the script 17.5-01-tree-to-list.py to convert arches, view_mode values, xpaths and tree_view_ref context keys. Run it instead of editing by hand.

name_get and _name_search are removed. 18.0 has _compute_display_name, _search_display_name(operator, value) (returns a domain) and name_search. A module that overrides name_get loses the override silently.

@api.depends("name", "isbn")
def _compute_display_name(self):
    for book in self:
        book.display_name = f"[{book.isbn}] {book.name}" if book.isbn else book.name

Access check methods. check_access_rights, check_access_rule and _filter_access_rules are deprecated since 18.0 in favour of check_access(operation), has_access(operation) and _filtered_access(operation).

ir.property is gone. ir_property.py exists on 16.0 and 17.0 and not on 18.0. Company-dependent fields are stored as a jsonb column on the model table (keys are company ids, defaults come from ir.default). SQL written against ir_property has to be rewritten.

SQL objects. odoo.tools.SQL exists from 17.0. Build queries with it rather than string formatting.

docs.title: 18.0 to 19.0 (from the 20 tree)
docs.text:
• @route(type='json') becomes type='jsonrpc'. The 20 router logs Since 19.0, @route(type='json') is a deprecated alias to @route(type='jsonrpc'). Script 18.1-02-route-jsonrpc.py replaces it in controllers.
  • _sql_constraints become models.Constraint attributes. Script 18.1-00-sql-constraint.py rewrites _sql_constraints = [(name, definition, message)] into _name = models.Constraint(definition, message).
  • self._cr, self._uid, self._context are deprecated (Deprecated since 19.0, use self.env.cr directly). Script 18.5-00-deprecated-properties.py rewrites them to .env.cr, .env.uid, .env.context. request.cr, request.uid and request.context carry the same deprecation in the HTTP layer.
  • Search view date filters and domain dynamic dates have rewrite scripts (18.5-00-domain-dynamic-dates.py).

docs.title: 19.0 to 20.0 (from the 20 tree)
docs.text:
• ACLs and record rules become ir.access. Script 19.4-00-ir-access.py converts ir.model.access and ir.rule data. The combining rule changes: permissions are OR-ed, restrictions AND-ed, no permission means no access. See the security chapters.
  • Groups use privileges. res.groups.privilege_id replaces category_id; user_ids replaces users; the user's groups are group_ids/all_group_ids instead of groups_id.
  • OWL 3. static props becomes useProps, useState becomes proxy, refs are signals, templates use this.. Script owl3-migration.py rewrites part of it. See the OWL 3 chapter.
  • type="base64" in XML data files becomes type="bytes" (Since 20.0, use type=bytes instead of type=base64 in tools/convert.py; script 19.3-00-base64-in-xml.py).
  • registry.clear_cache becomes transaction.invalidate_ormcache (script 19.4-00-ormcache-on-transaction.py), and ormcache is imported from odoo.api (Since 20.0 import ormcache from odoo.api).
  • The deprecated access methods are gone. check_access_rights, check_access_rule, _filter_access_rules and check_field_access_rights no longer exist in the 20 orm/models.py; check_access, has_access, _filtered_access and check_field_access(field, operation) remain. _check_access is deprecated in favour of Model._access_domain (Since 20.0, use Model._access_domain instead) and _check_field_access in favour of check_field_access().
  • Query and SQL. Query methods accept only SQL arguments in 20 (several Since 20.0 warnings in orm/query.py), and tools.sql helpers are renamed (escape_like_value).
  • concat() and union() warn when called with one iterable or on an empty recordset.
  • _rec_names_search is a tuple (script 19.5-00-tuple-rec_names_search.py), icons move from FontAwesome markup to Material Symbols (19.5-00-material-symbols-icons.py), and search date filters lose per-view month and year attributes (20.0-00-search-date-filters.py).

docs.title: Summary table
docs.text:
Topic 16.0 17.0 18.0 19.0 20 Field visibility in views attrs, states expressions expressions expressions expressions List view tag tree tree list list list _read_group signature old aggregates aggregates aggregates aggregates name_get yes deprecated removed removed removed _search_display_name no no yes yes yes Company-dependent storage ir.property ir.property jsonb column jsonb jsonb Access check check_access_rights check_access_rights check_access (old names deprecated) check_access check_access; old names removed Route type for JSON json json json jsonrpc (json alias) jsonrpc Constraints _sql_constraints _sql_constraints _sql_constraints models.Constraint models.Constraint ACL and rules ir.model.access + ir.rule same same same ir.access Frontend OWL 2 + legacy OWL 2 OWL 2 OWL 2 OWL 3

Cells for 19 are inferred from the deprecation markers and script prefixes and were not run on a 19 install.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Fixing the XML and forgetting the Python. The views load, the first button click fails on a removed method.
  • Overriding name_get on 18 or later. The method is gone and the override does nothing.
  • Running upgrade scripts blindly. They are best-effort rewrites; review the diff.
  • Treating a deprecation warning as optional. Each Since X marker above is a removal waiting for the next release.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Search your module for what the next version will break:

grep -rnE "attrs=|states=|<tree|name_get|_sql_constraints|type=.json|\._cr\b|\._uid\b|\._context\b|ir\.model\.access|ir\.rule" my_addons --include=*.xml --include=*.py --include=*.csv

Every hit is a line to review before you bump the version in the manifest.

docs.title: A portal feature
docs.text: A portal feature is three things that must agree: a controller that serves /my/... routes, QWeb templates that render the list and detail pages, and access control that makes sure a customer sees only their own records. This blueprint builds /my/loans, a list and detail page for library.loan records (the teaching model, see library module), using the same extension points the standard sales portal uses.

docs.title: Assumed model
docs.text:
class LibraryLoan(models.Model):
    _name = 'library.loan'
    _description = 'Library Loan'
    _inherit = ['portal.mixin', 'mail.thread']
    _order = 'date_loan desc, id desc'

    name = fields.Char(required=True, default='New', copy=False)
    partner_id = fields.Many2one('res.partner', required=True, index=True)
    book_id = fields.Many2one('library.book', required=True)
    date_loan = fields.Date(default=fields.Date.context_today)
    state = fields.Selection([('open', 'Open'), ('returned', 'Returned')], default='open')

    def _compute_access_url(self):
        super()._compute_access_url()
        for loan in self:
            loan.access_url = f'/my/loans/{loan.id}'

portal.mixin adds access_url, access_token, access_warning, and _get_share_url(). The standard sale.order does the same: its _inherit list contains portal.mixin, and it overrides _compute_access_url to return /my/orders/<id> (verified in Odoo 18). Without the mixin you have no token-based sharing and _get_page_view_values has nothing to read.

docs.title: Access control first
docs.text:
Write the security before the pages. Two layers:

id,name,model_id:id,group_id:id,perm_read,perm_write,perm_create,perm_unlink
access_library_loan_portal,library.loan portal,model_library_loan,base.group_portal,1,0,0,0
access_library_loan_user,library.loan user,model_library_loan,base.group_user,1,1,1,1

<record id="library_loan_rule_portal" model="ir.rule">
    <field name="name">Library Loan: portal sees own</field>
    <field name="model_id" ref="model_library_loan"/>
    <field name="domain_force">[('partner_id', 'child_of', [user.commercial_partner_id.id])]</field>
    <field name="groups" eval="[(4, ref('base.group_portal'))]"/>
    <field name="perm_read" eval="True"/>
    <field name="perm_write" eval="False"/>
    <field name="perm_create" eval="False"/>
    <field name="perm_unlink" eval="False"/>
</record>

The ACL says portal users may read the model at all. The rule says which rows. The standard sale rule uses message_partner_ids child_of commercial_partner_id, which lets a company's contacts see each other's orders; partner_id child_of commercial_partner_id is the simpler equivalent when the record has a single owner.

Never "fix" a portal access problem with sudo() in the controller and a hand-written filter. The record rule is the access control; sudo() removes it, and the first forgotten domain becomes a data leak.

docs.title: Controller
docs.text:
Inherit CustomerPortal from odoo.addons.portal.controllers.portal. In Odoo 18 it provides _prepare_home_portal_values(counters), _get_page_view_values(...), _document_check_access(model_name, document_id, access_token), and the module-level pager(...) helper.

from odoo import http
from odoo.exceptions import AccessError, MissingError
from odoo.http import request
from odoo.addons.portal.controllers.portal import CustomerPortal, pager as portal_pager


class LibraryPortal(CustomerPortal):

    def _prepare_home_portal_values(self, counters):
        values = super()._prepare_home_portal_values(counters)
        if 'loan_count' in counters:
            values['loan_count'] = (
                request.env['library.loan'].search_count([])
                if request.env['library.loan'].has_access('read') else 0
            )
        return values

    @http.route(['/my/loans', '/my/loans/page/<int:page>'],
                type='http', auth='user', website=True)
    def portal_my_loans(self, page=1, sortby='date', **kw):
        Loan = request.env['library.loan']
        searchbar_sortings = {
            'date': {'label': 'Newest', 'order': 'date_loan desc, id desc'},
            'name': {'label': 'Reference', 'order': 'name'},
        }
        order = searchbar_sortings.get(sortby, searchbar_sortings['date'])['order']

        total = Loan.search_count([])
        pager = portal_pager(
            url='/my/loans', url_args={'sortby': sortby},
            total=total, page=page, step=self._items_per_page,
        )
        loans = Loan.search([], order=order, limit=self._items_per_page,
                            offset=pager['offset'])
        values = self._prepare_portal_layout_values()
        values.update({
            'loans': loans,
            'page_name': 'loan',
            'pager': pager,
            'default_url': '/my/loans',
            'searchbar_sortings': searchbar_sortings,
            'sortby': sortby,
        })
        return request.render('library_portal.portal_my_loans', values)

    @http.route('/my/loans/<int:loan_id>', type='http', auth='public', website=True)
    def portal_my_loan(self, loan_id, access_token=None, **kw):
        try:
            loan_sudo = self._document_check_access('library.loan', loan_id, access_token)
        except (AccessError, MissingError):
            return request.redirect('/my')
        values = self._get_page_view_values(
            loan_sudo, access_token, {'loan': loan_sudo, 'page_name': 'loan'},
            'my_loans_history', False,
        )
        return request.render('library_portal.portal_my_loan', values)

Points that matter:

  • The list uses search([]) with the current user's environment, not sudo(). The record rule narrows it to the customer. There is no domain to forget.
  • The list route is auth='user': anonymous visitors are redirected to login. The detail route is auth='public' so a share link with ?access_token=... works without login. _document_check_access then does the real check: it tries check_access('read') as the current user and falls back to a constant-time comparison of the token. It returns the record sudoed, so reads in the template skip rules; this is safe only because access was just verified.
  • _items_per_page is defined on CustomerPortal (80 in Odoo 18). Do not hard-code your own.
  • _prepare_home_portal_values feeds the counters on /my; the /my/counters JSON route calls it with the list of placeholders requested by the home template.
  • Sort keys come from a whitelist dict. Never pass sortby straight into order=; that is SQL-injection-adjacent and an order error 500.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
The home page entry hooks into portal.portal_my_home, as sale.portal_my_home_sale does (it targets the portal_client_category div and calls portal.portal_docs_entry with title, url, placeholder_count).

<odoo>
    <template id="portal_my_home_library" name="Portal: loans entry"
              inherit_id="portal.portal_my_home" customize_show="True" priority="40">
        <xpath expr="//div[hasclass('o_portal_docs')]" position="before">
            <t t-set="portal_client_category_enable" t-value="True"/>
        </xpath>
        <div id="portal_client_category" position="inside">
            <t t-call="portal.portal_docs_entry">
                <t t-set="title">Your Loans</t>
                <t t-set="url" t-value="'/my/loans'"/>
                <t t-set="text">Follow your borrowed books</t>
                <t t-set="placeholder_count" t-value="'loan_count'"/>
            </t>
        </div>
    </template>

    <template id="portal_my_loans" name="My Loans">
        <t t-call="portal.portal_layout">
            <t t-set="breadcrumbs_searchbar" t-value="True"/>
            <t t-call="portal.portal_searchbar">
                <t t-set="title">Loans</t>
            </t>
            <t t-if="not loans">
                <p class="alert alert-warning">You have no loans.</p>
            </t>
            <t t-if="loans" t-call="portal.portal_table">
                <thead>
                    <tr class="active">
                        <th>Reference</th>
                        <th>Book</th>
                        <th class="text-end">Date</th>
                        <th class="text-end">Status</th>
                    </tr>
                </thead>
                <tbody>
                    <tr t-foreach="loans" t-as="loan">
                        <td><a t-att-href="loan.get_portal_url()"><t t-out="loan.name"/></a></td>
                        <td><t t-out="loan.book_id.display_name"/></td>
                        <td class="text-end"><span t-field="loan.date_loan"/></td>
                        <td class="text-end"><span t-field="loan.state"/></td>
                    </tr>
                </tbody>
            </t>
        </t>
    </template>

    <template id="portal_my_loan" name="My Loan">
        <t t-call="portal.portal_layout">
            <t t-set="o_portal_fullwidth_alert" t-value="True"/>
            <div class="card">
                <div class="card-body">
                    <h3 t-out="loan.name"/>
                    <p>Book: <span t-field="loan.book_id.display_name"/></p>
                    <p>Date: <span t-field="loan.date_loan"/></p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </t>
    </template>
</odoo>

Manifest: 'depends': ['portal', 'library'], data files in order: security CSV, rules XML, template XML. Templates in views/ need the website dependency only if you use website-only features; website=True on routes works when website is installed, which the portal pulls in on typical databases.

t-field renders with the viewer's language and the field's widget; t-out escapes. Never use t-raw, removed in 17 (use t-out with Markup).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
from odoo.tests import HttpCase, tagged


@tagged('post_install', '-at_install')
class TestLoanPortal(HttpCase):

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        super().setUpClass()
        cls.p1 = cls.env['res.users'].create({
            'name': 'Portal One', 'login': 'portal_one',
            'password': 'portal_one',
            'groups_id': [(6, 0, [cls.env.ref('base.group_portal').id])],
        })
        cls.p2 = cls.env['res.users'].create({
            'name': 'Portal Two', 'login': 'portal_two',
            'password': 'portal_two',
            'groups_id': [(6, 0, [cls.env.ref('base.group_portal').id])],
        })
        book = cls.env['library.book'].create({'name': 'Sample Book'})
        cls.loan1 = cls.env['library.loan'].create({
            'partner_id': cls.p1.partner_id.id, 'book_id': book.id})
        cls.loan2 = cls.env['library.loan'].create({
            'partner_id': cls.p2.partner_id.id, 'book_id': book.id})

    def test_list_shows_only_own(self):
        self.authenticate('portal_one', 'portal_one')
        res = self.url_open('/my/loans')
        self.assertEqual(res.status_code, 200)
        self.assertIn(self.loan1.name, res.text)
        self.assertNotIn(self.loan2.name, res.text)

    def test_detail_of_foreign_record_redirects(self):
        self.authenticate('portal_one', 'portal_one')
        res = self.url_open(f'/my/loans/{self.loan2.id}', allow_redirects=False)
        self.assertEqual(res.status_code, 303)

    def test_token_gives_access(self):
        self.loan2._portal_ensure_token()
        res = self.url_open(f'/my/loans/{self.loan2.id}?access_token={self.loan2.access_token}')
        self.assertEqual(res.status_code, 200)

    def test_rule_blocks_orm(self):
        from odoo.exceptions import AccessError
        with self.assertRaises(AccessError):
            self.loan2.with_user(self.p1).read(['name'])

Give the two loans distinct names (a sequence on create works) or the assertNotIn check is meaningless. groups_id is the Odoo 16-18 name on res.users.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Using sudo() in the list controller. All customers see everything.
  • No ACL line for base.group_portal: the page works for you as admin and returns an AccessError for every customer. Always test as a portal user.
  • A global record rule elsewhere that references internal-only fields breaks portal reads (see extending a standard workflow).
  • auth='public' on a list route. Public users have no partner; the rule's user.commercial_partner_id is empty, so the list is empty or errors.
  • Tokens: access_token in the URL is a bearer secret. Do not log full URLs, and do not generate tokens for records the customer should never share.
  • Missing placeholder_count in the counters method: the home page badge stays on a spinner.
  • Computing counts with sudo().search_count. Counts leak the existence of other customers' records.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: 16 to 18: the controller base class, _document_check_access, _get_page_view_values and the portal.portal_docs_entry pattern are the same. 17 and 18 use has_access('read') and check_access('read'); in 16 these are check_access_rights('read', raise_exception=False) and check_access_rule('read'). Home counters loaded through /my/counters are the model in 17 and 18; in 16 the home controller computed the values directly. t-raw is removed from 17.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Read-only: list the portal rules and ACLs already on the sales model, to model yours on them.

select name, domain_force from ir_rule r join ir_model m on m.id = r.model_id where m.model = 'sale.order';

Then log in as a portal user (not admin) in a private window and open /my/loans.

docs.title: Data repair scripts
docs.text: Production data goes wrong: a bug wrote duplicates, an import left orphans, a migration missed a field. A repair is safe when it is a read-only finding, a reviewed fix, and a record of what changed. This blueprint is a pattern, using library.loan as the example.

docs.title: The pattern
docs.text:
1. Write the read-only query that defines "bad".
  2. Count and sample it. Show the numbers to whoever owns the data.
  3. Write the fix, idempotent, with a dry-run mode that rolls back.
  4. Save the before values.
  5. Run on a restored copy, then on production.
  6. Verify with the query from step 1; it must return zero.

docs.title: Find
docs.text:
SELECT id, name, book_id, date_out, date_due
FROM library_loan
WHERE state = 'open' AND date_due < date_out
ORDER BY id;

Keep this query in the script; it is the acceptance test.

docs.title: A script that runs through odoo shell
docs.text:
Run it on a copy first. The script is a file you pass on stdin, so it is reviewed and versioned:

odoo-bin shell -d lib_copy --no-http < repair_loans.py

# repair_loans.py
import csv
import logging

_logger = logging.getLogger('repair')
DRY_RUN = True          # flip to False deliberately, in review

Loan = env['library.loan']
bad = Loan.search([('state', '=', 'open')]).filtered(lambda l: l.date_due < l.date_out)
_logger.info("found %s bad loans", len(bad))

with open('/tmp/loans_before.csv', 'w', newline='') as fh:
    w = csv.writer(fh)
    w.writerow(['id', 'date_out', 'date_due'])
    for loan in bad:
        w.writerow([loan.id, loan.date_out, loan.date_due])

for loan in bad:
    loan.with_context(tracking_disable=True).write({'date_due': loan.date_out})
    loan.message_post(body="Due date corrected by data repair.")

if DRY_RUN:
    env.cr.rollback()
    _logger.info("dry run, rolled back")
else:
    env.cr.commit()
    _logger.info("committed")

The script writes a CSV before touching anything, posts a chatter note on each record (the audit trail inside the database), and never commits unless the flag is switched.

docs.title: SQL variant for large volumes
docs.text:
BEGIN;
CREATE TABLE repair_loans_20250101 AS
  SELECT * FROM library_loan WHERE state = 'open' AND date_due < date_out;

UPDATE library_loan SET date_due = date_out
WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM repair_loans_20250101);

-- check, then COMMIT or ROLLBACK
SELECT count(*) FROM library_loan WHERE state = 'open' AND date_due < date_out;

The backup table lets you restore exact old values with a join. Name it with a date and drop it after sign-off.

SQL bypasses constraints, computed fields and the cache. After a SQL update of a field that other stored fields depend on, recompute them through the ORM, or the data is inconsistent.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Fixing and verifying in the same transaction without a fresh query; use a new connection for the check.
  • Repairing in a loop that fires emails and automations. Use tracking_disable and review active automations first.
  • No before-values. If the fix was wrong, you cannot reverse it.
  • Running on production before a copy. The sample you looked at is rarely the full shape of the problem.
  • Not scoping by company in a multi-company database.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text: Create three loans on a test database, set date_due earlier than date_out by SQL on two of them, run the script with DRY_RUN = True, confirm the log says two found and nothing changed, then flip the flag.

docs.title: Extending a standard workflow
docs.text: This blueprint extends sale.order the way a production module should: new fields, a confirmation guard that keeps super() and the state machine intact, a view inheritance anchored on real view ids, a record rule, and a test. The module is sale_extra_checks. The requirement is deliberately small: an order may only be confirmed when a "customer reference" is filled in, if the order's partner is flagged as requiring one.

docs.title: Module layout
docs.text:
sale_extra_checks/
  __manifest__.py
  __init__.py
  models/__init__.py
  models/sale_order.py
  models/res_partner.py
  views/sale_order_views.xml
  security/ir_rules.xml
  tests/__init__.py
  tests/test_confirm.py

# __manifest__.py
{
    'name': 'Sale Extra Checks',
    'version': '18.0.1.0.0',
    'category': 'Sales',
    'depends': ['sale'],
    'data': [
        'security/ir_rules.xml',
        'views/sale_order_views.xml',
    ],
    'license': 'LGPL-3',
}

depends lists sale only. Do not depend on sale_management or account unless you use something from them; every extra dependency is a module your customer must install.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
# models/res_partner.py
from odoo import fields, models


class ResPartner(models.Model):
    _inherit = 'res.partner'

    x_requires_customer_ref = fields.Boolean(
        string="Requires Customer Reference",
        help="Orders for this partner cannot be confirmed without a customer reference.",
    )

# models/sale_order.py
from odoo import _, api, fields, models
from odoo.exceptions import UserError


class SaleOrder(models.Model):
    _inherit = 'sale.order'

    x_customer_ref_required = fields.Boolean(
        compute='_compute_x_customer_ref_required',
        string="Customer Reference Required",
    )
    x_internal_check_note = fields.Text(string="Internal Check Note", copy=False)

    @api.depends('partner_id.commercial_partner_id.x_requires_customer_ref')
    def _compute_x_customer_ref_required(self):
        for order in self:
            order.x_customer_ref_required = (
                order.partner_id.commercial_partner_id.x_requires_customer_ref
            )

The standard client_order_ref field already holds the customer reference on sale.order, so we reuse it instead of adding a duplicate. Check what exists before you add a field: model catalogue.

The computed boolean is non-stored on purpose. It exists to drive required/invisible in the view; storing it would add a column and a recompute chain for no query benefit. See ORM for the trade-offs of stored computes.

Prefix custom fields with x_ only if your team's convention says so; on a module (as opposed to Studio) it is optional, but it keeps your additions greppable next to the standard ones.

docs.title: Overriding the confirm button
docs.text:
The button in the form calls action_confirm (verified in Odoo 18: sale/models/sale_order.py). The standard method first runs _confirmation_error_message() per order, raises UserError if it returns text, then writes the state, locks, and sends mails.

There are two hooks. Pick the lighter one.

    def _confirmation_error_message(self):
        """Return an error string if the order cannot be confirmed."""
        error = super()._confirmation_error_message()
        if error:
            return error
        if self.x_customer_ref_required and not self.client_order_ref:
            return _("This customer requires a customer reference before confirmation.")
        return False

_confirmation_error_message is called inside a for order in self loop in action_confirm, so self is a singleton there. If you override it, return the parent's message first: that preserves the standard checks (state must be draft or sent, every line has a product on non-section lines).

Overriding action_confirm itself is only needed when you must do something after confirmation:

    def action_confirm(self):
        res = super().action_confirm()
        for order in self.filtered(lambda o: o.state == 'sale'):
            order.message_post(body=_("Confirmed with customer reference %s", order.client_order_ref or "-"))
        return res

Rules for this override:

  1. Call super() exactly once and return its result. The return value can be a wizard action (for example when a context key asks for it); dropping it breaks callers.
  2. Never write state yourself. The state machine (draft -> sent -> sale, or cancel) belongs to the standard method; setting state = 'sale' skips locking, analytic validation, the confirmation date, and the mail template.
  3. Filter after super(), not before. The standard method already raised for invalid records, so everything left in self is confirmed.
  4. Operate on the recordset, not on self[0]. The method is also called on multi-record selections from the list view and by automated actions.

Do not raise from action_confirm after calling super(). The transaction rolls back, so nothing persists, but mails and external calls made inside super() may already have fired. Validate before, through the hook.

docs.title: View inheritance
docs.text:
The sales order form is sale.view_order_form (see the view id catalogue). In Odoo 18 the form holds payment_term_id inside the "sale_info" group, and there are two Confirm buttons, one per state, both with name="action_confirm". Because the name is not unique, anchor on a field, not on the button.

<odoo>
    <record id="view_order_form_extra_checks" model="ir.ui.view">
        <field name="name">sale.order.form.extra.checks</field>
        <field name="model">sale.order</field>
        <field name="inherit_id" ref="sale.view_order_form"/>
        <field name="arch" type="xml">

            <!-- 1. make the reference required when the partner demands it -->
            <field name="client_order_ref" position="attributes">
                <attribute name="required">x_customer_ref_required</attribute>
            </field>

            <!-- 2. the computed flag must be present in the view to be usable in a domain/attrs -->
            <field name="partner_id" position="after">
                <field name="x_customer_ref_required" invisible="1"/>
            </field>

            <!-- 3. internal note next to the payment terms -->
            <xpath expr="//field[@name='payment_term_id']" position="after">
                <field name="x_internal_check_note"
                       placeholder="Notes for the team, not shown to the customer"/>
            </xpath>

        </field>
    </record>
</odoo>

Notes:

  • required="x_customer_ref_required" is a Python expression evaluated client-side. Since Odoo 17 the attrs dictionary is gone; use direct attributes (invisible, readonly, required). In 16 you write attrs="{'required': [('x_customer_ref_required', '=', True)]}".
  • A field used in an expression must be in the view. Without the invisible field in step 2 the form raises an error on load.
  • Prefer <field name=... position=...> over a long absolute xpath. When you do need xpath, anchor on @name or @id. The first Confirm button carries id="action_confirm"; the second has no id, so //button[@name='action_confirm'] matches two nodes and Odoo uses the first one. That is silent and wrong half the time.
  • <attribute name="required"> replaces the whole attribute, it does not merge. Check what the parent already sets.

docs.title: Record rule
docs.text:
Requirement: salespeople who are not managers can only see orders of their own teams' partners flagged internal. For the example, a simpler rule: orders with x_internal_check_note set are readable only by sales managers.

<odoo>
    <record id="sale_order_rule_internal_note" model="ir.rule">
        <field name="name">Sale Order: restricted when internal note is set</field>
        <field name="model_id" ref="sale.model_sale_order"/>
        <field name="domain_force">[('x_internal_check_note', '=', False)]</field>
        <field name="groups" eval="[(4, ref('sales_team.group_sale_salesman'))]"/>
        <field name="perm_read" eval="True"/>
        <field name="perm_write" eval="True"/>
        <field name="perm_create" eval="False"/>
        <field name="perm_unlink" eval="True"/>
    </record>
</odoo>

Rules of the same model and group are OR-ed; rules without group are global and AND-ed with everything. The standard rules grant salespeople "all documents" through a group-bound rule (sale.sale_order_personal_rule and sale_order_see_all), so a new group-bound restriction is simply OR-ed with them and does nothing. To really restrict, either make the rule global (no groups) and add an exemption for managers in the domain, or restructure the groups. Test with a user, never as superuser: the superuser bypasses rules entirely.

For a global rule that still lets managers through:

<field name="domain_force">['|', ('x_internal_check_note', '=', False),
    ('user_id', '=', user.id)]</field>

The portal has its own rule on sale.order (sale.sale_order_rule_portal, based on message_partner_ids child_of commercial_partner). Global rules apply to portal users too. A global rule that references internal-only fields can lock customers out of their own orders. See A portal feature.

docs.title: Test
docs.text:
# tests/test_confirm.py
from odoo.exceptions import UserError
from odoo.tests import tagged
from odoo.addons.sale.tests.common import SaleCommon


@tagged('post_install', '-at_install')
class TestConfirmCheck(SaleCommon):

    def test_confirm_blocked_without_reference(self):
        self.partner.x_requires_customer_ref = True
        order = self.empty_order
        order.order_line = [(0, 0, {
            'product_id': self.product.id,
            'product_uom_qty': 1,
        })]
        with self.assertRaises(UserError):
            order.action_confirm()
        self.assertEqual(order.state, 'draft')

    def test_confirm_allowed_with_reference(self):
        self.partner.x_requires_customer_ref = True
        order = self.empty_order
        order.order_line = [(0, 0, {
            'product_id': self.product.id,
            'product_uom_qty': 1,
        })]
        order.client_order_ref = 'REF-001'
        order.action_confirm()
        self.assertEqual(order.state, 'sale')

    def test_flag_not_set_keeps_standard_behaviour(self):
        order = self.empty_order
        order.order_line = [(0, 0, {
            'product_id': self.product.id,
            'product_uom_qty': 1,
        })]
        order.action_confirm()
        self.assertEqual(order.state, 'sale')

SaleCommon ships with partner, product, and empty_order fixtures in 17 and 18. In 16 the equivalent base is sale.tests.common.TestSaleCommon with a different fixture set; adapt the setup rather than copying these names. Note that self.empty_order is created in setUpClass and shared across the class, but each test method runs in a savepoint, so changes roll back.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Overriding action_confirm and writing state directly. You skip locking, mails, and analytic validation.
  • Forgetting super() in a hook such as _confirmation_error_message. All standard checks silently disappear.
  • A non-stored compute used in a search domain or groupby. Add a search= method or store it.
  • required on a field whose value is set by an onchange later in the same save: the client validates before the server round trip.
  • Using //button[@name='action_confirm']. Two matches, first wins.
  • Testing record rules as admin. Use with_user() on a non-superuser.
  • Dropping the return value of super().action_confirm().

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: 16: view modifiers use attrs and states; 17 and 18 use inline Python expressions. The required="expr" form above does not work in 16. action_confirm and the _confirmation_error_message hook exist in 16, 17 and 18. In 16, the test base class and fixtures differ.

docs.text:
Read-only, in a Odoo shell on a development database you own:

env['ir.ui.view'].search([('inherit_id.key', '=', 'sale.view_order_form')]).mapped('name')
env['ir.rule'].search([('model_id.model', '=', 'sale.order')]).mapped('name')

The first lists every view extending the form, including yours. The second shows the rules you must stay compatible with. Then run the tests:

odoo-bin -d dev_db -i sale_extra_checks --test-tags /sale_extra_checks --stop-after-init

docs.text:
# models/book.py
from odoo import api, fields, models


class LibraryBook(models.Model):
    _name = 'library.book'
    _description = 'Book'
    _inherit = ['mail.thread']
    _order = 'name'

    name = fields.Char(required=True, tracking=True)
    isbn = fields.Char(copy=False)
    active = fields.Boolean(default=True)
    loan_ids = fields.One2many('library.loan', 'book_id')
    loan_count = fields.Integer(compute='_compute_loan_count')

    _isbn_unique = models.Constraint('unique(isbn)', 'The ISBN must be unique.')

    @api.depends('loan_ids')
    def _compute_loan_count(self):
        counts = dict(self.env['library.loan']._read_group(
            [('book_id', 'in', self.ids)], ['book_id'], ['__count']))
        for book in self:
            book.loan_count = counts.get(book, 0)

models.Constraint is the 18.0 declaration. On 16.0 and 17.0 use _sql_constraints = [('isbn_unique', 'unique(isbn)', '...')].

# models/loan.py
from odoo import api, fields, models
from odoo.exceptions import ValidationError


class LibraryLoan(models.Model):
    _name = 'library.loan'
    _description = 'Loan'
    _order = 'date_out desc'

    name = fields.Char(default='New', copy=False, readonly=True)
    book_id = fields.Many2one('library.book', required=True, ondelete='restrict')
    member_id = fields.Many2one('res.partner', required=True)
    date_out = fields.Date(default=fields.Date.context_today)
    date_due = fields.Date(required=True)
    date_in = fields.Date()
    state = fields.Selection(
        [('open', 'Open'), ('done', 'Returned')], default='open', required=True)

    @api.model_create_multi
    def create(self, vals_list):
        for vals in vals_list:
            if vals.get('name', 'New') == 'New':
                vals['name'] = self.env['ir.sequence'].next_by_code('library.loan') or 'New'
        return super().create(vals_list)

    @api.constrains('date_out', 'date_due')
    def _check_dates(self):
        for loan in self:
            if loan.date_due < loan.date_out:
                raise ValidationError("The due date cannot precede the loan date.")

    def action_return(self):
        self.write({'state': 'done', 'date_in': fields.Date.context_today(self)})

• A new model without an access line: tests run as superuser and pass, the first normal user fails.

docs.title: A REST integration
docs.text:
This blueprint connects Odoo to an imaginary external service, "acme-shop", that holds orders and customers. It has four parts: an outbound client with timeouts and retries, an inbound webhook controller that verifies an HMAC signature, a mapping model that links Odoo records to remote ids, and a queue drained by a cron. The queue is what keeps a slow or failing remote from blocking users or rolling back their transactions.

The module is acme_connector, depending on base and contacts.

acme_connector/
  __manifest__.py
  __init__.py
  controllers/webhook.py
  models/acme_mapping.py
  models/acme_queue.py
  models/acme_client.py
  models/res_partner.py
  data/cron.xml
  security/ir.model.access.csv
  tests/test_integration.py

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Keep the base URL, token and webhook secret in ir.config_parameter. Never hard-code them, and never put them in a field that ordinary users can read.

# models/acme_client.py
import logging
import time

import requests

from odoo import api, models
from odoo.exceptions import UserError

_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

TIMEOUT = (3.05, 15)           # (connect, read) seconds
RETRY_STATUS = {429, 502, 503, 504}
MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3


class AcmeClient(models.AbstractModel):
    _name = "acme.client"
    _description = "Acme API client"

    @api.model
    def _conf(self, key):
        return self.env["ir.config_parameter"].sudo().get_param(f"acme.{key}") or ""

    @api.model
    def _request(self, method, path, payload=None):
        base = self._conf("base_url").rstrip("/")
        if not base:
            raise UserError(self.env._("The acme base URL is not configured."))
        headers = {
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {self._conf('token')}",
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
        }
        last_exc = None
        for attempt in range(1, MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
            try:
                resp = requests.request(
                    method, f"{base}/{path.lstrip('/')}",
                    json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT,
                )
            except (requests.ConnectionError, requests.Timeout) as exc:
                last_exc = exc
            else:
                if resp.status_code not in RETRY_STATUS:
                    resp.raise_for_status()
                    return resp.json() if resp.content else {}
                last_exc = requests.HTTPError(f"HTTP {resp.status_code}", response=resp)
            _logger.warning("acme %s %s attempt %s failed: %s", method, path, attempt, last_exc)
            if attempt < MAX_ATTEMPTS:
                time.sleep(2 ** (attempt - 1))
        raise last_exc

self.env._() exists in Odoo 18. In 16 and 17 use from odoo import _ and _("...").

Three decisions in that function matter. The timeout is always a tuple: requests has no default timeout, and a stuck remote holds a worker until the worker's hard limit kills it. Only connection errors, timeouts and transient status codes are retried; a 400 or 404 is a bug in your payload and retrying it three times just triples the noise. The sleep is short (1s, 2s) because this code runs inside a worker. Longer backoff belongs in the queue, below.

docs.title: The mapping table
docs.text:
A mapping row says "this Odoo record is that remote object". Do not add x_acme_id fields to every model; one table works for any model and keeps the integration removable.

# models/acme_mapping.py
from odoo import fields, models


class AcmeMapping(models.Model):
    _name = "acme.mapping"
    _description = "Acme record mapping"

    model = fields.Char(required=True, index=True)
    res_id = fields.Many2oneReference(model_field="model", required=True, index=True)
    remote_id = fields.Char(required=True, index=True)
    remote_kind = fields.Char(required=True)       # "customer", "order"
    remote_hash = fields.Char()                    # hash of the last synced payload

    _sql_constraints = [
        ("remote_unique", "unique(remote_kind, remote_id)",
         "A remote object can be mapped only once."),
        ("record_unique", "unique(model, res_id, remote_kind)",
         "A record can be mapped only once per kind."),
    ]

    def _lookup(self, remote_kind, remote_id):
        return self.sudo().search(
            [("remote_kind", "=", remote_kind), ("remote_id", "=", remote_id)], limit=1)

    def _for_record(self, record, remote_kind):
        return self.sudo().search([
            ("model", "=", record._name), ("res_id", "=", record.id),
            ("remote_kind", "=", remote_kind)], limit=1)

_sql_constraints works in 16 to 18 (in 19 it is superseded by models.Constraint; this book does not cover 19 yet). Two unique constraints give you idempotency for free: a replayed webhook cannot create a second customer, it hits the constraint or finds the existing row. The remote_hash column lets you skip writes when nothing changed, which matters for loop prevention.

docs.title: The queue
docs.text:
Do not call the remote from write() or create(). A remote outage would then block saving a partner. Enqueue instead, and let a cron do the call.

# models/acme_queue.py
import hashlib
import json
import logging
from datetime import timedelta

from odoo import api, fields, models

_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
MAX_TRIES = 6


class AcmeQueue(models.Model):
    _name = "acme.queue"
    _description = "Acme outbound queue"
    _order = "id"

    model = fields.Char(required=True)
    res_id = fields.Integer(required=True)
    operation = fields.Selection([("push", "Push")], default="push", required=True)
    state = fields.Selection(
        [("pending", "Pending"), ("done", "Done"), ("failed", "Failed")],
        default="pending", index=True)
    tries = fields.Integer(default=0)
    next_try = fields.Datetime(default=fields.Datetime.now, index=True)
    last_error = fields.Text()

    @api.model
    def enqueue(self, record):
        domain = [("model", "=", record._name), ("res_id", "=", record.id),
                  ("state", "=", "pending")]
        if not self.search_count(domain):          # collapse duplicates
            self.create({"model": record._name, "res_id": record.id})

    @api.model
    def _cron_process(self, batch=50):
        jobs = self.search(
            [("state", "=", "pending"), ("next_try", "<=", fields.Datetime.now())],
            limit=batch)
        for job in jobs:
            try:
                with self.env.cr.savepoint():
                    job._run()
                job.write({"state": "done", "last_error": False})
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - queue must survive anything
                tries = job.tries + 1
                _logger.warning("acme job %s failed (%s): %s", job.id, tries, exc)
                job.write({
                    "tries": tries,
                    "last_error": str(exc),
                    "state": "failed" if tries >= MAX_TRIES else "pending",
                    "next_try": fields.Datetime.now() + timedelta(minutes=2 ** tries),
                })
            self.env.cr.commit()   # keep what we finished if a later job kills the worker
        if len(jobs) == batch:
            self.env.ref("acme_connector.ir_cron_acme_queue")._trigger()

    def _run(self):
        self.ensure_one()
        record = self.env[self.model].browse(self.res_id).exists()
        if not record:
            return
        payload = record._acme_payload()
        digest = hashlib.sha256(
            json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
        mapping = self.env["acme.mapping"]._for_record(record, record._acme_kind)
        if mapping and mapping.remote_hash == digest:
            return                                   # nothing changed, nothing to send
        client = self.env["acme.client"]
        if mapping:
            client._request("PUT", f"{record._acme_kind}s/{mapping.remote_id}", payload)
            mapping.remote_hash = digest
        else:
            data = client._request("POST", f"{record._acme_kind}s", payload)
            self.env["acme.mapping"].sudo().create({
                "model": record._name, "res_id": record.id,
                "remote_id": str(data["id"]), "remote_kind": record._acme_kind,
                "remote_hash": digest,
            })

The explicit commit() is allowed in cron code and is what you want here: after a successful remote call the mapping must be saved, otherwise the next run creates a duplicate remote object. The remote call itself cannot be rolled back, so keep the window between "remote succeeded" and "commit" as small as possible. _trigger() re-schedules the cron for an immediate run when the batch was full (it exists in 16 to 18).

The cron record:

<!-- data/cron.xml -->
<odoo noupdate="1">
  <record id="ir_cron_acme_queue" model="ir.cron">
    <field name="name">Acme: process outbound queue</field>
    <field name="model_id" ref="model_acme_queue"/>
    <field name="state">code</field>
    <field name="code">model._cron_process()</field>
    <field name="interval_number">5</field>
    <field name="interval_type">minutes</field>
  </record>
</odoo>

Odoo 16 and 17 cron records usually carry numbercall (-1) and sometimes doall. The Odoo 18 source I checked no longer has those fields on ir.cron; drop them there, keep them in older versions.

docs.title: Hooking the model
docs.text:
# models/res_partner.py
from odoo import api, models

SYNC_FIELDS = {"name", "email", "phone", "street", "city", "zip", "country_id"}


class ResPartner(models.Model):
    _inherit = "res.partner"
    _acme_kind = "customer"

    def _acme_payload(self):
        self.ensure_one()
        return {"name": self.name, "email": self.email or None,
                "phone": self.phone or None, "city": self.city or None}

    @api.model_create_multi
    def create(self, vals_list):
        partners = super().create(vals_list)
        if not self.env.context.get("acme_no_sync"):
            for partner in partners:
                self.env["acme.queue"].sudo().enqueue(partner)
        return partners

    def write(self, vals):
        res = super().write(vals)
        if SYNC_FIELDS & set(vals) and not self.env.context.get("acme_no_sync"):
            for partner in self:
                self.env["acme.queue"].sudo().enqueue(partner)
        return res

docs.title: Inbound webhook with HMAC
docs.text:
The remote signs the raw body with a shared secret and sends the hex digest in a header. Verify against the raw bytes, not against re-serialised JSON: key order and whitespace would change the digest.

# controllers/webhook.py
import hmac
import hashlib
import json
import logging

from odoo import http
from odoo.http import request

_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class AcmeWebhook(http.Controller):

    @http.route("/acme/webhook", type="http", auth="public", methods=["POST"],
                csrf=False)
    def webhook(self):
        body = request.httprequest.get_data()
        secret = request.env["acme.client"].sudo()._conf("webhook_secret")
        given = request.httprequest.headers.get("X-Acme-Signature", "")
        expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
        if not secret or not hmac.compare_digest(given, expected):
            return request.make_response("forbidden", status=403)
        try:
            event = json.loads(body)
        except ValueError:
            return request.make_response("bad json", status=400)
        self._handle(event)
        return request.make_response("ok", status=200)

    def _handle(self, event):
        env = request.env(su=True)
        env = env(context=dict(env.context, acme_no_sync=True))
        if event.get("type") != "customer.updated":
            return
        data = event["data"]
        mapping = env["acme.mapping"]._lookup("customer", str(data["id"]))
        vals = {"name": data["name"], "email": data.get("email")}
        if mapping:
            env["res.partner"].browse(mapping.res_id).write(vals)
        else:
            partner = env["res.partner"].create(vals)
            env["acme.mapping"].create({
                "model": "res.partner", "res_id": partner.id,
                "remote_id": str(data["id"]), "remote_kind": "customer"})

auth="public" is correct here: the signature is the authentication. request.env(su=True) is the Odoo 16 to 18 spelling for a superuser environment. Use hmac.compare_digest, never ==, to avoid timing leaks.

Return quickly. If the event needs heavy work, create a queue row of another operation and answer 200; remote senders retry on timeouts and you will receive the same event twice.

docs.title: Loop prevention
docs.text:
Without care, the flow is: remote update, webhook writes the partner, write() enqueues, cron pushes back, remote fires another webhook. Three layers stop it:

  1. The webhook writes with acme_no_sync=True, so it never enqueues.
  2. The queue compares the payload hash with mapping.remote_hash and skips unchanged data. After an inbound write, also store the hash so the next outbound run is a no-op.
  3. enqueue collapses duplicate pending jobs.

Layer 1 alone is not enough if the remote echoes changes caused by your own PUT; layer 2 is the one that ends the loop.

docs.title: Tests with mocked HTTP
docs.text:
Never let tests reach the network. Patch requests.request where the client uses it.

# tests/test_integration.py
import hashlib
import hmac
import json
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from odoo.tests import HttpCase, TransactionCase, tagged


def _response(status=200, data=None):
    resp = MagicMock()
    resp.status_code = status
    resp.content = b"x"
    resp.json.return_value = data or {}
    resp.raise_for_status.side_effect = None
    return resp


@tagged("post_install", "-at_install")
class TestAcmeQueue(TransactionCase):

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        params = self.env["ir.config_parameter"].sudo()
        params.set_param("acme.base_url", "https://acme.invalid/api")
        params.set_param("acme.token", "t")

    @patch("odoo.addons.acme_connector.models.acme_client.requests.request")
    def test_push_creates_mapping(self, mock_req):
        mock_req.return_value = _response(201, {"id": 42})
        partner = self.env["res.partner"].create({"name": "Test Customer"})
        self.env["acme.queue"]._cron_process()
        mapping = self.env["acme.mapping"]._for_record(partner, "customer")
        self.assertEqual(mapping.remote_id, "42")
        mock_req.assert_called_once()

    @patch("odoo.addons.acme_connector.models.acme_client.time.sleep")
    @patch("odoo.addons.acme_connector.models.acme_client.requests.request")
    def test_transient_error_is_retried(self, mock_req, _sleep):
        mock_req.side_effect = [_response(503), _response(200, {"id": 7})]
        data = self.env["acme.client"]._request("POST", "customers", {})
        self.assertEqual(data["id"], 7)
        self.assertEqual(mock_req.call_count, 2)

    @patch("odoo.addons.acme_connector.models.acme_client.requests.request")
    def test_unchanged_payload_is_not_resent(self, mock_req):
        mock_req.return_value = _response(201, {"id": 1})
        partner = self.env["res.partner"].create({"name": "Test Customer"})
        self.env["acme.queue"]._cron_process()
        self.env["acme.queue"].enqueue(partner)
        self.env["acme.queue"]._cron_process()
        self.assertEqual(mock_req.call_count, 1)


@tagged("post_install", "-at_install")
class TestAcmeWebhook(HttpCase):

    def _post(self, payload, secret="s3cret", sign=True):
        body = json.dumps(payload).encode()
        headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
        if sign:
            headers["X-Acme-Signature"] = hmac.new(
                secret.encode(), body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
        return self.url_open("/acme/webhook", data=body, headers=headers)

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.env["ir.config_parameter"].sudo().set_param("acme.webhook_secret", "s3cret")

    def test_rejects_bad_signature(self):
        self.assertEqual(self._post({"type": "x"}, secret="wrong").status_code, 403)

    def test_creates_partner_without_enqueue(self):
        event = {"type": "customer.updated", "data": {"id": 9, "name": "Webhook Customer"}}
        self.assertEqual(self._post(event).status_code, 200)
        partner = self.env["res.partner"].search([("name", "=", "Webhook Customer")])
        self.assertEqual(len(partner), 1)
        self.assertFalse(self.env["acme.queue"].search([("res_id", "=", partner.id)]))

Note one catch: a TransactionCase test calls _cron_process, which calls self.env.cr.commit(). In tests the cursor is a test cursor and commit() is neutralised, so this is safe. Keep it that way: do not open your own cursors in this code.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• No timeout. The most common integration bug. A hung socket holds a worker until the limit kills the request and everything it did.
  • Calling the remote inside write(). Outage on their side becomes "cannot save" on yours, and a rollback after a successful call leaves the remote ahead of Odoo.
  • Verifying the signature on parsed JSON. The digest will not match reliably. Hash the raw bytes.
  • Comparing signatures with ==. Use hmac.compare_digest.
  • Trusting remote ids as unique per kind. Different kinds can reuse the same id; that is why the mapping key includes remote_kind.
  • Webhook handlers that are not idempotent. Senders retry. Look up the mapping first.
  • Retrying non-transient errors. A 422 will never succeed; mark the job failed and surface last_error to a human.
  • Forgetting multi-worker races. Two cron runs cannot overlap on the same job because ir.cron locks its own row, but a webhook and the cron can touch the same partner; the unique constraints turn that race into an error rather than a duplicate.

docs.text:

psql testdb -c "select state, count(*) from acme_queue group by state"
