docs.title: Spreadsheet import
docs.text:
The built-in import screen is fine for admins who know the field names. It is the wrong tool when a customer sends a file in their own format and expects a clear answer: which rows are wrong, why, and what will be created. This blueprint builds a wizard that uploads a CSV or XLSX, validates every row into a preview with per-row errors, and only then creates records in batches, each batch protected by a savepoint.

The example imports contacts into res.partner from columns name, email, phone, country (ISO code) and vat. Module name: partner_import, depending on base.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
Two models:

  • partner.import.wizard (transient): holds the file, the options, and the state (upload, preview, done).
  • partner.import.line (transient): one row per parsed input row with its values, its error text and its status.

Validation and creation are separate steps. Validation never writes business records, so it is safe to repeat. Creation re-reads the preview lines, not the file, so what the user saw is what gets created.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
# models/import_wizard.py
import base64
import csv
import io
import logging

from odoo import api, fields, models
from odoo.exceptions import UserError

_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

COLUMNS = ["name", "email", "phone", "country", "vat"]
BATCH = 100


class PartnerImportWizard(models.TransientModel):
    _name = "partner.import.wizard"
    _description = "Partner import wizard"

    file = fields.Binary(required=True, attachment=False)
    filename = fields.Char()
    state = fields.Selection(
        [("upload", "Upload"), ("preview", "Preview"), ("done", "Done")],
        default="upload")
    line_ids = fields.One2many("partner.import.line", "wizard_id")
    valid_count = fields.Integer(compute="_compute_counts")
    error_count = fields.Integer(compute="_compute_counts")
    created_count = fields.Integer()
    skip_errors = fields.Boolean(
        string="Import valid rows only",
        help="If unchecked, nothing is created while any row has an error.")

    @api.depends("line_ids.error")
    def _compute_counts(self):
        for wiz in self:
            wiz.error_count = len(wiz.line_ids.filtered("error"))
            wiz.valid_count = len(wiz.line_ids) - wiz.error_count

    # -- parsing -----------------------------------------------------------

    def _read_rows(self):
        """Return a list of dicts keyed by lower-cased header."""
        self.ensure_one()
        raw = base64.b64decode(self.file)
        name = (self.filename or "").lower()
        if name.endswith(".xlsx"):
            return self._read_xlsx(raw)
        return self._read_csv(raw)

    def _read_csv(self, raw):
        try:
            text = raw.decode("utf-8-sig")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            text = raw.decode("latin-1")
        try:
            dialect = csv.Sniffer().sniff(text[:4096], delimiters=",;\t")
        except csv.Error:
            dialect = csv.excel
        reader = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text), dialect=dialect)
        if not reader.fieldnames:
            raise UserError(self.env._("The file is empty."))
        return [
            {(k or "").strip().lower(): (v or "").strip() for k, v in row.items()}
            for row in reader
        ]

    def _read_xlsx(self, raw):
        try:
            import openpyxl
        except ImportError:
            raise UserError(self.env._("XLSX support needs the openpyxl library."))
        book = openpyxl.load_workbook(io.BytesIO(raw), read_only=True, data_only=True)
        sheet = book.active
        rows = sheet.iter_rows(values_only=True)
        header = next(rows, None)
        if not header:
            raise UserError(self.env._("The file is empty."))
        keys = [str(h or "").strip().lower() for h in header]
        out = []
        for values in rows:
            if all(v in (None, "") for v in values):
                continue
            out.append({k: ("" if v is None else str(v).strip())
                        for k, v in zip(keys, values)})
        return out

    # -- step 1: validate ---------------------------------------------------

    def action_validate(self):
        self.ensure_one()
        rows = self._read_rows()
        if not rows:
            raise UserError(self.env._("The file has no data rows."))
        missing = [c for c in ("name",) if c not in rows[0]]
        if missing:
            raise UserError(self.env._(
                "Missing required column(s): %s", ", ".join(missing)))

        countries = {c.code: c.id for c in self.env["res.country"].search([])}
        existing = set(self.env["res.partner"].search(
            [("email", "!=", False)]).mapped(lambda p: (p.email or "").lower()))
        seen = set()
        self.line_ids.unlink()
        vals_list = []
        for number, row in enumerate(rows, start=2):   # row 1 is the header
            errors = []
            name = row.get("name", "")
            email = row.get("email", "").lower()
            code = row.get("country", "").upper()
            if not name:
                errors.append(self.env._("Name is required."))
            if email and "@" not in email:
                errors.append(self.env._("Invalid email."))
            if email in seen:
                errors.append(self.env._("Duplicate email in the file."))
            elif email and email in existing:
                errors.append(self.env._("A contact with this email already exists."))
            if code and code not in countries:
                errors.append(self.env._("Unknown country code %s.", code))
            if email:
                seen.add(email)
            vals_list.append({
                "wizard_id": self.id,
                "row_number": number,
                "name": name,
                "email": email,
                "phone": row.get("phone", ""),
                "country_id": countries.get(code),
                "vat": row.get("vat", ""),
                "error": "\n".join(errors) or False,
            })
        self.env["partner.import.line"].create(vals_list)
        self.state = "preview"
        return self._reopen()

    # -- step 2: create -----------------------------------------------------

    def action_import(self):
        self.ensure_one()
        if self.error_count and not self.skip_errors:
            raise UserError(self.env._(
                "%s row(s) have errors. Fix the file, or tick "
                "'Import valid rows only'.", self.error_count))
        lines = self.line_ids.filtered(lambda l: not l.error and not l.partner_id)
        created = 0
        for start in range(0, len(lines), BATCH):
            batch = lines[start:start + BATCH]
            created += self._import_batch(batch)
        self.write({"created_count": created, "state": "done"})
        return self._reopen()

    def _import_batch(self, batch):
        """Create one batch. On failure, retry row by row to isolate the bad one."""
        try:
            with self.env.cr.savepoint():
                self._create_partners(batch)
            return len(batch)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            _logger.info("batch failed, falling back to row-by-row", exc_info=True)
        done = 0
        for line in batch:
            try:
                with self.env.cr.savepoint():
                    self._create_partners(line)
                done += 1
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                line.error = str(exc)
        return done

    def _create_partners(self, lines):
        partners = self.env["res.partner"].create([{
            "name": l.name,
            "email": l.email or False,
            "phone": l.phone or False,
            "country_id": l.country_id.id,
            "vat": l.vat or False,
        } for l in lines])
        for line, partner in zip(lines, partners):
            line.partner_id = partner

    def _reopen(self):
        return {
            "type": "ir.actions.act_window",
            "res_model": self._name,
            "res_id": self.id,
            "view_mode": "form",
            "target": "new",
        }

    def action_back(self):
        self.line_ids.unlink()
        self.state = "upload"
        return self._reopen()


class PartnerImportLine(models.TransientModel):
    _name = "partner.import.line"
    _description = "Partner import preview line"
    _order = "row_number"

    wizard_id = fields.Many2one("partner.import.wizard", ondelete="cascade", required=True)
    row_number = fields.Integer()
    name = fields.Char()
    email = fields.Char()
    phone = fields.Char()
    country_id = fields.Many2one("res.country")
    vat = fields.Char()
    error = fields.Text()
    partner_id = fields.Many2one("res.partner")

# models/__init__.py
from . import import_wizard

docs.text:
<!-- views/import_wizard_views.xml -->
<odoo>
  <record id="partner_import_wizard_form" model="ir.ui.view">
    <field name="name">partner.import.wizard.form</field>
    <field name="model">partner.import.wizard</field>
    <field name="arch" type="xml">
      <form>
        <field name="state" invisible="1"/>
        <group invisible="state != 'upload'">
          <field name="file" filename="filename"/>
          <field name="filename" invisible="1"/>
        </group>
        <group invisible="state != 'preview'">
          <field name="valid_count"/>
          <field name="error_count"/>
          <field name="skip_errors" invisible="error_count == 0"/>
        </group>
        <group invisible="state != 'done'">
          <field name="created_count"/>
        </group>
        <field name="line_ids" invisible="state == 'upload'" readonly="1">
          <list decoration-danger="error" decoration-success="partner_id">
            <field name="row_number"/>
            <field name="name"/>
            <field name="email"/>
            <field name="country_id"/>
            <field name="error"/>
            <field name="partner_id" optional="hide"/>
          </list>
        </field>
        <footer>
          <button string="Validate" type="object" name="action_validate"
                  class="btn-primary" invisible="state != 'upload'"/>
          <button string="Import" type="object" name="action_import"
                  class="btn-primary" invisible="state != 'preview'"/>
          <button string="Back" type="object" name="action_back"
                  invisible="state != 'preview'"/>
          <button string="Close" special="cancel"/>
        </footer>
      </form>
    </field>
  </record>

  <record id="partner_import_wizard_action" model="ir.actions.act_window">
    <field name="name">Import contacts</field>
    <field name="res_model">partner.import.wizard</field>
    <field name="view_mode">form</field>
    <field name="target">new</field>
  </record>

  <menuitem id="menu_partner_import" name="Import contacts"
            parent="contacts.menu_contacts" action="partner_import_wizard_action"/>
</odoo>

The <list> tag and bare invisible="state != 'upload'" expressions are Odoo 17 and 18 syntax. In Odoo 16 the tag is <tree> and conditions are written attrs="{'invisible': [('state', '!=', 'upload')]}". Add contacts to the manifest depends for the menu parent.

Access rights: transient models need no ir.model.access.csv rows in 16 to 18, but the user opening the wizard needs create rights on res.partner. Restrict the menu with groups="base.group_system" or a dedicated group if only some users may import.

docs.title: Test
docs.text:
# tests/test_import.py
import base64

from odoo.tests import TransactionCase, tagged

CSV = (
    "name,email,phone,country,vat\n"
    "Test One,one@example.test,111,BE,\n"
    ",missing@example.test,,BE,\n"
    "Test Three,bad-email,,XX,\n"
    "Test Four,one@example.test,,,\n"
)


@tagged("post_install", "-at_install")
class TestPartnerImport(TransactionCase):

    def _wizard(self, text=CSV):
        return self.env["partner.import.wizard"].create({
            "file": base64.b64encode(text.encode()),
            "filename": "contacts.csv",
        })

    def test_validation_reports_each_error(self):
        wiz = self._wizard()
        wiz.action_validate()
        self.assertEqual(wiz.valid_count, 1)
        self.assertEqual(wiz.error_count, 3)
        by_row = {l.row_number: l.error for l in wiz.line_ids}
        self.assertIn("Name is required", by_row[3])
        self.assertIn("Unknown country", by_row[4])
        self.assertIn("Duplicate email", by_row[5])

    def test_blocks_when_errors_unless_skipping(self):
        wiz = self._wizard()
        wiz.action_validate()
        with self.assertRaises(Exception):
            wiz.action_import()
        wiz.skip_errors = True
        wiz.action_import()
        self.assertEqual(wiz.created_count, 1)
        self.assertTrue(self.env["res.partner"].search([("email", "=", "one@example.test")]))

    def test_bad_row_does_not_lose_batch(self):
        wiz = self._wizard("name,email\nTest A,a@example.test\nTest B,b@example.test\n")
        wiz.action_validate()
        original = type(wiz)._create_partners

        def flaky(self_, lines):
            if lines[:1].name == "Test B" or len(lines) > 1:
                raise ValueError("boom")
            return original(self_, lines)

        type(wiz)._create_partners = flaky
        try:
            wiz.action_import()
        finally:
            type(wiz)._create_partners = original
        self.assertEqual(wiz.created_count, 1)
        self.assertEqual(wiz.line_ids.filtered("error").mapped("name"), ["Test B"])

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Encoding. Spreadsheet exports from desktop tools are often cp1252 or UTF-8 with a BOM. utf-8-sig strips the BOM; the latin-1 fallback never fails, so check names visually in the preview.
  • Delimiter. Many locales export ;. csv.Sniffer can guess wrong on tiny files; fall back to csv.excel as above and show the preview so a wrong split is visible.
  • XLSX types. str(v) turns the number 1234 into 1234 but a float cell into 1234.0, and dates into datetime strings. Format-sensitive columns (phone, VAT, codes) should be text cells, or parse them explicitly.
  • Validating against a stale state. The preview is computed at one moment. The import step creates rows later; a unique constraint may still fire. That is why the batch falls back to row-by-row inside savepoints.
  • A savepoint is not a commit. If the whole request fails after the loop, everything rolls back, including batches that "succeeded". For very large files, commit between batches in a cron or a queue (see the REST blueprint) rather than in the wizard.
  • Memory and time. A request has a time limit. Beyond a few thousand rows, store the file in an attachment and process it from a cron, reporting progress on a record.
  • Transient cleanup. Wizard and line records are vacuumed by ir.autovacuum; do not keep anything you need as an audit trail in them. Log the result to the chatter or a real model if you must.
  • Open-ended except Exception. Acceptable around a savepoint where you record the message per row; never elsewhere.
  • mapped(lambda ...) on all partners with an email loads every partner. For a big database, query only the emails present in the file with search_read([("email", "in", emails)], ["email"]).

docs.title: A wizard with a PDF report
docs.text:
A wizard asks the user for parameters, a report turns data into a document. Together they are the most common "small feature" in Odoo: pick a date range and a member, press Print, get a PDF. This blueprint builds one on the neutral library module, file by file, for Odoo 18. Each file is complete; add them to the manifest in the order shown.

The feature: Loan summary. The user opens Library > Reports > Loan summary, chooses a date range and optionally a member, and receives a PDF listing the loans in that range, grouped by member, with a count of overdue ones.

docs.title: Assumed starting point
docs.text:
The module already has two models. Shown here so the rest is checkable.

# library/models/library_book.py
from odoo import fields, models


class LibraryBook(models.Model):
    _name = 'library.book'
    _description = 'Book'

    name = fields.Char(required=True)
    isbn = fields.Char()

# library/models/library_loan.py
from odoo import api, fields, models


class LibraryLoan(models.Model):
    _name = 'library.loan'
    _description = 'Book loan'
    _order = 'date_loan desc, id desc'

    book_id = fields.Many2one('library.book', required=True, ondelete='restrict')
    member_id = fields.Many2one('res.partner', string='Member', required=True)
    date_loan = fields.Date(required=True, default=fields.Date.context_today)
    date_due = fields.Date(required=True)
    date_return = fields.Date()
    is_overdue = fields.Boolean(compute='_compute_is_overdue', store=True)

    @api.depends('date_due', 'date_return')
    def _compute_is_overdue(self):
        today = fields.Date.context_today(self)
        for loan in self:
            loan.is_overdue = not loan.date_return and loan.date_due < today

is_overdue is stored but depends on today's date, so it goes stale at midnight. For a report it is cleaner to compute overdue in the report code, as done below. The stored field is kept here only because other chapters use it.

docs.text:
# library/__manifest__.py
{
    'name': 'Library',
    'version': '18.0.1.0.0',
    'depends': ['base', 'web'],
    'license': 'LGPL-3',

Order matters: the wizard view defines the action the menu points to, and the menu file loads last. web provides the report layouts (web.external_layout, web.html_container).

docs.title: The wizard model
docs.text:
A wizard is a TransientModel: a normal model whose rows are temporary and vacuumed automatically. It holds the form's field values and the button's logic.

# library/wizard/loan_summary_wizard.py
from odoo import api, fields, models
from odoo.exceptions import UserError


class LoanSummaryWizard(models.TransientModel):
    _name = 'library.loan.summary.wizard'
    _description = 'Loan summary wizard'

    date_from = fields.Date(
        string='From', required=True,
        default=lambda self: fields.Date.context_today(self).replace(day=1),
    )
    date_to = fields.Date(
        string='To', required=True,
        default=fields.Date.context_today,
    )
    member_ids = fields.Many2many(
        'res.partner', string='Members',
        help='Leave empty to include every member.',
    )
    only_overdue = fields.Boolean(string='Only overdue')

    @api.constrains('date_from', 'date_to')
    def _check_dates(self):
        for wiz in self:
            if wiz.date_from > wiz.date_to:
                raise UserError(self.env._("The start date must not be after the end date."))

    def _get_loan_domain(self):
        self.ensure_one()
        domain = [
            ('date_loan', '>=', self.date_from),
            ('date_loan', '<=', self.date_to),
        ]
        if self.member_ids:
            domain.append(('member_id', 'in', self.member_ids.ids))
        if self.only_overdue:
            domain += [('date_return', '=', False),
                       ('date_due', '<', fields.Date.context_today(self))]
        return domain

    def action_print(self):
        self.ensure_one()
        loans = self.env['library.loan'].search(self._get_loan_domain())
        if not loans:
            raise UserError(self.env._("No loans match the selected criteria."))
        data = {
            'date_from': self.date_from,
            'date_to': self.date_to,
            'loan_ids': loans.ids,
        }
        return self.env.ref('library.action_report_loan_summary').report_action(
            loans, data=data,
        )

# library/wizard/__init__.py
from . import loan_summary_wizard

# library/__init__.py
from . import models
from . import wizard
from . import report

Notes:

  • report_action(docs, data=...) returns a client action dictionary. The wizard does not render anything itself; it hands the client a URL to fetch the PDF from.
  • The wizard searches once and passes ids. The report must not search again with different criteria, or the PDF and the validation ("no loans match") can disagree.
  • self.env._() is the Odoo 18 shorthand for translation. In 16 and 17 import and use from odoo import _ and _("...").

<!-- library/report/loan_summary_report.xml -->
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<odoo>
    <record id="action_report_loan_summary" model="ir.actions.report">
        <field name="name">Loan summary</field>
        <field name="model">library.loan</field>
        <field name="report_type">qweb-pdf</field>
        <field name="report_name">library.report_loan_summary</field>

No binding_model_id, deliberately. Setting it would add this report to the Print menu of every loan list, where it would run without the wizard's parameters. Reports reached only through a wizard stay unbound.

report_name is <module>.<template id>, and it also names the abstract model that supplies the data: report.library.report_loan_summary.

docs.title: The data provider
docs.text:
# library/report/loan_summary_report.py
from collections import defaultdict

from odoo import api, fields, models


class ReportLoanSummary(models.AbstractModel):
    _name = 'report.library.report_loan_summary'
    _description = 'Loan summary report'

    @api.model
    def _get_report_values(self, docids, data=None):
        data = data or {}
        loans = self.env['library.loan'].browse(data.get('loan_ids') or docids).exists()
        today = fields.Date.context_today(self)

        by_member = defaultdict(lambda: self.env['library.loan'])
        for loan in loans:
            by_member[loan.member_id] |= loan

        groups = []
        for member, member_loans in sorted(by_member.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[0].name or ''):
            overdue = member_loans.filtered(
                lambda l: not l.date_return and l.date_due < today
            )
            groups.append({
                'member': member,
                'loans': member_loans,
                'overdue_count': len(overdue),
            })

        return {
            'doc_ids': loans.ids,
            'doc_model': 'library.loan',
            'docs': loans,
            'date_from': data.get('date_from'),
            'date_to': data.get('date_to'),
            'groups': groups,
            'today': today,
            'total': len(loans),
        }

# library/report/__init__.py
from . import loan_summary_report

If the abstract model is missing, Odoo falls back to rendering the template with just docs for the selected records. That is fine for simple documents; here we need the grouping, so we provide the model. Passing data through report_action is what lets the PDF reflect the wizard's choice instead of whatever was highlighted in a list.

docs.title: The QWeb template
docs.text:
<!-- library/report/loan_summary_templates.xml -->
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<odoo>
    <template id="report_loan_summary">
        <t t-call="web.html_container">
            <t t-call="web.external_layout">
                <div class="page">
                    <h2>Loan summary</h2>
                    <p>
                        Period:
                        <span t-out="date_from" t-options="{'widget': 'date'}"/>
                        to
                        <span t-out="date_to" t-options="{'widget': 'date'}"/>
                        — <span t-out="total"/> loans
                    </p>

                    <t t-foreach="groups" t-as="group">
                        <h4 class="mt-4">
                            <span t-out="group['member'].display_name"/>
                            <small t-if="group['overdue_count']" class="text-danger">
                                (<span t-out="group['overdue_count']"/> overdue)
                            </small>
                        </h4>
                        <table class="table table-sm o_main_table">
                            <thead>
                                <tr>
                                    <th>Book</th>
                                    <th>Loaned</th>
                                    <th>Due</th>
                                    <th>Returned</th>
                                </tr>
                            </thead>
                            <tbody>
                                <tr t-foreach="group['loans']" t-as="loan">
                                    <td><span t-field="loan.book_id.name"/></td>
                                    <td><span t-field="loan.date_loan"/></td>
                                    <td><span t-field="loan.date_due"/></td>
                                    <td><span t-field="loan.date_return"/></td>
                                </tr>
                            </tbody>
                        </table>
                    </t>
                </div>
            </t>
        </t>
    </template>
</odoo>

t-field renders a record field with the user's formatting and language and respects access rights; use it for record fields. t-out prints a plain value and is what you use for computed numbers and dictionary values. t-esc is the older name for t-out.

Versions: t-out replaced t-esc in 15 and both work in 16 to 18. The <list> tag replaced <tree> for list views in 18; the form used here is unaffected. Inline invisible="..." expressions replaced attrs in 17, so a 16 port of a form that hides fields must use attrs.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
id,name,model_id:id,group_id:id,perm_read,perm_write,perm_create,perm_unlink
access_library_loan_user,library.loan user,model_library_loan,library.group_library_user,1,0,0,0
access_library_loan_manager,library.loan manager,model_library_loan,library.group_library_manager,1,1,1,1

Save as library/security/ir.model.access.csv. Notes:

  • Transient models need no access line since Odoo 14: any internal user may create and read their own wizard rows. A line for library.loan.summary.wizard is not required and the file above omits it. In 12 and earlier one was needed.
  • The report reads library.loan as the printing user, so that user needs read access on loans and on res.partner. The menu is limited to the manager group, but the report URL itself is checked by the same ACLs, not by the menu.
  • The abstract report model has no table and no ACL.

The groups themselves live in security/library_security.xml (define group_library_user and group_library_manager there and list the file before the CSV in data).

docs.title: The test
docs.text:
# library/tests/test_loan_summary.py
from odoo.exceptions import UserError
from odoo.fields import Date
from odoo.tests import TransactionCase, tagged


@tagged('post_install', '-at_install')
class TestLoanSummary(TransactionCase):

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        super().setUpClass()
        cls.member = cls.env['res.partner'].create({'name': 'Test Member'})
        cls.book = cls.env['library.book'].create({'name': 'Test Book'})
        cls.loan = cls.env['library.loan'].create({
            'book_id': cls.book.id,
            'member_id': cls.member.id,
            'date_loan': '2025-01-10',
            'date_due': '2025-01-24',
        })

    def _wizard(self, **vals):
        base = {'date_from': '2025-01-01', 'date_to': '2025-01-31'}
        return self.env['library.loan.summary.wizard'].create({**base, **vals})

    def test_print_returns_report_action(self):
        action = self._wizard().action_print()
        self.assertEqual(action['type'], 'ir.actions.report')
        self.assertEqual(action['report_name'], 'library.report_loan_summary')
        self.assertEqual(action['data']['loan_ids'], self.loan.ids)

    def test_no_matches_raises(self):
        wiz = self._wizard(date_from='2024-01-01', date_to='2024-01-31')
        with self.assertRaises(UserError):
            wiz.action_print()

    def test_bad_dates_raise(self):
        with self.assertRaises(UserError):
            self._wizard(date_from='2025-02-01', date_to='2025-01-01')

    def test_report_values_group_by_member(self):
        wiz = self._wizard()
        data = wiz.action_print()['data']
        values = self.env['report.library.report_loan_summary']._get_report_values(
            self.loan.ids, data=data)
        self.assertEqual(values['total'], 1)
        self.assertEqual(values['groups'][0]['member'], self.member)
        self.assertEqual(values['groups'][0]['overdue_count'], 1)

    def test_pdf_renders(self):
        report = self.env.ref('library.action_report_loan_summary')
        html = report._render_qweb_html(
            report.report_name, self.loan.ids,
            data=self._wizard().action_print()['data'])[0]
        self.assertIn(b'Test Member', html)

# library/tests/__init__.py
from . import test_loan_summary

Run it:

odoo-bin -d test_db -i library --test-tags /library --stop-after-init

The test renders HTML, not PDF. Producing a real PDF needs wkhtmltopdf, which test databases often lack; HTML rendering exercises the template and the data provider, which is where the bugs are.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• The report shows records from a stale selection. If you omit data and rely on docids, the PDF reflects whatever the click carried, not the wizard criteria. Pass ids in data and read them in _get_report_values.
  • report_name mismatch. The abstract model name must be exactly report. plus report_name. A typo gives no error: Odoo silently falls back to the default values and your groups variable is undefined in the template.
  • Template renders in HTML but PDF is blank or missing styles. wkhtmltopdf fetches assets through web.base.url. Behind a proxy or with a wrong web.base.url the layout loses its CSS. Check the system parameter before debugging the template.
  • Heavy search inside the template. QWeb has no query planning. Compute in the provider, iterate in the template.
  • Wizard fields stored in the PDF by accident. Transient rows are vacuumed after a while; never reference a wizard record from a long-lived record.
  • Report bound to the model by habit. binding_model_id on a wizard-driven report exposes it with no parameters.
  • Constraints on wizard fields that need the user's context. @api.constrains runs on create as well as write; raising there blocks the dialog before Print is pressed, which is usually what you want.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
• 16: use from odoo import _; hide fields with attrs="{'invisible': [...]}" in forms; list views use <tree>.
  • 17: invisible="expr" replaces attrs; <tree> still used for list views.
  • 18: <list> is the list view tag; self.env._() is available for translation; the report engine and report_action are unchanged.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text: Add a group_by field to the wizard (selection with member and book), branch on it in _get_report_values, and add a test for each branch. Then open the report as HTML without a PDF engine by visiting /report/html/library.report_loan_summary/<loan id> while logged in, which is quicker for iterating on layout.

• search without limit on a large table inside a loop.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Action. A record telling the client what to open: a window action (ir.actions.act_window), a report, a server action, or a URL.

Addon / module. A directory with a __manifest__.py that adds models, views, data or code. Used interchangeably in this book.

Addons path. The list of directories Odoo scans for modules, set by addons_path.

Aggregate. In _read_group, a string like 'fee:sum' or '__count' computed per group.

Batch (create). A call to create with a list of value dicts, handled by @api.model_create_multi.

Chatter. The message and activity panel from mail.thread.

Command. A tuple-like helper (Command.create, Command.link, and others) used to write x2many fields.

Computed field. A field filled by a method listed in compute=; stored only if store=True.

Context. A dictionary carried on the environment: language, time zone, defaults, and feature flags like tracking_disable.

Cursor (cr). The database connection wrapper for the current transaction.

Domain. A list of conditions in prefix notation used to filter records.

Environment (env). The bundle of cursor, user, context and registry through which all ORM calls go.

External ID (xml id). A stable name module.name stored in ir.model.data that points to a record.

Filestore. The directory holding attachment files; a database dump does not include it.

Group. A set of users with access rights, defined in res.groups.

Inheritance, classical. _inherit = 'model' without _name: extend a model in place.

Inheritance, delegation. _inherits with a Many2one: a model exposes the fields of another through a link.

Inheritance, prototype. _inherit with a new _name: copy a model into a new one.

Manifest. The __manifest__.py file declaring name, version, dependencies and data files.

Migration script. A pre-, post- or end- Python file in a module's migrations/<version> folder, run on update.

Model. A Python class mapped to a table and registered by _name; abstract models have no table, transient ones are temporary.

noupdate. A flag on data that stops the file from overwriting user changes on later updates.

ORM. The layer mapping models and fields to PostgreSQL tables.

OWL. Odoo's JavaScript component framework used in the web client since 16.0.

Record rule. A domain-based row-level access restriction on a model.

Recordset. An ordered set of records of one model; the unit of all ORM operations.

Registry. The loaded set of models for one database.

Sequence. An ir.sequence record generating numbered references.

sudo(). Returns a recordset that bypasses access rights and record rules.

Transient model. A model for wizards, with rows purged periodically.

View. An ir.ui.view record with an XML arch describing a form, list, search, kanban or other layout. The list view tag was tree until 16.0.

Wizard. A form on a transient model that collects input and then performs an action.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Using "module" for a Python package and "addon" for a deliverable in the same project; pick one in your own docs.
  • Confusing the xml id (module.name) with the database id, which differs between databases.

docs.title: Manifest reference
docs.text: __manifest__.py is a single Python dict literal. Odoo reads it with ast.literal_eval, not by importing the file, so it cannot contain expressions, function calls, or variables. Keys and defaults below come from odoo/modules/module.py in Odoo 18, where the defaults dict _DEFAULT_MANIFEST is defined.

docs.title: Minimal manifest
docs.text:
{
    'name': 'Library',
    'version': '18.0.1.0.0',
    'summary': 'Books and loans',
    'category': 'Services',
    'license': 'LGPL-3',
    'depends': ['base', 'mail'],
    'data': [
        'security/ir.model.access.csv',
        'views/library_book_views.xml',
    ],
    'application': True,
    'installable': True,
}

docs.title: Keys and defaults
docs.text:
Key Default Meaning name required display name version '1.0' module version. Odoo prefixes it with the series if it has fewer than 5 parts, so 1.0 becomes 18.0.1.0; prefer the full 18.0.x.y.z summary '' one-line description for the Apps list description '' long description (reStructuredText); README.rst is preferred in new modules author 'Odoo S.A.' set your own website '' URL shown in the Apps list category 'Uncategorized' Apps grouping license not defaulted in the list; Odoo warns when absent and assumes LGPL-3 declare LGPL-3 or another depends [] modules that must be loaded first; controls load order and which XML IDs you may reference data [] XML/CSV files loaded on install and update, in order demo [] files loaded only on databases created with demo data assets {} asset bundles: {'web.assets_backend': ['library/static/src/**/*']} external_dependencies {} {'python': ['requests'], 'bin': ['wkhtmltopdf']}; install fails if missing application False shows the module as an app in the Apps menu installable True False hides the module from installation auto_install False True or a list of modules: installs automatically when all its dependencies are installed (the "glue module" pattern) bootstrap False for web-type modules loaded before the database web False set by the web module family sequence 100 ordering in the Apps list pre_init_hook '' name of a function in the module run before install post_init_hook '' function run after install uninstall_hook '' function run on uninstall post_load '' function called when the module's Python is loaded, before the registry is built (monkey-patching hook) countries [] restricts auto-install suggestions to given country codes (localisations) cloc_exclude [] globs excluded from the line-count tool images [] website app store screenshots configurator_snippets, new_page_templates, images_preview_theme, live_test_url unset website theme keys init_xml, update_xml, demo_xml, test [] legacy keys, still in the defaults dict; do not use

Fields such as icon and addons_path are computed (the icon from static/description/icon.png), not set in the manifest.

docs.title: Load order
docs.text:
Odoo loads modules by dependency graph. Within a module, data files load in listed order, so security files come first, then data, then views, then menus that refer to actions. An XML ID referenced before the file that defines it is loaded fails with External ID not found.

'data': [
    'security/library_security.xml',
    'security/ir.model.access.csv',
    'data/sequences.xml',
    'views/library_book_views.xml',
    'views/library_menus.xml',
],

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
# hooks.py
def post_init_hook(env):
    env['ir.config_parameter'].set_param('library.loan_days', '14')

'post_init_hook': 'post_init_hook',

In Odoo 18 hooks receive env. In 16 they received (cr, registry).

docs.title: Assets
docs.text:
'assets': {
    'web.assets_backend': [
        'library/static/src/js/**/*',
        'library/static/src/xml/**/*.xml',
        'library/static/src/scss/library.scss',
    ],
    'web.assets_frontend': ['library/static/src/frontend/**/*'],
},

Globs are allowed. Files in a bundle but not matched by any rule are not served; adding a JS file does not require a manifest change if a glob covers it.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Non-literal values. 'version': VERSION or 'data': get_files() fails to parse. Write literals.
  • Forgetting depends. The module installs in a database that already has the other module, then fails in a clean one. Test installs on an empty database.
  • File listed but missing. The update aborts with a file-not-found. Check paths in data after renaming views.
  • Data in demo that production needs. Demo files are not loaded when demo data is disabled.
  • auto_install on a module with a heavy dependency set. It silently adds the module to databases that happen to have all dependencies.
  • Version bumps. Odoo does not use version for migrations as such; migration scripts in migrations/<version>/ run when the stored version is lower than the manifest version. Forgetting to bump the version means pre/post migration scripts do not run.

Versions. Hooks changed signature between 16 (cr, registry) and 17 onward (env). The attrs/states removal and <list> rename affect view files, not the manifest. Odoo 20 is not covered here.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Read a module's manifest as Odoo does, from a shell, without touching data:

from odoo.modules.module import get_manifest
m = get_manifest('sale')
print(m['version'], m['depends'], m['application'])

docs.title: Model catalogue
docs.text: The models below come up in almost every customisation. Names and fields were read from the Odoo 18 source (_name and the field declarations in each module's models folder). The list is a starting point, not a schema dump: for a full list use env[model]._fields in a shell.

docs.title: Core (base)
docs.text: Model Purpose Notes res.partner contacts, companies, addresses fields include name, is_company, vat, email, lang, type, parent_id, child_ids, category_id, commercial_partner_id res.users users each user delegates to a res.partner through partner_id res.groups security groups referenced as module.group_xml_id res.company companies multi-company filters use company_id res.currency, res.currency.rate currencies and rates ir.model, ir.model.fields model and field registry ir.ui.view views inherit_id, arch, mode, priority ir.actions.act_window window actions ir.actions.act_window.view per-action view binding ir.actions.server server actions ir.actions.client, ir.actions.act_url client and URL actions ir.cron scheduled actions ir.cron.trigger, ir.cron.progress one-off triggers and batch progress ir.rule record rules ir.attachment files res_model, res_id, res_name ir.sequence, ir.sequence.date_range numbering ir.config_parameter system parameters

docs.title: Sales
docs.text:
Model Key fields (as declared in source) sale.order name, company_id, partner_id, state, date_order, origin, user_id, order_line, amount_total, invoice_ids sale.order.line order lines; related to sale.order through order_id

sale.order.state is the usual place where custom flows attach: drafts are quotations, confirmed orders are the same record in a later state.

docs.title: Accounting
docs.text:
Model Key fields account.move name, state, move_type, company_id, partner_id, line_ids, invoice_line_ids, amount_total, payment_state, user_id account.move.line journal items and invoice lines

Invoices, bills, credit notes and journal entries are all account.move, told apart by move_type. invoice_line_ids is a subset of line_ids; the source says so in a comment. Write product lines to invoice_line_ids, and let Odoo build the balancing lines.

docs.title: Inventory and products
docs.text:
Model Key fields stock.picking name, origin, move_type, state, move_ids, picking_type_id, partner_id, company_id, user_id stock.picking.type operation types stock.move stock movements stock.quant on-hand quantities per location stock.quant.package packages product.template product master: uom_id, weight_uom_name, volume_uom_name, and so on product.product product variants

product.template is what users see as "Product"; product.product is the variant that sales lines and stock moves reference. Mixing them up is a common source of wrong joins.

docs.title: Purchasing
docs.text: purchase.order and purchase.order.line mirror the sales pair. View IDs for both are in the view ID catalogue.

docs.title: Mail
docs.text: Model Purpose mail.thread abstract mixin for chatter, tracking, message_post mail.activity.mixin abstract mixin adding activities mail.message messages and notes mail.mail outgoing emails queue mail.followers followers mail.activity scheduled activities; _rec_name is summary

docs.title: Reading a model definition
docs.text:
Model = env['sale.order']
print(Model._name, Model._description, Model._order)
print(Model._inherit)
f = Model._fields['state']
print(f.type, f.selection, f.store, f.tracking)

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Treating res.users as a contact. A user has a partner; customer data belongs on the partner. Writing to the user's name writes through to the partner.
  • Writing to line_ids on invoices. It is easy to unbalance an entry. Use invoice_line_ids for business lines.
  • Searching product.product when you meant the template. A product with variants appears once as a template and many times as variants.
  • Using ir.config_parameter for secrets or large payloads. It is world-readable by admins and loaded on many code paths.

Versions. The models listed exist in 16, 17 and 18, but fields move: Odoo 17 and 18 reworked UoM, tax and stock reservation fields. Confirm any field on your target version with env[model]._fields before relying on it. Odoo 20 is not covered.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Find which module defines a model and its fields, read-only:

rec = env['ir.model'].search([('model', '=', 'sale.order')])
print(rec.modules)
print(env['ir.model.fields'].search([('model', '=', 'sale.order'), ('name', 'like', 'amount')]).mapped('name'))

docs.title: View ID catalogue
docs.text:
External IDs of standard views that custom modules inherit most often. All names below were extracted from Odoo 18 source (the ir.ui.view records in each module's views folder). The ID in inherit_id is module.record_id. Note that some IDs still say tree even though the arch root is <list> in 18; Odoo did not rename the records.

Versions. IDs are stable across 16, 17 and 18 for the views listed here, but arch content is not: <tree> became <list>, and attrs/states became direct invisible/readonly expressions in 17. Re-check anchors for the version you target. Odoo 20 is not covered.

To find any ID from a running instance: Settings > Technical > Views with developer mode, or env['ir.ui.view'].search([('model','=','res.partner')]) in a shell.

docs.text:
<field name="inherit_id" ref="sale.view_order_form"/>

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Guessing IDs from the menu label. base.view_partner_tree is the partner list; there is no view_partner_list. Look the ID up instead of inferring it.
  • Inheriting the wrong variant. Sales orders and quotations share a form but have separate lists. Check which one the action uses.
  • IDs added by other modules. A view like mail.res_partner_view_form_inherit_mail is a child of base.view_partner_form. Extending it instead of the base view adds a dependency on mail that may be unwanted.
  • Different edition layout. Enterprise modules add children to many of these views. Your anchor still resolves, but the neighbouring nodes may differ.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
List the children of a view in your instance, read-only:

v = env.ref('sale.view_order_form')
for c in v.inherit_children_ids.sorted('priority'):
    print(c.priority, c.xml_id, c.name)
